title: Crownfall
blurb: Crownfall is a dark epic fantasy standalone by Michael Vadney, set in the island city of Burunt under the rule of the Prikaz Empire.

quote.text: Anyone we meet is either an opportunity, an ally, or a tool.

Burunt, a territory of the Prikaz Empire

lead:
Crownfall is a dark epic fantasy standalone novel by Michael Vadney, first published in April 2026. It is set in Burunt, an island city built on a mountainside, which at the start of the story has been a territory of the Prikaz Empire for nearly a decade under Viceroy Gian Magnus. The novel runs to 55 chapters and alternates among three viewpoint characters: Kyndel Heim, a young Draumer thief; Major Jelert Egarro, a signaric engineer in imperial service; and Lady Amara Khar, the heir of an impoverished noble house.

At the outset Kyndel is nineteen, lives in the fire-damaged slum of the Warrens, and intends to kill the Viceroy 1. Jelert comes to Burunt from the Empire convinced that signarium, the Empire's rune-based technology, should be used to improve people's lives, and he refuses to design weapons 2. Amara relies on negotiation and intrigue to keep House Khar solvent 3.

sections.html:
The first edition of Crownfall is dated April 2026. Katerina Belikova provided the cover art, Adrian M Gibson designed the cover and interior, and Jennifer Trippett edited the text. The book is dedicated to Jennifer, and its copyright page states that it was written without the assistance of generative AI.

The back-cover copy presents each of the three leads in turn: Kyndel Heim as someone who knows the truth about how the Viceroy came to power, Major Jelert Egarro as an engineer who came to Burunt intending to build something better, and Lady Amara Khar as the heir who must restore her family's legacy.

Every chapter carries the name of its viewpoint character as a heading, and the narration rotates among the three leads with no fixed pattern. Amara has the largest share, with twenty chapters (3, 6, 7, 11, 13, 17, 21, 23, 27, 29, 34, 36, 38, 39, 42, 44, 46, 48, 51 and 54). Kyndel has eighteen (1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 14, 16, 19, 24, 26, 30, 32, 33, 41, 43, 47, 49 and 52), and Jelert has sixteen (2, 8, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 31, 35, 37, 40, 45, 50 and 53).

The first three chapters introduce the leads one at a time, beginning with Kyndel, followed by Jelert and then Amara. Consecutive chapters from a single viewpoint are rare and never exceed two, as with Kyndel in Chapters 4 and 5 and Amara in Chapters 6 and 7. In several places a single event is narrated from two perspectives, with the viewpoint changing between chapters in the middle of a scene. In the manuscript the heading of Chapter 23 misspells Amara's name as Anara.

Chapter 55, the epilogue, is the only chapter with more than one viewpoint. It consists of three sections, narrated successively by Jelert, Kyndel and Amara.

The novel has no named parts. For convenience, the summaries below divide its chapters into stages of the story. Each summary covers the complete plot of the chapters concerned and is hidden as a spoiler.

The story opens in Burunt shortly before the social season. Kyndel Heim, who sold stolen goods through the fence Lefty in the Warrens, was saving to buy forged papers that would admit him to the nobility's parties and bring him close enough to kill Viceroy Gian Magnus. On a visit to Mintika Point he intervened when a young imperial soldier was beating an old woman, and left the soldier to bleed to death 1. Major Jelert Egarro, sailing to Burunt on a troop ship, declined to repair the signaric spear of Private Mirek. When Alshien rebels raided the ship for its cargo, Mirek was among the dead, and Lieutenant Dusan of the Iron Spears repelled the attackers 2. Amara Khar, meanwhile, outmaneuvered the merchant Naveed in the market and planned economies for her nearly bankrupt house 3.

The three storylines soon began to intersect. While burgling a poorly guarded manor, Kyndel stole a Founder's ring engraved with the name Khar'andor; Redarms then pursued him into the path of a group of smugglers led by Khamron 4. The Warrens Baron Heraldur recognized Kyndel as the son of Enir, murdered Luca in his presence, and pressed him into service as a thief and a spy among the nobility 5. Amara discovered that her late father's ring had been stolen and that her debts had been transferred to Brothers Incorporated, while also coping with the declining memory of her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar 6. When one of her smuggling ships was threatened with inspection, Jelert and Dusan, unaware of what it carried, lent soldiers to unload the contraband, and Amara invited Jelert to dinner 7. At Signarium Hall Jelert proposed a rail system to Gian, was rebuffed by Master Lazaro, and accepted an offer of friendship from Blazej Rodion 8. Kyndel attended the Stilton party disguised as Khorshed Kazemi, where a public argument with Amara contributed to the failure of his attempt to steal a hexagonal rune plate 9.

Kyndel returned at night and stole the plate, broke it during his escape, and handed Heraldur a forged replica in its place 10. Amara agreed to supply the Alshien through their agent Otisen at a 19 percent surcharge 11. Jelert told Dusan about the Yeshall rebellion, during which his runeforge capacitor had been converted into an explosive that killed thousands 1213. In the same period a dinner with Amara marked the beginning of a closer relationship between them 13.

This stretch of the novel centers on Kyndel's development as a Draumer. Driven by anger, he forged his first lasting creation, a dagger; soon afterward a Redarm, after hesitating to ask who he was, took Liena's obsidian flower from him. Heraldur rescued him and revealed that he was himself a Draumer, with an affinity for jade, and that he stole artifacts for the runes on them. Kyndel traded the location of the Draumer camps in exchange for training 14. Heraldur taught him to forge by channeling anger and admitted that he had built the Obelisk, the machine that had drained Kyndel during his imprisonment in the camps 16. Jelert, for his part, showed Blazej a new rune of his own design, aetheric magnetic flux 15. The Alshien leader Clodagh demanded that Amara help free Otisen from a gate checkpoint. Amara obtained Clodagh's signed confession as a safeguard and began to question the official account of the Draumer 17.

Jelert and Blazej succeeded in levitating a test puck on the flux rail 18. Kyndel quarreled with Heraldur, who declared that the upcoming palace gala would be his final theft, and later fought a Redarm on the rooftops 19. Swayed by Blazej's warnings, Jelert told Dusan that his work took precedence over their friendship 20.

At the Viceroy's gala Amara secured several new contracts, including one with Lord Yasser Turan, before Isadore Meyers informed her that the newly federalized bank was calling in House Khar's debts 21. Jelert's attempt at reconciliation with Dusan failed 22, and Amara rebuffed Blazej after he insulted her and tried to draw Jelert away from her 23. In his Khorshed persona, Kyndel met Turan, an old friend of his father, and found Amara unexpectedly gracious. From the balcony Gian gave the assembled guests his version of the Requing raid in which his brother had died ten years earlier 24. He then unveiled the railcaster, a weapon carried by Redarms. Jelert recognized his own aetheric magnetic flux runes in its design and watched as Gian credited Blazej with founding Burition signarium 25.

The gala ended in violence. Kyndel, sent to steal a rune-etched torc from Lazaro's office, took it and then attacked Gian when the Viceroy entered the room; Gian pulled Lazaro into the path of the blade. Two Redarms cornered Kyndel. The larger of them, Latif, proved to be a Draumer and cut off Kyndel's left arm. The smaller Redarm killed Latif and took off her helmet, revealing herself as Liena, who had become an overdrawn Redarm. She carried the dying Kyndel out of the engineering wing 26.

On the carriage ride home from the gala, Otisen told Amara about his past. He had been a guard at the Heim Estate when Gian stormed it, had shot Gian with a crossbow and fled with the young Kyndel, and had later lost the boy when his own cousin sold him for the Viceroy's bounty. Amara asked to join the Alshien in earnest, and privately concluded that Khorshed was Kyndel 27.

Liena brought Kyndel to Jelert's rooms. She explained that every Redarm was an overdrawn Draumer kept under control by a lethal rune collar, that the Empress was aware of this, and that Kyndel would die unless he adapted to overdraw. Jelert hid Kyndel and repaired the cracked torc 28. Gian then summoned Amara and accused her of conspiring with Khorshed. Believing Khorshed dead, she disclosed that he was Kyndel Heim. Gian kept her father's ring and hired her ships to carry cyrusite in secret 29.

Kyndel survived the fever that accompanied his overdraw 30. Jelert learned that Blazej had been responsible for killing the rail project, struck him, and bluffed his way into Gian's office to bid for the post of head engineer. Given Lazaro's unfinished torc to complete, he secretly built a feedback loop into it 31. Kyndel woke with a forged iron arm and a new ability to reshape his creations, escaped from the palace, and returned to Heraldur 32. On a rooftop Heraldur showed him the Eldtree, which he described as the tether of the whole world, and revealed that he was Heydar Magnus, Gian's brother. He had helped build the Obelisk before Gian imprisoned and tortured him. He agreed to allow the collared Redarms a single opportunity to be spared 33.

House Khar now served as a base for Clodagh's Alshien. After lashing out at her mother, Amara proposed reviving the House Khar charity gala as a trap in which to kill Gian 34. Gian, in turn, implied to Jelert that he had arranged Blazej's death, showed him raw cyrusite from a source outside the Empire, and bombed Signarium Hall to silence dissenting engineers, attributing the attack to the Alshien 35. On an evening when her mind was clear, Dhonya offered Amara counsel 36.

At Lord Modir's gala Jelert confessed everything to Amara 37, and the next day Clodagh reluctantly accepted him 38. Amara noticed an unfamiliar machine covered in spines among Gian's cargo, and smuggled Jelert into the caverns beneath the palace hidden in a crate. Before they separated, the two declared their feelings for one another 39. Jelert overloaded the engine that drove the railcaster assembly line, and as it exploded he ran directly into Gian 40.

Some weeks later Kyndel was training with a working iron arm, and Heraldur planned a raid through the sewers on the Draumer camp, timed for the night of the Khar gala 41. On that night Amara awaited Gian with crossbowmen concealed in the hall outside her office 42.

Kyndel led Heraldur's crew into the prison beneath Mintika Point. They freed about two dozen prisoners but found that the Obelisk had been taken away. Two Redarms told them that Liena had been punished for breaking ranks to save Kyndel 43.

Gian arrived at the Khar gala accompanied by Redarms and with Jelert as his prisoner. He revealed a number of towering metal Warriors and declared himself the first king of Burunt, while Isadore Meyers read out charges of treason against House Khar. A Warrior killed Clodagh, and Dhonya was struck down 44. In Gian's carriage Jelert discovered that the Alshien commander Farzin was Gian's agent and that Lazaro's torc, which Jelert himself had completed, was the power source for the Warriors. An explosion overturned the carriage and killed Isadore. Using Gian's lenses, Jelert found that every Warrior contained a mutilated Draumer, and that the damaged Warriors went berserk when they forged 45.

Otisen saved Amara from execution. Dhonya died after telling her daughter to live for those still living, and Amara assumed command of the survivors 46. Kyndel discovered that Liena had been made into a Warrior, and broke her torc so that she could die as herself. He afterward found Heraldur dead in the street 47. He then joined the resistance Amara had assembled from Buritions and Prikizans together; the group learned to target the Warriors' torcs and withdrew to the Warrens 48.

Kyndel proposed stopping the Warriors with the Obelisk, the device that converts Draumer power into cyrusite. Amara admitted that she had unwittingly smuggled it into the palace, and Jelert offered to rebuild Heraldur's protective vambrace so that Kyndel could supply the device with power. Otisen pledged his service to Kyndel, Jelert confessed that his sabotage had caused the Warriors' madness, and Amara rallied the city 49.

Kyndel, Jelert, Dusan and Otisen made their way to the ruined factory beneath the palace, where Gian was failing to operate the Obelisk. Kyndel informed him that his brother had died that night, and with Warriors closing in the two parties agreed to a truce 50. Amara led more than a thousand people to the Warrens, won over nine surviving Redarms, and secured entry by invoking Kyndel's name 51. Kyndel powered the Obelisk by means of the vambrace 52. Once it was running, Gian struck Jelert and killed a Redarm who had turned against him, and Jelert shot Gian dead. A pulse from the Obelisk disabled every Warrior, after which the device burst into a massive formation of cyrusite that destroyed the palace 53. At the Warrens wall, the defenders saw the Warriors fall, freed a collared Redarm, and witnessed sunrise through the crystal 54.

The epilogue takes place three months after the climax. Jelert was serving as Master Engineer of an independent Burunt and planning a rail line between the islands, while living with guilt over having killed Gian. Kyndel, deprived of his revenge, spent his time in the Warrens with Otisen. Amara, whom the surviving nobility had crowned the first Queen of Burunt, visited the memorial to "The Remembered of Crownfall" and came forward to give a speech 55.

Trust. The book's tagline, Trust is the hardest Lesson, identifies trust as its central concern. All three leads begin the story isolated. Kyndel has taught himself to depend on no one 1; Jelert is an outsider, mocked by the ship's men with the nickname Major Meddle 2; and Amara regards everyone she meets as an opportunity, an ally or a tool 3. The resolution of Kyndel's arc depends on his decision to share his plan with others even at the risk of being used, a decision he makes with Heraldur's solitary death in mind 49.

Inventions turned to harm. Jelert holds that signarium should improve lives and will not build weapons 2. The novel repeatedly contrasts these principles with the uses to which others put his work, from the runeforge capacitor at Yeshall to the railcasters derived from his rail runes 1325.

Survival and manipulation. Amara keeps her house afloat by means of contracts, bribes and smuggling 3. She justifies manipulation to herself as necessary for survival, though she feels guilty about the way she uses Jelert 23.

Legacy. Amara's aim is the restoration of House Khar 3. On her deathbed, her mother dismisses concern for legacy and urges her to live for the people who are still alive 46.

Official history. Imperial posters warn the population of Burunt against the Draumer 1. Over the course of the book the official account of Gian's rise is gradually shown to be a fabrication concealing murder and betrayal 273344.

Revenge. Kyndel has committed himself to inflicting as much harm on the Empire as he can, through many small blows 1. In the epilogue, after Gian has died at someone else's hands, Kyndel finds himself without purpose, and Otisen tells him that living in a world without Gian is the greater revenge 55.

• Kyndel Heim: a nineteen-year-old Draumer thief from the Warrens who wants to kill the Viceroy 1.
  • Jelert Egarro: a young imperial signaric engineer and major, newly posted to Burunt, who refuses to make weapons 2.
  • Amara Khar: heir of the impoverished House Khar, a shrewd trader determined to save her family 3.
  • Gian Magnus: Viceroy of Burunt, who rose to power a decade ago during the struggle that burned the Warrens 1.
  • Heraldur: a feared one-eyed gang lord and Warrens Baron 5
  • Liena: a girl from Kyndel's past, linked to the obsidian flower he carries 4
  • Dusan: a lieutenant of the Iron Spears and Jelert's friend 2.
  • Balfourd: the loyal, elderly majordomo of House Khar 3.
  • Dhonya Khar: Amara's mother and former matriarch of House Khar, whose memory is failing 6
  • Blazej Rodion: an engineer at Signarium Hall who offers Jelert an alliance 8
  • Otisen: a hard-bitten Alshien agent 11
  • Clodagh: an older Alshien woman 17
  • Lazaro: head engineer of Signarium Hall 8

See also the chapter guide, the timeline and minor characters.

title: Chapter guide
blurb: A chapter-by-chapter summary of Crownfall, with each summary hidden behind a spoiler gate for its chapter.

quote.text: There’s no help in this city.

lead:
This guide summarizes each of the 55 chapters of Crownfall. Every chapter is headed with its point-of-view character: Kyndel Heim, Jelert Egarro or Amara Khar. The final chapter is shared among all three.

Each summary is hidden until revealed and covers only events up to the end of its own chapter. The manuscript heads Chapter 23 with the name Anara; it is an Amara chapter and is listed here under her name. For an overview of the whole story, see the book article; for in-world dates, see the timeline.

sections.html: Kyndel Heim went into the Warrens, the district of Burunt burned during the Viceroy's rise a decade earlier, to sell stolen goods to the fence Lefty. Lefty attacked him with shears, as was his habit, and Kyndel avoided the blow by drawing on his tether. Kyndel wanted forged papers that would admit him to noble parties in the coming social season. Lefty refused, saying such papers required far more goods and a believable lineage, paid him a few imperial silvers, and mentioned that Heraldur's crew had absorbed the rival fences. Kyndel decided to steal from the nobility directly and went to scout Mintika Point. While cutting down an old anti-Draumer poster, he saw a young imperial soldier beating a homeless woman and attacked him. His mist-forged dagger broke apart in a burst of light, so he wounded the soldier in the thigh with an ordinary blade. The soldier, about Kyndel's age, asked for help; Kyndel refused and left him to bleed to death, then escaped a patrol with Draumer speed. The chapter establishes his goal of killing Viceroy Gian.

Major Jelert Egarro was traveling to Burunt aboard a signaric troop ship without sails, whose crew held a party for him after he repaired its stove. Lieutenant Dusan of the Iron Spears told him the event was really meant to reduce friction between soldiers and sailors, and that the men had nicknamed him Major Meddle. Private Mirek asked him to fix a damaged signaric spear. Jelert declined, later explaining to Dusan that he did not make weapons because signarium should improve lives. A small boat without lights then attacked with flaming arrows. Dusan pushed Jelert into cover and organized the defense with brightshields and spears, while Jelert observed that the raiders were disciplined and were taking particular crates. The attackers were repelled and one was captured, at the cost of two sailors, Mirek and two more of Dusan's soldiers. Dusan identified them as Alshien rebels, the group his unit had been sent to help the Viceroy destroy. Jelert was physically sick and dwelt on Mirek's death, as the private had died holding the spear Jelert had refused to repair.

In a Burunt market, Amara Khar, heir of the impoverished House Khar, signed a contract for goods that the merchant Master Naveed had reserved only by verbal agreement, which carries no legal weight in Burunt. Naveed had been held up by the harbor master over a clerical error, and the text strongly implies that Amara arranged the delay. When he accused and insulted her, she left with her majordomo, Balfourd. She walked home to save money, noting the difference between the stiff Prikizans and the graceful native Buritions. Balfourd listed the household's problems: an overgrown bougainvillea, a leaking fountain, a delayed cargo and a cook who had quit. Amara recalled her father's death from illness and her mother's later decline into a harsher affliction. She told Balfourd to pre-sell the delayed Requing liquors, defer the repairs and hire an inexpensive young cook from the Warrens. The chapter ends on her governing rule, which sorts every person she meets into one of three categories: opportunity, ally or tool.

Kyndel entered a lightly guarded noble manor through its garden kitchen door after several of his forged iron lockpicks broke apart into light. The house had already been stripped of valuables. He took food, passed a sleeping figure and searched a sparse study, where a locked drawer held a Founder's ring engraved with the name Khar'andor. A pulse from the ring identified it as a Draumer creation. It was too recognizable to sell, but he took it along with two books. Two Redarms, the Viceroy's Draumer hunters, chased him toward the Warrens with bolos and glowing boots that carried them over carts, and one crushed his forged dagger. Kyndel scattered forged caltrops and pushed himself close to overdraw. Near the Warrens he ran into Khamron, a bruiser whose gang was unloading smuggled signaric devices. The larger Redarm attacked the gang, and a thrown device set off a series of explosions. The chapter notes that Kyndel carried an obsidian flower, his last connection to someone named Liena. Stunned, he was seized by Khamron, who intended to bring him before his boss.

Khamron brought Kyndel, hooded and tied, to a cellar in the Warrens, where he was beaten after breaking a thug's nose. The gang lord Heraldur, a one-eyed man with a jade cane, recognized him as the son of Enir, a guild master and well-known Draumer. Luca, son of Baron Taher, burst in to demand his overdue goods and told Heraldur to step down. Heraldur feigned agreement, killed Luca with a blow of the cane, and sent Khamron with three dozen men and rune charges to kill Taher and burn Luca's inn. Kyndel denied being a Draumer and claimed that a house guard had saved him during Gian's purges. The gang found the Khar ring and Liena's obsidian flower on him, and Heraldur revealed that Lefty worked for him. Kyndel admitted that he intended to kill Gian, whom he remembered murdering his parents during a fire, and Heraldur ridiculed the plan. Heraldur released him on condition that he repay the gang's losses as a thief and spy among the nobility, and returned the flower and the ring, which he said Kyndel would need.

Amara discovered that her late father's Founder's ring was missing from the drawer she kept locked so that her mother could not take it. Balfourd reported that the thief had come in through the kitchen door overnight and taken food and two books. The household guards had been dismissed a week earlier because the House could not pay them. A letter from Goldguard bank informed Amara that her accounts and loans had been transferred to Brothers Incorporated, a local bank that trades in debt, and named Isadore Meyers as her contact. Her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar, came in disoriented, asking about preparations for the family gala, speaking of her husband as if he were alive and referring to the Council of Lords as though the Empire did not govern Burunt. The maid Sireen led her away. Amara reflected that House Khar had lost its trade routes when the Empire banned commerce with the Requing Federation, and that she had since turned to smuggling to keep the House alive. She told Balfourd to investigate the new bank and repeated her vow to manage everything herself.

Amara's ship, the Alisma, arrived but was scheduled for an inspection at dawn that would expose the contraband hidden in its false-bottomed crates. Warned by a bribed contact, she went to the harbor dockhouse in her best sapphire kaftan to confront Dockmaster Riocard. He told her the docks were closed because an imperial ship carrying a senior officer and a prisoner had priority. Since the Alisma was berthed beside it, not even her own crew could unload. She considered and rejected staging a robbery, dumping the cargo or scuttling the ship. Major Jelert Egarro and his lieutenant, Dusan, then arrived. After a private exchange in Prikizan, Jelert offered a dozen soldiers to unload the Alisma before sunset, and Amara accepted. Dusan gave Riocard a list of the supplies stolen by the raiders and mentioned a meeting at the palace. Recognizing a possible route into the palace, Amara suggested that Jelert thank her with a dinner, and he promised to call on her. Imperial soldiers then unloaded her contraband without knowing what it was.

About a week later, Jelert was working at Signarium Hall, the palace laboratory, and was distracted by thoughts of Amara. Head engineer Master Lazaro reprimanded him, as no one had told him it was inspection day. Viceroy Gian Magnus arrived dressed in high Prikizan fashion. Lazaro tried to steer him past Jelert's station, but Jelert spoke up and proposed a magno-signaric rail system, powered by refined cyrusite, that would link Burunt across the archipelago to the mainland. Gian said he knew Jelert's name and had heard about his past work in the Empire. The remark disturbed Jelert, who had tried to leave that history behind. Gian and Lazaro rejected the rail line as too expensive for Burunt's limited cyrusite allocation, though Gian said he would follow Jelert's progress and would return the following month. Afterward Blazej Rodion, a fellow academy graduate, introduced himself. He cautioned that the laboratory was ruthless and that sabotage was suspected, and proposed an alliance, which Jelert accepted.

Several weeks into his service, Kyndel rode with Heraldur to a party at the Stilton estate and remembered his last carriage ride as a child with his parents. His assignment was to steal a hexagonal metal plate marked with Prikizan runes, whose purpose Heraldur would not explain. He posed as Khorshed of House Kazemi, nephew and expected heir of a childless lord, and wore the Khar Founder's ring, which had become stuck on his finger. After finding the plate in a room of signaric artifacts, he set fire to the drapes of a library as a diversion. Hurrying back, he collided with Amara Khar and tore her dress. The two traded harsh insults, and his taunt about her father's money visibly hurt her. On noticing the ring, she accepted his claim to House Kazemi, apologized for slighting another Founding House, and mentioned that her own House's ring had recently been stolen. Kyndel then realized who she was. The quarrel drew a crowd and spoiled his diversion, so he left, determined to take the plate by his own methods.

Kyndel returned to the Stilton house after midnight in ragged clothes and broke several forged lockpicks before he got the front door open. In the dark display room he used Draumer strength to lift the glass case from the hexagonal plate. Guards discovered him. He threw the case, seized the plate and fought with twin forged daggers, while the guards, identifying him as a Draumer, tried to capture him alive for the bounty. Lord Stilton fired at him from the stairs with a rare Requing musket, and Kyndel escaped through the front doors and ran until dawn. In an alley he found that the plate had split in two. Assuming a broken artifact had no value, he pushed into overdraw to forge an iron copy with the same shape and runes, and threw the real pieces onto a refuse heap. At Heraldur's newest base, a former alehouse guarded by Khamron, he delivered the copy with a warning that it was fragile. Heraldur examined it doubtfully but praised the work and promised more jobs, and Khamron acknowledged Kyndel with a brief nod.

A few days after the incident at House Stilton, Amara woke at her desk with ink on her face. Balfourd showed in a visitor, Otisen, a weathered man with a military bearing, who wanted to buy the goods she had taken from Master Naveed: grain, salted fish, medical tinctures, canvas and boots. He said he acted for unnamed parties. From his mended clothing and manner, Amara inferred that he was Alshien and said so, and his reaction confirmed it. She falsely claimed that selling to him would breach a contract with a loyal customer, said she had regular shipments arranged for months ahead, and demanded a premium. After negotiation they agreed on recurring deliveries at fair market price with an additional 19 percent for hazard. Otisen left a deposit and an address. Amara regarded this as the first significant contract she had secured since taking charge of House Khar, and judged that dealing with the Alshien would either rescue the House or ruin it.

After twenty-one consecutive days of work, Jelert met Dusan at the Three Coins tavern. He complained that the engineers sabotaged one another with the Master Engineer's encouragement, and that his long hours with Blazej left him little time to write to Amara. Dusan said that the soldiers already stationed on Burunt were uncooperative, and that the Iron Spears had spent a month pursuing Farzin, the Alshien leader blamed for the attack on their ship, who seemed to anticipate every trap. Jelert asked whether Dusan had served at Yeshall. He had not, but a captain he knew had told him that commanders there used a new signaric explosive that killed rebels and civilians alike, women and children among them. The account revived Jelert's guilt, since the explosive was his own runeforge capacitor. Dusan moved the conversation to Jelert's planned dinner with Lady Amara and teased him about it. When they parted, Dusan warned him that the island was different from how it appeared.

Amara and Jelert dined at a Prikizan restaurant while she privately assessed his value as an ally to House Khar. He told her he had volunteered for the territories after years in the service of the Empress, described cyrusite as a gift of the Earth Mother Valenska, and disclosed that he was heir to the military Egarro line. When he described his levitating rail design, Amara proposed a partnership, then learned that the Viceroy had not approved it. She told him that her father had died of illness when she was nine and that her mother, Dhonya, had raised the House's standing before a slow loss of memory overtook her. Jelert described the ambush on his ship, and Amara explained that the Alshien had formed in the first year of Gian's rule, after Gian brought in Prikaz to stop a Requing invasion. Jelert admitted that his runeforge capacitor had been turned into a weapon to suppress the Yeshall rebellion, killing thousands, and that he had chosen Burunt partly because signaric weapons are illegal there. They agreed the evening had been a date, and Amara later found herself thinking of his gray eyes.

Kyndel had stolen three artifacts for Heraldur and attended two more parties as Khorshed without once seeing Gian. Angry, he threw forged daggers at an alley wall; they dissolved on impact until one, thrown in pure fury, stayed solid in the stone. A Redarm dropped from a roof and attacked him. During the fight Liena's obsidian flower fell, and the Redarm picked it up, stopped, and asked through its helmet's filter who he was. Heraldur struck it with his cane. He then showed a glowing honey-colored eye in the socket Kyndel had believed empty and forged a jade stiletto, revealing himself as a Draumer. The wounded Redarm fled with the flower. Heraldur led Kyndel through tunnels to a hidden signaric workshop, explained that the counterfeit plate's signature had given Kyndel away, and said he stole artifacts for their runes in order to build a device to use against Gian. Kyndel admitted that he had escaped the Draumer camps, where Liena had died. Heraldur wanted the camps' location, and Kyndel traded it for training and swore to keep Heraldur's nature secret.

In Signarium Hall, an engineer knocked over Jelert's tool tray while others looked on in amusement. More than a month after his arrival, Jelert was still ostracized and refused basic requisitions. Blazej helped him, repeated his advice to stay alert, and offered to speak to the other engineers on his behalf. Jelert complained that Master Lazaro played favorites. Blazej asked to see Jelert's project before the next presentation day, and Jelert showed him plans for causeways connecting the islands to the Empire by rail. Blazej, whose father is a railway engineer, dismissed the idea because of its cyrusite cost until Jelert explained that it relied on aetheric magnetic flux, a rune Jelert had discovered himself. Blazej was astonished, noting that the last person to discover a rune had been appointed to the Empress's personal advisory board. Jelert again avoided explaining why he had left the Empress's service. The two worked late, with Blazej suggesting a stabilizing matrix, until Jelert left to meet Dusan. Blazej declined to join him, saying that soldiers did not understand engineers.

Kyndel trained with Heraldur in an abandoned Warrens warehouse, where Heraldur's twin jade batons repeatedly broke his iron daggers. Heraldur explained that forged iron differs from natural iron: it carries its maker's individual signal, is about as durable as glass, and draws its strength from the maker's focus and will. Lacking time for the usual regimen of practice and meditation, he taught a shortcut, which was to forge with anger instead of suppressing it. When Kyndel asked why Gian was still alive, Heraldur said that the Obelisk had to be dealt with first, and admitted that he had built it as a young man in the hope of strengthening Burunt with Draumer power. After he refused Gian further help, Gian turned the device on him and scarred his face. Kyndel had spent years chained before the Obelisk and blamed it for Liena's death. Driven by memories of his parents and the camps, he attacked Heraldur, and this time his dagger held against the jade. Heraldur pinned him, drove the dagger into the stone floor, where it stayed intact, praised the weapon Kyndel's anger had produced and ordered him to repeat it.

Clodagh, an older Alshien woman, pushed past Balfourd into Amara's office. Otisen and twelve others had been stopped at the southeast gate, where soldiers were detaining everyone after a known smuggler was flagged, and Clodagh feared the weaker men would talk under questioning. Amara at first called the Alshien terrorists. Clodagh replied that many of them were parents of children who had woken with Draumer abilities, and admitted that Otisen was more important than he let on. Amara wrote a sealed letter vouching for the group as her dock workers and sent Balfourd on a horse that Clodagh paid for. Before he left, Amara required Clodagh to sign a confession naming herself leader of the Alshien, giving each woman the means to destroy the other. Clodagh hesitated, then signed, and Amara locked the document in the drawer from which her father's ring had been stolen. Clodagh drove her knife into the desk. In the argument that followed, Amara repeated the common claim that the Draumer had cheated Burunt, and Clodagh said it was false. Amara allowed that she might need to reconsider, returned the knife, and the two reached a cautious mutual respect.

Late at night in an empty Signarium Hall, Jelert and Blazej tested the aetheric magnetic flux prototype. It consisted of a model rail on which a metal puck stood in for a carriage, with interchangeable rune plates along the circuit. They sheltered behind a blast shield taken without a requisition, because an earlier test had launched the puck into the stone wall. After a quiet prayer to Valenska, Jelert pressed the activation rune, and the puck rose an inch above the rails and moved smoothly along them. He explained that alternating polarity pushed and pulled the load and that faster switching raised its speed. Blazej praised him and spoke admiringly of the force of the earlier ricochet. Jelert tensely ended that line of talk, citing the Empress's ban on signaric weapons in the territories, and Blazej apologized with ease. The presentation to the Viceroy was set for the next day. When Jelert realized he was late to meet Dusan, Blazej cautioned him about Dusan, arguing that outsiders resented the engineers' work. Jelert defended his friend but stayed to help, and they finished after midnight.

Kyndel remembered Liena giving him bread in a camp cell and forbidding him to give up. In a windowless room in the Warrens, Heraldur told him that his next theft, at the palace gala, would be his last. It would complete a signaric vambrace to shield them from the Obelisk, which they would then destroy. Kyndel insisted on going after Gian and accused Heraldur of cowardice. When he drew on his tether, Heraldur attacked with a jade club that reshaped itself into a sword, broke Kyndel's dagger and held the blade at his throat. Heraldur could somehow sense when Kyndel drew power, and as punishment he refused to teach him how to reshape constructs. Kyndel left in anger and failed to reshape his surviving dagger. From a rooftop he created flashes of collapsing mist to lure the Redarm that had taken the flower. A different Redarm, tall and thin with lightning-charged hands, answered instead. Applying Heraldur's lessons, Kyndel held his own, kicked it off the roof and escaped to the edge of the Warrens, elated and newly confident that he would reach Gian.

Jelert arrived nearly two hours late to meet Dusan at the Third Coin, having stayed to brainstorm with Blazej. He reported that the prototype had performed better than expected, that the Viceroy wanted more capacity and speed, and that Blazej was coordinating with the Viceroy's private engineers. The two exchanged news, and Dusan urged Jelert to attend the Viceroy's gala the following week and dance with Amara, whose letters had been notably formal. Jelert reluctantly agreed. Dusan admitted that this was the worst posting the Iron Spears had received: relations with the local soldiers were deteriorating, and constant shifts spent chasing reported Alshien sightings had produced nothing. Jelert brushed these concerns aside, which hurt his friend. When Dusan said he looked exhausted and should rest, Jelert recalled Blazej's warning and retorted that his work mattered more than Dusan did. Dusan answered with a stiff salute and addressed him only by rank and as sir. Jelert left convinced that Blazej had been right.

Amara attended the gala in the ballroom of Viceroy Gian's palace, which was lit by enormous signaric chandeliers and hung with tapestries alternating Gian's profile with Eld, the World Tree. She wore her mother's black velvet gown embroidered with gold branches, along with a gold circlet, and approached the evening as a battle. Her mother, Dhonya, came in white and silver, alert and happy, while Balfourd watched for any return of her confusion. Amara weighed whether working through the Alshien network would be sound strategy or recklessness. Within an hour she had arranged six meetings, obtained three verbal commitments and secured a preliminary written contract signed by Lord Yasser Turan. Isadore Meyers of the Brothers Incorporated Banking Institute then informed her that the Institute was calling in House Khar's debts. Under Burunt's newly federalized banking system, the Viceroy could recall debts in an emergency, and he had done so, citing Alshien attacks on shipping. House Khar had a month to pay ten percent and a further three-month grace period for the remainder. Other Houses were affected as well.

Jelert wore formal military dress for the first time in months, a muted teal coat with brass buttons and a sash denoting his rank of major and his role as an engineer. The other engineers at the gala avoided him. He saw Amara surrounded by guests but lost his nerve and ate pastries instead. He found Dusan among other soldiers, and Dusan greeted him coldly by rank and surname. In an alcove Jelert apologized and admitted that other engineers' warnings had influenced him. Dusan pointed out that Jelert had once called those same engineers saboteurs, learned that Blazej was the one turning Jelert against his friends, and suggested that Blazej was exploiting someone lonely and eager to belong. He added that Jelert had come to Burunt alone and had nowhere else to go if this failed, and that he had warned for months that something on the island was wrong. Hurt, Jelert said that if Dusan forced him to choose between friendship and work, he had already chosen, and walked away. Trusting no one, he decided to approach Amara.

Jelert greeted Amara, who felt guilty for letting Balfourd answer his letters with vague replies she had dictated. Weighed down by the bank's demand, she hesitated, then reminded herself that manipulation was how she survived and assured him that House Khar was in its strongest position in years. Jelert told her about his falling out with Dusan. She comforted him, unsettled by how readily he gave her power over him. Major Blazej Rodion interrupted, pressing Jelert to come with him for a surprise concerning their project, and insulted Amara as a frivolous indulgence. Jelert missed the insult. Amara rebuked Blazej, observing that he relied on Jelert's work for his own advancement. Jelert took her side, called her his friend and stayed, promising to be in the laboratory first thing the next day. Blazej's composure briefly faltered before he left. Amara warned Jelert to be wary of him, since such men seldom want what they appear to want. She then sent Jelert for drinks, telling herself she was only guiding him, and half believed it.

Heraldur had instructed Kyndel to listen to the Viceroy's announcement, steal a rune-etched torc from the Master Engineer's office and avoid any confrontation with Gian. As Khorshed, Kyndel traded barbs with nobles. Lord Yasser Turan, an old friend of Kyndel's father, approached him. Kyndel feared recognition, but Turan only offered his help to Khorshed Kazemi. Kyndel ran into Amara and expected another quarrel, but she was gracious, vouched for Turan's honesty and, noticing his surprise, asked what he was hiding. Jelert returned with drinks, and Amara introduced the two men and took them to the balcony. When Gian was announced, Kyndel relived the memory of Gian dragging his mother by her hair and holding a knife to her throat. Gian told the guests that a Requing raid ten years earlier had killed his brother, that he had rallied Prikizan soldiers to defeat it, and that he had then led the nation into the Empire. He called for the Alshien to be rooted out. Nine Redarms entered carrying new devices, and none of them detected Kyndel.

The Redarms carried long devices with glowing runic bases, grips and shoulder straps. Gian introduced the weapon as the railcaster, designed to drive off enemies at a distance in the event of a future Requing invasion. In a demonstration the Redarms fired at heavy wooden targets with an electric crack. The targets burst apart, and metal projectiles lodged in the doors behind them. A Burition servant was wounded by shrapnel while the applauding crowd paid no attention. Jelert recognized the runes as his own aetheric magnetic flux design and remembered the puck embedded in the laboratory wall. He saw in it a repetition of the runeforge capacitor and Yeshall, with his work turned into a weapon for the second time. He feared he would be branded a traitor for helping a territory build weapons of war against the Empress's prohibition. Gian then presented Blazej Rodion of the Petrovskaya Academy as the founder of Burition signarium, and Blazej climbed the dais in triumph. Jelert understood that he had been betrayed, and when Amara tried to console him, he pulled away.

Kyndel left the gathering, smashed a chair in an empty hall and cut his arm. A Burition maid bandaged him and directed him to Lazaro's office, where he picked the lock and took the torc. Lazaro arrived with Gian and two Redarms. Against orders, Kyndel forged a dagger from his rage and rushed Gian, who pushed Lazaro into its path, and Kyndel stabbed Lazaro between the ribs. Gian escaped. Kyndel cut the helmet strap of the larger Redarm and exposed a Burition man who forged a stone axe, revealing that the Redarms were Draumer. The smaller Redarm, the one who had taken Liena's flower, ordered him, by the name Latif, to take Kyndel alive. Latif outfought Kyndel, reshaped his axe head to disarm him and cut off his left arm, and Kyndel forged iron over the stump to stop the bleeding. As Latif moved to execute him, the smaller Redarm killed Latif with an obsidian blade and removed her helmet. She was Liena, older and with glowing honey-colored eyes. Kyndel wept against her, then pushed her away as an enemy and collapsed into overdraw. Liena carried him out, repeating her old command that he must not give up.

After the announcement, Amara found that every conversation had turned to the railcaster and the prospect of war. She concluded that the weapon and the federalization of the bank were parts of one scheme, that Gian had violated the Prikizan ban on signaric weapons in the territories, and that she could not pay her debts without Alshien help. Otisen, her bodyguard for the evening, rode home with her. Asked what troubled him, he said he had been a guard at the Heim Estate when Gian attacked it with foreign soldiers. He had seen Gian cut Mistress Heim's throat, had shot Gian in the shoulder with a crossbow, and, at the pleading of the bound Master Heim, had fled with their son, Kyndel. He hid the boy with his sister in the countryside until his own cousin sold Kyndel to Prikizan soldiers for the bounty. Otisen did nothing to stop it and left that night to join the rebellion. Moved, Amara told him she wanted to join the Alshien in earnest. Otisen mentioned a young man at the gala who resembled a grown Kyndel, and Amara named him as Khorshed Kazemi. Otisen dismissed the idea, but Amara was privately certain.

Jelert paced his palace rooms, blaming himself for the railcasters and fearing he could be hanged for treason. Opening his door to go and confront Gian, he found Khorshed, bloodied and barely conscious, supported by a Burition woman in Redarm armor. The young man's left arm was encased in a misshapen mass of iron. Jelert took them in and treated the wounds with field medicine learned years before, using an obsidian knife the woman forged. She gave her name as Liena and identified the patient as Kyndel, who had tried to kill Gian, and said she had killed a fellow Redarm to save him. She explained that Kyndel was becoming overdrawn and would either adapt or die. Every Redarm, she said, was an overdrawn Draumer enslaved by a rune-etched collar that would kill its wearer at Gian's will, if tampered with, or upon Gian's death, and the Empress knew of this. She believed the railcasters had been built in secret laboratories beneath the palace. She left an obsidian flower for Kyndel with a message urging him to leave Burunt. Jelert repaired the cracked torc and found it to be an energy converter for an unknown source. Kyndel woke briefly, then convulsed and lost consciousness.

Prikizan soldiers escorted Amara, by now a sworn member of the Alshien, to the palace at Gian's summons. Gian, wearing new orange-lensed spectacles, showed her a blood-encrusted iron dagger and her father's Founder's ring. Both had been taken from Khorshed Kazemi, who he said had tried to kill him and had murdered his head engineer, and the ring had been removed from the assassin's severed arm. Accused of conspiring with him, and believing him dead, Amara revealed her suspicion that Khorshed was really Kyndel Heim, a Draumer. Gian was visibly shaken before he regained his composure. Amara falsely claimed that her men had been investigating. Gian kept the ring until the matter was resolved and asked her to report any news of Kyndel. Realizing that Kyndel might still be alive, Amara regretted exposing him. Gian then hired her company to move shipments of cyrusite discreetly, out of sight of Prikizan soldiers and anyone who might report to the Empire. Suspecting a trap, Amara confessed her House's smuggling. Gian laughed, handed her a signed sheet of pickup and delivery details, and dismissed her, saying he looked forward to their cooperation.

In the fever of overdraw, Kyndel experienced a series of visions: Liena being taken from him in a camp cell; the faces of his parents, Gian, Otisen and Liena, all of whom he felt had betrayed him; beatings over bread; Luca's blood; Heraldur consumed by his scars; Jelert burning; and the Obelisk tearing out his power. His tether then widened, and for a moment he sensed an immense source of energy. He woke gagged, which Jelert explained was because he had been shouting. Jelert told him he had been unconscious for days, that the palace was in turmoil and that he had killed Master Lazaro. Kyndel said that Gian had thrown Lazaro in his path. The engineers' leave after Lazaro's death had allowed Jelert to hide him. Asked why he was helping, Jelert said he preferred to keep the world together one person at a time, and that deciding to care required a less common kind of strength. Kyndel called this foolish, but conceded that acting alone and refusing to trust Heraldur's plan had brought him to this point. Before losing consciousness again, he asked Jelert not to blame him for cutting away what was corrupt.

Prompted by Kyndel's words, Jelert resolved to stop avoiding the misuse of his inventions. In the laboratory he found Blazej building a railcaster from their rail prototype. Blazej claimed he had done it for both of them and promised funding and hospitals, but let slip that he had gone to Gian on inspection day and sunk the railway project himself. Jelert punched him in the face. He then used his rank to get past the guard at Gian's office and interrupted a meeting. Playing the arrogant engineer, he claimed credit for aetheric magnetic flux, cited his three years in the Empress's service and the runeforge capacitor, and asked to be made head engineer. Gian noted that Blazej had already secured Lazaro's post but set a test: Jelert was to complete Lazaro's unfinished prototype, which Gian said the assassin had stolen, within three days. The schematics showed the torc Jelert had been repairing, and he promised a working one by the end of the day. Asked how he would get around the weapons ban, Gian said that was his own problem. In an office in the east wing, Jelert built in a concealed row of runes that would trigger a feedback loop at high energy and disable the torc.

Kyndel woke alone at night with sharpened senses and found his left arm replaced by fused iron that he recognized as his own creation. With effort he shaped it into a working arm, gaining control one finger at a time. Beneath it, the stump a few inches below the shoulder was sealed with iron veins. He understood that he was now permanently at full draw, though he could reduce the flow to a steady stream, and that he could reshape his creations, turning a dagger into his father's mason's hammer, a spoon, a hook and shears. In the mirror his eyes were a bright molten orange, which accounted for Heraldur's long advantage over him. He took the torc and a coat and climbed down the palace wall on forged hooks. Near the Warrens he watched a Draumer girl forge a crowbar and, for the first time, saw a tether as a cord of light running from the back of her neck. He realized that his own flaring tether had been leading Redarms to him. At the gang's hideout his eyes caused men to mistake him for a Redarm, and he fought several of them until Khamron recognized him. Heraldur appeared, his own tether visible, and the two withdrew to talk.

Kyndel demanded answers and an equal partnership. Heraldur refused the partnership but agreed to answer his questions once Kyndel handed over the torc. From the roof Kyndel saw the Eldtree, strands of light rising from the ground throughout Burunt and joining above the palace into a column that branched out above the clouds. Heraldur described it as the tether of the world and said he did not know what it drew upon. He then revealed that Gian was his brother. They had once worked together toward a free Burunt. Heraldur taught himself Signarium, and together they built the Obelisk, which was intended to let a Draumer produce cyrusite voluntarily. When Heraldur tried to destroy it, Gian chained him, tortured him with it and cut his face, and Heraldur became overdrawn in one eye. On the night Gian seized the city, Heraldur killed four soldiers and escaped, and Gian announced that Heydar Magnus had died fighting the Requing. After two failed attempts on Gian's life, Heraldur had spent five years building strength. His plan was to destroy the Obelisk, free the camps and storm the palace. Kyndel proposed freeing the collared Redarms as well, Liena among them, and Heraldur granted him a single chance.

In her office, Amara found Clodagh going through House Khar's books and alarmed at the size of its debt. They agreed on terms: House Khar would give the Alshien a base and a public front, and Amara accepted the rebellion as her own cause. Clodagh estimated their strength at just over a thousand fighters, with perhaps five hundred more following Farzin, against roughly 3,500 soldiers under Gian, and reported that mass production of railcasters was expected within two months. She rejected Amara's proposal to recruit Jelert. Amara shared her belief that Khorshed Kazemi was Kyndel Heim, and Otisen, visibly pale, was sent to find him. Dhonya then burst in demanding the Founder's ring for a charity ball. Amara lost her temper, called her sick and delusional, blamed her for the House's ruin, and revealed that Gian held the ring. Dhonya, briefly lucid, apologized and left with a disappointed Balfourd. Amara said her mother had been ill since Amara was thirteen. She then proposed reviving House Khar's annual charity gala, funded by raids on cyrusite shipments, as a controlled setting in which to isolate and kill Gian. Clodagh agreed.

Jelert had returned from Gian's test to find that Kyndel had left through the window, taking Jelert's favorite wool coat. Days later he was settling in as Master Engineer but had not seen Blazej. Gian, now always guarded by a Redarm, visited and implied that Blazej had been killed for lying. Jelert realized that his own honesty had brought this about. Gian said that many engineers had protested the railcasters and that he had made arrangements for the dissenters. He offered Jelert an inducement in the form of a home and a city built around Signarium, while admitting that he would build weapons to defend against the Empire and refusing a rail line to the mainland. When Jelert warned that the cyrusite supply would run out, Gian showed him a glowing piece of raw, unrefined cyrusite, implying a source outside the Empire. An explosion then shook the palace, serving as the threat that accompanied the offer. Signarium Hall had been bombed and every engineer inside killed, and Gian intended to blame the Alshien. Frightened, Jelert submitted and told Gian he understood.

Amara came home after sundown, exhausted, and found her mother, Dhonya, in the parlor. Dhonya was fully lucid and spoke with the authority of the matriarch who had once led House Khar. Amara admitted that she felt she was only postponing an inevitable collapse and pretending to be strong. Dhonya told her that leadership consists of holding things together by persistent personal effort, that damaged things can endure if someone keeps repairing them, and that strength lies in what a person does whatever title they hold. When Amara said she felt like the villain, Dhonya replied that heroes tend to die young and leave disorder behind, while Amara was a survivor and a leader. Dhonya joked about how seldom her lucid periods came, and the two reminisced about her habit of putting too much cream in her coffee. The conversation repaired the rift left by Amara's earlier outburst. They talked for hours, and Amara went to bed feeling restored.

Jelert was in effect a prisoner. Gian controlled the ports and had given him Lazaro's notes but no access to the production facilities. Jelert had avoided contacting Dusan, who had been right about Gian, in order to protect him. On Gian's orders he attended Lord Modir's gala, where a drunk noblewoman praised him for the railcasters under a garbled name, and he reflected that he was no freer than the Redarms. Amara arrived in a teal and brown gown, and they joked about the poor pastry and oversalted pork. She mentioned the newspapers' account of an Alshien attack on the engineers. Although clearly attracted to her, Jelert told himself she was simply his only friend. She led him to a private alcove, took his hand and embraced him, and his composure gave way. He admitted that the railcasters had grown from his idea against his intentions, that he had taken the Master Engineer post to stop them, and that Gian himself had bombed the engineers to silence them and blamed the Alshien. After visibly weighing the situation, Amara told him she could help and that there were people she wanted him to meet.

The morning after the Modir gala, Amara brought Jelert to meet Clodagh, who reacted with fury to the presence of an imperial officer. Jelert explained that he had been raised to believe in the Empire's order until Yeshall, a territory north of Prikaz, was destroyed by explosives adapted from his power cell, and that he had asked to be sent to Burunt as atonement. He told them that Blazej had built the railcasters behind his back, that Gian had had Blazej killed, and that he had sheltered Kyndel for several days. Clodagh grudgingly accepted him. Drawing on Lazaro's notes, Jelert reported that the railcaster production line in the caverns beneath the palace would be complete that week. Amara planned to smuggle him in inside a crate with her next cyrusite delivery so that he could sabotage it. Jelert proposed recruiting Dusan, arguing that Gian was separating Empire-loyal Prikizans from his own followers, and Amara allowed discreet contact. He warned that the Empress would have to be confronted once Gian fell, and that a cyrusite source outside the Empire could undermine faith in Valenska. He expected to have no home in the Empire afterward and considered the cost worth paying.

At night, Amara's crew loaded cyrusite crates at an apparently abandoned three-story factory between the city center and Mintika Point. The foreman called it imperial storage, but Amara concluded that it was a front for a cyrusite mine. She noticed long wooden boxes missing from the manifest, which the foreman said held parts of a large signaric machine bound for the palace. She had one opened and found an object of black metal nearly six feet tall, with a round base tapering to a point, curling jagged spines and inactive runes; it looked grown more than built. Jelert, hidden in her carriage, offered to examine it, but she insisted that the railcasters came first. An extra crate had been slipped into the shipment to carry him. Before he left, Jelert told her she was different from the person he had taken her for, and she apologized for misleading him. He said that he cared about her, and she replied that she knew and felt the same.

After hours inside the crate, Jelert climbed out in a storeroom beneath the palace and followed a humming sound to a vast cavern. From a walkway he observed an assembly line. Belts fed a central wheel driven by a signaric engine, which workers fueled with raw, honey-colored cyrusite. Unskilled laborers each performed a single step, and heated stamps imprinted the runes, so that only one trained engineer was needed. He estimated that the line finished a railcaster every six minutes and that perhaps a couple hundred were already crated. When a worker lost his hand in the machinery, the foreman stopped the line for a half-hour break, which gave Jelert his opportunity. Judging that subtle sabotage would be repaired quickly, he cut the power line to every station, chiseled away the engine's regulator runes, routed all power to the furnace, opened the throttle and fled. In a hallway he ran directly into Gian, his advisors and two Redarms. Gian remarked that he had not expected Jelert quite so soon. The engine exploded behind them, and Gian's smile disappeared.

Weeks after his escape from the palace, Kyndel was training with Heraldur and growing impatient to rescue Liena. His iron arm, shaped over the stump with ventilation holes, rubbed his skin raw, and Heraldur had trimmed the stump with a bonesaw to help it heal. Heraldur warned that Kyndel was burning through his own reserves. Both men now showed their orange eyes openly, and rumors of fire-eyed demons had raised their standing in the Warrens. At a safehouse with Khamron and his lieutenants, Heraldur set out the plan. He and Kyndel would lead a strike team through the sewers to the Draumer camps to free and recruit the prisoners, while the others fortified the old Warrens wall. The operation was timed for the night of the Khar gala, when Gian would be distracted. They still had no way to free the Redarms without a collar to study. Heraldur had rejected the Alshien plan to free the Draumer and scatter them, preferring to unite them as a fighting force. Kyndel was reunited with Lefty, now Heraldur's quartermaster, who teased him about his attachment to the Redarm.

On the night of the revived Khar gala, the estate was lavishly decorated with Alshien money. The plan called for Amara to invite Gian to her office for a private conversation. In the narrow hallway his Redarms would have to walk ahead or behind him, allowing Alshien crossbowmen to shoot through concealed openings between two paintings and finish what Otisen had attempted ten years earlier. Three weeks had passed since Jelert disappeared into the palace, and Amara hoped he was alive in captivity. Alshien operatives posed as servers and minstrels, Clodagh mingled in formal silks, and Otisen watched the palace perimeter. Gian's men had returned the Founder's ring days earlier. Dhonya, lucid and in high spirits, wore it and told Amara that her father would be proud of her, as she herself was. She then said she would wait in the kitchens, showing that she understood more than a party was under way and asserting her authority over her own house. Balfourd went with her. Amara welcomed her guests and prepared for the Viceroy's death.

Kyndel led Heraldur and nearly a hundred Warrens fighters through the sewers to the Draumer prison beneath Mintika Point. Heraldur wore the completed vambrace, which protected those near him from the Obelisk. They blew open the patched breach through which Kyndel had once escaped and entered the Yard, where Kyndel was briefly paralyzed by memories. Guards armed with railcasters killed about a dozen of the team before Kyndel cut them down with forged blades and iron claws. Only about two dozen starved prisoners remained, and they were carried to the Warrens. Kyndel opened the Obelisk chamber by flowing his iron hand into the lock, but the Obelisk was gone. Heraldur blamed Kyndel's attack on Gian, slammed him against a wall and said he should have killed him. Two Redarms, a man with a crystal axe and a woman with a forged bow, then ambushed them. After a fight with no deaths they agreed to talk, but the talks soured when Heraldur demanded a collar to study. Pressed about Liena, the Redarms said she had been taken away for breaking ranks to help Kyndel. A rhythmic pounding then approached.

Gian arrived at Amara's gala in military regalia, accompanied by Redarms and attendants wearing yellow armbands. He mocked her pretensions to her station and proclaimed a Burunt that would submit to neither the Requing nor the Empire. Amara, who knew that the Requing incursion of ten years earlier had been a fabrication Gian used to destroy his rivals, saw Jelert in his escort shaking his head in warning. A pounding grew louder, and the doors burst open to admit silent metal constructs nearly ten feet tall, which were Gian's Warriors. Gian vowed to drive out the Empire and eliminate those who had corrupted the nation from within. A Redarm seized Amara, and Isadore Meyers read the charges against her: treason, conspiring with the Alshien to assassinate Gian Magnus as the first king of Burunt, and paying House debts with traceable stolen money. House Khar was to be dissolved, its members executed and the name Khar'andor struck from record. The disguised Alshien attacked and were crushed. Clodagh charged Gian from behind a smoke screen and was killed by a Warrior's blow. The nobles looked away. Balfourd was dragged in bleeding, Dhonya was struck to the floor, and Gian announced that he had a city to purge.

Jelert, who had been Gian's prisoner for weeks, saw Amara knocked unconscious and taken away. In Gian's carriage, Captain Farzin, wearing a yellow band, reported that the Alshien had entered the city as expected, and Jelert realized that the rebel leader Dusan had hunted for months was Gian's agent. Gian said that losing his first engineering partner had taught him patience, and that Jelert's completion of Lazaro's torc had made the Warriors possible. The feedback loop Jelert had hidden in it had never triggered. An explosion overturned the carriage, and a rock through the window killed Isadore Meyers. Outside, Gian's forces were fighting loyal Prikizans in teal. Jelert helped three Prikizan soldiers and, haunted by Yeshall, built a crude bomb from the carriage's cyrusite housing. Wearing Gian's cracked spectacles, he saw a cord of light rising from the neck of every Redarm and Warrior. The bomb tore open four Warriors and exposed human flesh inside. As they repaired themselves with forged mist, a glowing noose formed where torc met tether; they began screaming and attacked friend and foe indiscriminately. Jelert fled, horrified by his own part in what had happened.

Amara woke in a carriage, believing her mother dead and wishing to die herself. In the rain her Redarm captor bound her in forged stone manacles and prepared to execute her on Gian's orders, but a thrown handaxe killed him as Otisen and Alshien fighters arrived to rescue her. Otisen broke her manacles and told her that the Alshien leaders were dead or missing and that she was now their hope. He also told her that her mother was alive but gravely wounded, that Farzin had betrayed all their plans, and that twenty-seven people had died at the estate. In a townhouse in the merchant quarter, the dying Dhonya told Amara that legacy matters little, urged her not to repeat her own mistake of living for a dead husband's memory, and asked her to live for the people still alive. After Dhonya's death Amara vowed to give it meaning. She took command of the survivors and organized scouts, care for the wounded and supplies. A teenage scout brought in a bound Prikizan officer who claimed to be a friend: Jelert. He admitted he had made a mistake, and Amara told him they would set it right.

A towering steel figure covered in runes emerged from the prison's mess hall. Kyndel recognized it as Liena: her limbs had been amputated and her torso fused into a Warrior frame, with a bronze torc at her neck and her eyes empty. The female Redarm said this was what Gian did to the disloyal and blamed Kyndel. When Liena forged obsidian armor, the torc and her tether formed a leash of light that drove her into a screaming frenzy, and she killed both Redarms. Heraldur saved Kyndel from an obsidian spear and urged retreat. When Kyndel refused, Heraldur left, saying he regretted losing a useful tool. Alone, Kyndel forged a massive iron wall, split it into bands around her frame, kicked out her knee, pinned her and tore the torc apart. Her scream became human again. She apologized for being unable to stop, thanked him for letting her die as herself, and asked him to forgive both himself and her. She died, her eyes fading to brown. Following Heraldur's trail, Kyndel found two dead Warriors and then Heraldur himself, dead against a building. He gathered the pieces of the cracked vambrace and walked toward the burning city.

Hours later, with Burunt burning for the second time in a decade, Amara directed a growing joint resistance of Buritions and Prikizans from a storefront, sending the Iron Spears to the east docks and organizing chains to carry water. Kyndel arrived with an iron left arm, transformed from the awkward Khorshed she had known. He said he had freed two Warriors on the way by destroying their torcs. He explained that Warriors were enslaved Draumer whose tethers the torcs hijacked, that they went mad when they forged, and that they died soon after being freed. Jelert connected this to his feedback loop. Amara ordered the information spread so that fighters would aim for the torcs. She named Gian, last seen fleeing Warriors west of Mintika Point, a secondary objective to be captured alive. Kyndel objected violently but accepted her promise of eventual justice. More than a hundred Warriors were thought to be loose. Dusan reported that they attacked Redarms first, and Jelert said they could see tethers. Kyndel reported Heraldur's death and identified the militia holding the Warrens as Heraldur's gangs. Amara ordered the camp moved there and asked for ideas to stop the Warriors.

As Warriors ravaged the city, Kyndel hesitated to share an idea that required trusting others with his fate. Remembering Heraldur dying alone, and Liena, who had not died alone, he spoke. The Obelisk drained Draumer power and converted it into cyrusite, so it should also work on the Warriors. Prikizan officers called this blasphemy, but Jelert confirmed that he had seen its product. Amara admitted that Gian had used her to smuggle the Obelisk into the palace in pieces. Because its range was only about thirty feet, Jelert proposed powering it through Kyndel's tether and guessed that it stood on the ruined factory floor. Kyndel gave him Heraldur's broken vambrace to repair. Amara sent Kyndel and Jelert to the palace, and Dusan and Otisen volunteered to go with them. Kyndel recognized Otisen as the guard who had saved him and later given him up. He cut off Otisen's apology, and Otisen swore loyalty to him on the Eldtree and on his parents' graves. Jelert confessed that his sabotage had driven the Warriors mad, and Kyndel said blame could wait. Amara, in ill-fitting leather armor, rallied hundreds of people by declaring all of them her own.

Jelert repaired the vambrace by touch and wished he could meet its maker, and Kyndel told him the man was dead. A smugglers' tunnel brought the four close to the palace. Dusan's spear and Kyndel's billhook arm brought down one Warrior, but more than a dozen others gave chase. Kyndel found a service door and sealed the tunnel behind them with the largest iron wall he had ever forged. On the cleared factory floor stood the Obelisk, a twisted tree of dark metal with pulsing runes, and Gian, in a dirty undershirt and accompanied by two Redarms, was trying to make it work. Gian aimed a railcaster at Jelert, called him a traitor and insisted that Lazaro's designs should have worked. Kyndel defended Jelert and accused Gian of imprisoning his own brother and torturing children, and told him that his brother had died that night. Gian maintained that his brother had died fighting the Requing, then broke down, calling everything a sacrifice for Burunt. With Warriors approaching, they agreed to a truce, and Gian warned that because of his wrist band the Redarms would die if he did. Jelert and Gian rebuilt the Obelisk while the others barricaded the entrances and held off the Warriors.

Amara led a column of soldiers and civilians through the burning city toward the Warrens, while volunteers acted as decoys to draw Warriors away, knowing they would probably die. Stragglers joined until the column numbered more than a thousand. Near the Warrens two Warriors crashed into the crowd. When a ring of soldiers failed to stop them, Amara ordered the crowd to overwhelm one, deliberately accepting heavy losses, and a broad woman with a woodcutter's axe split its torc. The second Warrior turned on a group of nine surviving Redarms. Amara told them about the torcs, and they brought it down. Their leader, without a helmet, pledged their help, observing that they knew Gian was alive because they themselves still lived. At the Warrens gate, Heraldur's men refused to admit Prikizans and Redarms until Amara told them that Heraldur was dead and that Kyndel Heim had sent her. The gate opened. A great wave of Warriors, some bounding on all fours or crossing the rooftops, then charged toward the Warrens, and Amara quietly urged Jelert to hurry.

On the factory floor, Kyndel fought at full draw, and his hatred of Gian and will to survive made his iron harder than ever. Otisen pulled him away from a killing blow. Kyndel told him to strike only at Warriors already down because he was too slow, and Otisen told Kyndel to stay alive so that he could protect them all afterward. With the stone-forging Redarm and Dusan, they brought down two more Warriors, one of which fired glass-like shards from its chest. Jelert called Kyndel to the Obelisk and strapped the repaired vambrace to his flesh arm, since it would not work through iron. He warned that if the link broke before it stabilized, the feedback would destroy the Obelisk, Kyndel and probably the chamber. Power flooded Kyndel through proper channels, unlike the torment of the camps, and he credited the design to Heraldur, or to Jelert. Jelert and Gian laid down covering fire with railcasters. With his entire tether consumed, Kyndel could not forge. The runes flared, agony gripped the base of his skull, and he fell to his knees with his hand still on the panel, calling out for Jelert.

Through his lenses, Jelert saw that the arrays were holding stable and that the pain was the cost of channeling so much power. He eased two regulators and reassured Kyndel. Gian then struck him with a railcaster and declared that he no longer needed a traitor. With Kyndel bound to the Obelisk, Gian insisted that the Warriors had been meant to free Burunt from foreign rulers and never for conquest, and Kyndel shouted that he was lying. The stone-forging Redarm broke away from the battle, declaring that he would take no more, and Gian shot him through the chest. Jelert seized his own railcaster and shot Gian beneath the collarbone. Gian looked at him with bitter disappointment and bled to death. The Obelisk released a blinding white wave, and every Warrior fell. Dusan and Otisen returned carrying the unconscious crystal-forging Redarm. Kyndel looked at Gian's body and told Jelert that he had killed him. Orange cyrusite crystals then burst from the Obelisk's branches and drove into the stone. Otisen carried Kyndel out, Dusan carried the Redarm, and the palace collapsed behind them.

At the Warrens wall the defenders were losing ground despite the Redarms' forged defenses. A copper-forging Redarm killed a Warrior on Amara's section of the wall, but a Prikizan laborer and the soldier fighting beside her were killed. A Warrior breached the wall a hundred feet away, and four more poured through, killing dozens. A shimmering wave of energy then swept across the city and extinguished the signaric lights. Every Warrior collapsed, as did the copper-forging Redarm beside Amara, though she herself felt nothing. A Burition used the Redarm's own axe to break his collar while it was nullified, and a minute later the Redarm stirred and was helped to his feet. With a deafening crack, a colossal orange cyrusite formation burst out of the palace, which collapsed beneath it. Amara prayed for the four men she had sent there. The rising sun shone through the translucent crystal and lit the city in orange. Survivors cheered, mourned and wandered, all uncertain about what would follow. Amara straightened and resolved that the night would not cost them their future as well.

Three months after the Empire's cyrusite shipments stopped, Jelert was Master Engineer, working from a half-built office. He won over Prikizan merchants seeking cyrusite by promising a magno-signaric rail line connecting every sizable island in the chain. He was building the Signarium-powered city Gian had promised, now meant to serve everyone, and he carried guilt for killing Gian. He wore a new coat Amara had given him. Kyndel sat with Otisen at a broken fountain in the Warrens. Revenge had been his guiding purpose, and with Gian dead he had lost his sense of direction; he resented that Jelert had struck the fatal blow. Otisen argued that living in a world without Gian would be the greater revenge, but Kyndel stayed away from the Queen's speech. Amara had been crowned first Queen of Burunt by a unanimous vote of the nobility led by Lord Yasser Turan. She touched the names Dhonya Khar'Andor and Clodagh Askar on a memorial inscribed "The Remembered of Crownfall." She had formed a ruling council, offered Prikizans safe passage home and received no reply from the Empress. She and Jelert were now a couple. She climbed the dais and spoke about the future they would build together.

title: Timeline
blurb: An in-world chronology of Burunt, from the founding of its oldest houses to the aftermath of Crownfall.

quote.text: It’s hard to believe it’s been nearly ten years

lead:
This timeline places the events of Crownfall and its backstory in in-world order. Exact dates are rare in the book, and most past events are located relative to the Viceroy's rise to power, roughly a decade before the story opens 1. Where the order of events is unclear in the book, this is noted.

Each entry is hidden until the chapter in which it is revealed. See also the history of Burunt and the chapter guide.

sections.html:
The deep past is largely undated. The entries below follow the order implied by the story, where one is implied.

  • Prikaz expanded into an empire. Its people believe that cyrusite, which forms far below their capital, is the blood of the Earth Mother Valenska, and that it confers a mandate to elevate other civilizations 13.
  • House Khar has belonged to Burunt since the city was founded 13.
  • The original surname of House Khar was Khar'andor 29.
  • The oldest bloodlines of Burunt, the Founding Houses, possess Founder's rings: silvery bands that are Draumer creations 49.
  • The Eldtree, which Heraldur describes as the tether of the whole world, stands over Burunt and can be seen by only a few people. According to Heraldur it has always existed 33.
  • At one time Draumer moved freely through the streets of Burunt 1.
  • Burunt was governed by the Council of Lords 6. House Khar became wealthy through its fleet and its trade with the Requing Federation 6, and held an annual charity gala to close the social season 634.

• Guild Master Heim (Enir), a Draumer, wielded considerable influence among the city's craftsmen and Draumer. His son, Kyndel, was born at the Heim Estate 527.
  • Amara Khar spent her childhood in an independent Burunt. Her father died of illness when she was nine, and her mother, Dhonya, took charge of the House and improved its standing 313.
  • Gian Magnus and his brother Heydar (later known as Heraldur) worked together for a free Burunt. Heraldur taught himself Signarium so that his designs could be manufactured in Gian's factories 33.
