  • The brothers built the Obelisk, which was intended to allow a Draumer to create cyrusite voluntarily. In practice it extracted power by force 33.
  • After Heraldur tried to destroy the Obelisk, Gian had him chained, tortured him with the device and cut his face. Heraldur became overdrawn in one eye and was held as a power source for producing cyrusite 1633.

These events occurred about ten years before the novel begins 124.

  • Gian used a fabricated Requing incursion as a pretext for eliminating his rivals 44. His public account holds that a Requing raid killed his brother and that he rallied Prikizan soldiers docked in the city to defeat it 24.
  • Gian stormed the Heim Estate with foreign soldiers and killed Mistress Heim in front of her son. At Master Heim's pleading, the house guard Otisen shot Gian in the shoulder with a crossbow and escaped with Kyndel 527.
  • The Warrens were gutted by fire during the conflict that brought the Viceroy to power 1.
  • On the night Gian took the city, Heraldur killed the four soldiers sent to move him and escaped. Gian announced that Heydar Magnus had died fighting the Requing 33.
  • Gian brought Burunt into the Prikaz Empire and governed it as Viceroy 1324. In return he obtained imperial engineers to finish the Obelisk 33.
  • The Empire banned trade with the Requing Federation, destroying House Khar's trade routes 617.

• The Alshien rebellion formed during the first year of Gian's rule 13.
  • Gian carried out a purge of Draumer and their prominent relatives. Draumer were hunted, and those captured were sent to the Draumer camps 15.
  • Otisen hid Kyndel with his sister in the countryside until Otisen's cousin sold the boy to Prikizan soldiers for the Viceroy's bounty. Otisen left the same night to join the rebellion 27.
  • In the camps Kyndel befriended Liena and spent years chained in front of the Obelisk 1619. Liena was removed from the cells, and Kyndel came to believe she had died of overdraw 1626.
  • Gian enslaved overdrawn Draumer as Redarms, controlled by rune-etched collars, with the knowledge of the Empress 28.
  • Heraldur remained weak for months after his escape and failed in a solo attempt on Gian's life. Years later, a second attempt using hired fighters was defeated by the Redarms 33.
  • Dhonya Khar fell ill when Amara was thirteen. At fourteen Amara represented the House in court over the repossession of its first ship 34.
  • Roughly five years before the novel, Heraldur began accumulating followers, influence and power in preparation for a final confrontation 33.
  • Roughly two years before the novel, Kyndel escaped the camps through an opening created when an elderly Draumer woman died in an explosion 514.

The book does not place these events in relation to the history of Burunt.

  • Jelert Egarro graduated first in his class at the Imperial Academy and received the Admiralty's Bronze Pin before the age of twenty 2.
  • Jelert spent several years working for the Empress 13, later specified by him as three 31.
  • Jelert's runeforge capacitor was adapted into an explosive and used to suppress the Yeshall rebellion, killing thousands. He was awarded a medal 1213.
  • Jelert volunteered for service in the territories and selected Burunt in part because signaric weapons are illegal there 13.

sections.h: The novel: spring and the social season
sections.html:
• With the social season approaching, Kyndel decided to infiltrate the nobility's parties and kill the Viceroy 1. Jelert was at sea, bound for Burunt 2.
  • Alshien raiders attacked Jelert's troop ship, killing Mirek and four others 2.
  • Kyndel stole the Khar Founder's ring 4 and was conscripted by Heraldur 5. House Khar's debts were transferred to Brothers Incorporated 6.
  • Jelert arrived in Burunt and, without realizing it, helped unload Amara's contraband 7.
  • Almost a week later Jelert presented his rail proposal to the Viceroy 8. Some weeks into his service to Heraldur, Kyndel met Amara at the Stilton party 9.
  • Amara began supplying the Alshien 11. Roughly a month after the raid, Jelert and Amara had dinner together 1213.
  • Heraldur disclosed that he was a Draumer and began to train Kyndel 1416.
  • Amara obtained Clodagh's confession to leading the Alshien 17.
  • The rail prototype was successfully tested 18. One week before the Viceroy's gala, Jelert and Dusan fell out 20.

sections.h: The novel: the Viceroy's gala and its aftermath
sections.html:
• At the gala, Gian used the federalized bank to call in the nobility's debts 21.
  • Gian unveiled the railcaster and attributed it to Blazej 25.
  • Kyndel stole the torc; Lazaro was killed; Kyndel lost his arm; and Liena killed Latif and revealed her identity 26.
  • Amara joined the Alshien 27. A few days later Gian hired her to smuggle cyrusite 29.
  • Jelert became a candidate for head engineer and finished Lazaro's torc 31.
  • Kyndel woke overdrawn, with an iron arm, and went back to Heraldur, who disclosed that he was Gian's brother 3233.
  • Less than a week after Kyndel's attack, Gian bombed Signarium Hall and had Blazej killed 35.
  • Jelert confessed to Amara at Lord Modir's gala and joined the Alshien the following morning 3738.
  • Two days afterward Jelert was smuggled beneath the palace, where he destroyed the railcaster line and was captured by Gian 3840.
  • Three weeks later House Khar held its revived gala 4142.

sections.h: The novel: the night of Crownfall
sections.html:
The climax spans a single night, from the evening of the Khar gala to sunrise 4254.

  • Heraldur and Kyndel raided the Draumer prison and found that the Obelisk was no longer there 43.
  • At the Khar gala Gian revealed the Warriors, proclaimed himself king, and killed Clodagh 44.
  • Isadore Meyers died, and the Warriors went berserk throughout the city 45.
  • Dhonya Khar died, and Amara took command of the survivors 46.
  • Kyndel released Liena from her torc before her death. Heraldur was killed fighting Warriors 47.
  • Amara's combined resistance relocated to the Warrens 48.
  • Jelert killed Gian. Kyndel powered the Obelisk, which disabled every Warrior before growing into a colossal mass of cyrusite that destroyed the palace 5354.
  • The sun rose over the ruined city, its light passing through the crystal 54.

• Imperial shipments of cyrusite to Burunt ceased 55.
  • Amara was crowned the first Queen of Burunt and established a ruling council. Prikizans were offered safe passage home, and several hundred chose to remain 55.
  • A few weeks before the epilogue, Burunt began mining its own cyrusite 55.
  • By the summer, three months after the shipments ended, a memorial to "The Remembered of Crownfall" stood in the square, and the Empress had not yet responded to Amara's request for a parley 55.

title: Kyndel Heim
blurb: Kyndel Heim is a nineteen-year-old Draumer thief from the Warrens of Burunt and one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall.

quote.text: There’s no help in this city.

rows: Lordling (used by Lefty)1; Khorshed of House Kazemi9
Heraldur's crew5; the joint resistance led by Amara Khar48
Draumer: tether draw and forging1; affinity for iron4; overdrawn, with a forged iron left arm32
Enir (father)5; Mistress Heim (mother)27
Alive; living in the Warrens three months after Crownfall55

lead:
Kyndel Heim is a Draumer and street thief from the Warrens, the burned-out slum district of Burunt.1 Nineteen years old when the story begins, he is the first of the novel's three point-of-view characters; the other two are Jelert Egarro and Amara Khar.1 His goal is to assassinate Viceroy Gian Magnus, who governs Burunt for the Prikaz Empire, and his plan is to reach him by gaining entry to the parties of the nobility.1

Kyndel regards his life as a long campaign of small, repeated injuries against the Empire.1 He funds it by selling stolen goods to the fence Lefty, and he relies on his Draumer abilities for speed and night vision.1 He is soon drawn into the service of the Warrens Baron Heraldur, who later becomes his unwilling teacher.5

sections.html:
Kyndel has shoulder-length, easily tangled hair, dark eyes and a narrow waist. He ties up his breeches with a length of rope, having had no proper belt since childhood.1, 9 His clothes are threadbare and his leather shoes worn.4 He is of modest size, though taller than Amara.9 His skin is warm brown and his hair dark. His eyes, originally brown, began to glow amber and later a molten orange. After losing his left arm at the palace, he replaced it with a construct of forged iron.26, 28, 32

His temperament is quick and abrasive. He is sarcastic, loses his temper easily and curses readily; his usual oath is thorns.1 Having lived alone for years, he habitually talks to himself.4 He hates the Empire, the Viceroy and the nobility, whom he blames for standing by while Burunt was sold.4 He favors direct action over intrigue and considers his own thieving the more honest way of getting what he needs.9

Beneath the anger he shows signs of conscience. He hesitated before abandoning a dying imperial soldier who pleaded with him for help.1 Anger serves him as a defense against grief and fear, and after nearly dying he acknowledged that his insistence on doing everything alone had brought about his downfall.19, 30

As a Draumer, Kyndel draws on his tether to gain a surge of euphoric power that heightens his senses and improves his speed, strength, balance and night vision.1 He can also forge: he expels gray mist from his palm and shapes it into solid objects.1 His early constructs, which he uses as daggers, lockpicks and caltrops, are brittle and release a blinding flash of light when they shatter.1, 4

Kyndel has an affinity for iron, although his early iron constructs shatter as easily as the rest.4 Holding too much power brings skull pain, tunnel vision and the risk of overdraw, and heavy use is followed by a fatigue resembling a hangover; for this reason he avoids alcohol.4, 9 His control improved in stages. He produced his first durable construct, a dagger that stayed solid and sharp, when he threw it in a moment of pure fury.14 Heraldur later taught him that a construct's strength depends on its maker's focus and will during forging, and trained him to channel his rage into forging instead of suppressing it.16

The fight at the palace left Kyndel permanently overdrawn. His tether remains at full draw, though he can reduce it to a steady flow that keeps his senses keen and dulls his pain.32 His eyes now glow orange, and he gained two new abilities. He can reshape a construct after forging it, for example turning a dagger into a mason's hammer, a hook, a lockpick or shears, and he can perceive other Draumer's tethers as cables of light.32 The second ability led him to realize that the flare of his own tether had been guiding the Redarms to him.32 Heraldur later showed him the Eldtree from a rooftop and described it as the tether of the world.33

Over the stump of his left arm Kyndel forged a mass of iron that became a functioning arm, controllable down to the individual fingers.32 He can dissolve its hand into mist to fill and break a lock, grow claws from it, or reshape it into a shield or a billhook.43, 47, 50 Prolonged contact with the iron rubs his skin raw.41

By the end of the story Kyndel was forging much larger works, among them an iron wall braced into the rock of a tunnel, the largest construct he had ever made.50 Wearing a repaired vambrace on his remaining arm, he channeled his tether into the Obelisk. The effort caused him agonizing pain and left him unable to forge anything else.52, 53

Kyndel is the son of Enir, a guild master and well-known Draumer.5 His father was a mason with his own workshop; his mother kept a library and wore a red tasseled shawl.1, 9, 14 When Gian Magnus took power roughly ten years before the story, he killed both of Kyndel's parents himself. Kyndel retains fragments of the attack: his mother's scream breaking off, his father dying as he reached for his son, and Gian holding a bloodied knife.5, 24 A house guard carried him to safety.5

By Kyndel's account, the guard who rescued him later sold him for the Viceroy's bounty, and he was sent to the Draumer camps.14 He spent years there, first confined to a cell and then chained before the Obelisk, which drained his power.14, 16 In the camps he befriended another child prisoner, Liena, who made him a flower of obsidian.14 He escaped two years before the story began, when an old Draumer woman set off an explosion that killed her and breached the wall.5, 14 He believed that Liena had died in the camps.14

The guard was Otisen, who later gave Amara his own account of events. He had witnessed Gian cut Mistress Heim's throat, wounded Gian in the shoulder with a crossbow bolt, and fled with the boy at Master Heim's urging.27 He hid Kyndel with his sister in the countryside until his own cousin sold the boy to Prikizan soldiers, and Otisen did nothing to prevent it.27

Chapters 1 to 9

Kyndel is introduced entering the Warrens to sell stolen goods to Lefty. He intends to use the money for forged papers that would admit him to the nobility's parties during the coming social season.1

Leaving Mintika Point, he attacked a young imperial soldier who was kicking an old woman, cut his thigh and left him to bleed to death.1 He then burgled a lightly guarded manor that proved to belong to House Khar, taking two books and a Founder's ring engraved with the name Khar’andor.4 Pursued by two Redarms, he pushed himself to the edge of overdraw and was caught by Khamron after a smuggling run exploded.4

Khamron delivered him to Heraldur, who recognized him as Enir's son. Once Kyndel admitted his intention to kill Gian, Heraldur forced him into service as a thief and spy among the nobility.5 Using the identity of Khorshed of House Kazemi, Kyndel attended a party at the Stilton estate to steal a hexagonal rune plate. A public argument with Amara Khar, during which she noticed the ring on his hand, cost him the opportunity.9

Chapters 10 to 19

Kyndel returned to the Stilton manse and stole the plate, only to find it broken in two. He forged an iron copy and gave it to Heraldur, who accepted it.10 After three successful thefts without a single sighting of Gian at any party, his frustration produced his first lasting dagger.14 A Redarm then attacked him and took Liena's flower. Heraldur intervened, revealed that he was also a Draumer, and agreed to train Kyndel in return for guidance to the Draumer camps.14

The training was marked by violence. When Heraldur disclosed that he had built the Obelisk, Kyndel attacked him.16 Later Heraldur explained that one more theft would complete a signaric vambrace to shield them from the Obelisk. When Kyndel demanded that they move against Gian instead, Heraldur beat him, and Kyndel then drew a Redarm onto the rooftops, fought it and got away.19

Chapters 24 to 33

At the Viceroy's gala Kyndel encountered Lord Yasser Turan, an old friend of his father who failed to recognize him, and spoke with Amara and Jelert.24 Gian's speech, which attributed his brother's death to a Requing raid, revived Kyndel's memories of his mother's murder.24 He went on to steal the signaric torc from Master Lazaro's office. When Gian entered, Kyndel rushed him, and Gian pushed Lazaro into the path of the dagger.26 The Redarm Latif then cut off Kyndel's left arm. The second Redarm killed Latif and removed her helmet, revealing herself as Liena, and carried the overdrawn Kyndel away.26

Liena took Kyndel to Jelert's room, where Jelert tended his wounds and concealed him for several days.28, 30 Kyndel survived the overdraw and told Jelert that Gian had used Lazaro as a shield.30 In the meantime Gian confronted Amara with the ring and dagger recovered from the assassin's severed arm, and she identified Khorshed as Kyndel Heim.29

On waking alone, Kyndel shaped his iron arm, took the torc and Jelert's coat, and climbed down the palace wall.32, 35 At the Warrens hideout he handed the torc to Heraldur, who disclosed that Gian was his brother and set out his plan to destroy the Obelisk and free the Draumer. Kyndel persuaded him to give the collared Redarms one opportunity to be freed.33

Chapters 41 to 47

In the following weeks Kyndel trained with Heraldur while rumors of fire-eyed demons spread through the Warrens.41 On the night of the Khar gala he guided Heraldur and nearly a hundred men through the sewers to the Draumer prison beneath Mintika Point, where he killed the railcaster gunners and freed about two dozen prisoners. The Obelisk had already been moved.43 Two Redarms told him that Liena had broken ranks on his behalf and had been taken as a result.43

Liena then appeared, transformed into one of Gian's Warriors. Heraldur withdrew from the fight and left Kyndel to face her alone. Kyndel destroyed the torc that controlled her, and she died in his arms after asking him to forgive himself.47 Following Heraldur's trail afterward, he found him dead outside Mintika Point and took his broken vambrace.47

Chapters 48 to 55

Kyndel joined Amara's command post, where he explained that the Warriors were enslaved Draumer controlled through their torcs. He objected violently to Amara's decision to capture Gian alive.48 He proposed turning the Obelisk against the Warriors and agreed to power it himself.49 At the post he also recognized Otisen as the guard who had rescued him in childhood.49

In the cavern beneath the palace, Kyndel informed Gian that his brother had died that night, then accepted an uneasy truce so that the Obelisk could be completed.50 While Kyndel channeled his tether into the machine, Gian attacked Jelert, and Jelert shot him dead.52, 53 The Obelisk's wave brought down every Warrior in the city, and Otisen carried the collapsed Kyndel out before the palace fell.53

Three months later Kyndel was living in the ruins of the Warrens with Otisen, left without direction once his revenge was gone. He resented Jelert for taking the killing blow from him and did not attend Queen Amara's speech.55

Heraldur: Heraldur was in turn Kyndel's employer, captor and teacher. Their relationship was violent and marked by mutual distrust. Kyndel sought Heraldur's respect and never felt he had earned it, while Heraldur addressed him dismissively as a boy and refused to treat him as a partner.5, 16, 33, 43

Liena: Liena was Kyndel's closest friend in the camps, where she kept him alive by refusing to let him give up.19 Her death as a Warrior left him mourning the future the two of them never had.47

Amara Khar: Kyndel burgled her house and wore her father's ring while posing as Khorshed.4, 9 She later disclosed his identity to Gian.29

Jelert Egarro: Jelert saved Kyndel's life and hid him in his room, and Kyndel came to acknowledge the value of an ally.28, 30 He restrained his anger when Jelert admitted sabotaging the Warrior torc49 and defended him to Gian,50 but afterward resented him for killing Gian.55

Otisen: Otisen rescued Kyndel as a boy.27 He later swore his life to him and remains at his side in the epilogue.49, 55

Gian Magnus: Gian murdered Kyndel's parents and was the object of his revenge.5 Kyndel never had the chance to kill him personally.53

title: Jelert Egarro
blurb: Major Jelert Egarro is a young Prikizan signaric engineer posted to Burunt and one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall.

quote.text: I don’t make weapons

rows: Major Meddle, a nickname among the ship's crew2
Not stated; he won the Admiralty's Bronze Pin before turning twenty<cite>2</cite>
Prikaz Empire; Signarium Hall8; the Alshien conspiracy against Gian38
Signaric engineer2; Master Engineer of Burunt3555
Heir to the Egarro military line; his father is a career soldier who disapproves of his posting13
Alive; Master Engineer of independent Burunt55

lead:
Major Jelert Egarro is a signaric engineer of the Prikaz Empire and one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall.2 At the start of the novel he arrives in Burunt aboard a troop ship to take up a post in the palace laboratory, Signarium Hall.2, 8 He is a talented and idealistic inventor who believes signarium can improve the lives of ordinary citizens, and he refuses to design weapons.2

Jelert is inquisitive and earnest, given to long technical digressions, and easily flustered by Lady Amara Khar, whom he meets at the docks soon after landing.2, 7 The Viceroy, Gian Magnus, is aware of Jelert's earlier activities in the Empire, a period of his life that Jelert has worked hard to leave behind.8

sections.html:
Jelert is tall, lanky and slender, with pale pink skin, gray eyes and overgrown, untidy light-brown hair, and he blushes readily.2, 7 Amara thinks of his eyes as storm-gray.13 His formal dress is the muted teal coat, waistcoat and rank sash of a Prikizan major and engineer.22

He is intensely curious, asks constant questions, and tends to keep talking about engineering well after his listeners have lost interest.2 He is ambitious and performs well under pressure,8 and he is uncomfortable with the formalities of rank.12 He is also highly sensitive; he vomited following his first battle and agonized over a soldier whose request he had turned down.2 He prays to Valenska for luck and swears by the Goddess and the Halls below.15, 18 Under stress he falls back on humor, often poorly judged, and he describes himself as a citizen of humanity first and of the Empire second.38

Jelert graduated at the top of his class, the youngest person in a decade to do so. Three of his designs were adopted by the Artificer Corps, and before the age of twenty he received the Admiralty's Bronze Pin for systems innovation.2 His skill extends from small repairs, such as fixing a ship's stove by realigning its third runic array,2 to large projects, including a rail system powered by refined cyrusite.8

The rail design depends on a rune Jelert discovered himself, which he named aetheric magnetic flux. It allows a carriage to float above the rails on a repulsion field, moving without friction and using little power.13, 15 New runes are found so rarely that the last person to discover one was appointed to the Empress's personal advisory board.15

Before his posting, Jelert invented the runeforge capacitor, a power source intended for manufacturing, medicine and construction. Someone found a way to make it release all of its energy at once, and it was used as an explosive to crush the rebellion at Yeshall, killing thousands.12, 13

Jelert learned field medicine five years before the story and can treat wounds.28 He repaired the cracked torc Kyndel had stolen and identified it as an energy converter for an unknown power source.28 He is also an effective improviser; he built a crude impact-triggered bomb from a carriage's cyrusite housing.45 With Gian's orange-lensed spectacles he can see Draumer tethers.45 He repaired and enhanced Heraldur's vambrace and rewired the Obelisk to draw its power directly from Kyndel's tether.50

Jelert was educated at the Petrovskaya Academy and worked for the Empress before being posted to Burunt.8

He is the heir to the Egarro family's long military tradition. His father, a career soldier, was proud of his son's talent for signarium but scorns his posting to the territories, mocking it as building toilets for farmers.13

Jelert served the Empress directly for several years (three, by his later account) and was awarded a medal after his runeforge capacitor became the weapon used at Yeshall.13, 31 He stayed on for a time trying to correct the problem, then volunteered for service in the territories. He chose Burunt partly because signaric weapons are banned there.13

Chapters 2 to 8

Jelert is introduced aboard a sail-less signaric troop ship bound for Burunt, whose crew holds a celebration after he repairs its stove.2 He becomes friends with Lieutenant Dusan of the Iron Spears and turns down Private Mirek's request to fix his signaric spear, explaining that he does not make weapons.2

When Alshien rebels raided the ship, Mirek was killed with the unrepaired spear still in his hands. Jelert vomited and held himself responsible.2 In Burunt he lent a dozen soldiers to unload Amara Khar's ship, the Alisma, unaware that it carried contraband, and she invited him to take her to dinner.7 At Signarium Hall he came into conflict with Master Lazaro and presented his rail system to Viceroy Gian, who rejected it as too expensive and alluded to Jelert's past in the Empire. Blazej Rodion then proposed an alliance, and Jelert agreed.8

Chapters 12 to 25

The laboratory proved hostile: the other engineers avoided Jelert and his requisitions were refused.12, 15 Over dinner he told Amara about Yeshall.13 He shared his new rune with Blazej, and together they built a prototype in which a metal puck floated and glided along a track.15, 18 After Blazej warned him about Dusan, Jelert told his friend that his work mattered more than their friendship.18, 20 His attempt to apologize at the Viceroy's gala failed when Dusan suggested that Blazej was using him, and the two parted on bad terms.22 Jelert took Amara's side when Blazej insulted her.23

Gian then unveiled the railcaster, a weapon built on Jelert's aetheric magnetic flux runes, and gave the credit to Blazej, presenting him as the founder of Burition signarium. Jelert saw in it a repetition of Yeshall.25

Chapters 28 to 40

The Redarm Liena brought the wounded Kyndel Heim to Jelert's door and explained that the Redarms were enslaved Draumer. Jelert treated Kyndel and hid him for several days.28, 30 Kyndel's insistence that corruption had to be cut out moved Jelert to act.30, 31 On learning that Blazej had sunk the rail project, he punched him, then talked his way into Gian's office and asked to be made head engineer. Gian set him a test, the completion of Lazaro's torc, and Jelert built a concealed feedback loop into it designed to make it fail under real use.31

As Master Engineer, Jelert discovered that Gian had had Blazej killed for lying and had bombed Signarium Hall to silence engineers who objected to his weapons, blaming the attack on the Alshien.35 Gian also showed him raw cyrusite obtained from a source outside the Empire.35 Feeling like a prisoner, Jelert confessed everything to Amara at Lord Modir's gala.37 She introduced him to Clodagh, and he agreed to sabotage the railcaster production line beneath the palace.38 Smuggled inside in a crate, he overloaded and destroyed the factory's central engine, then ran directly into Gian.39, 40

Chapters 44 to 55

After three weeks as Gian's prisoner, Jelert appeared in the Viceroy's escort at the Khar gala and warned Amara without speaking.44 In Gian's carriage he learned that Farzin was Gian's agent and that his own completed torc had made the Warriors possible.45 When the carriage was blown over, he joined loyal Prikizan soldiers and built a bomb. Looking through Gian's spectacles, he saw that the Warriors were Draumer whose torcs drove them mad whenever they forged.45

Jelert reached Amara's camp as a bound prisoner and admitted to her that he had made a mistake.46 He told Kyndel that his sabotage had caused the Warriors' madness,49 then went to the palace with Kyndel, Dusan and Otisen and worked alongside Gian to make the Obelisk run on Kyndel's tether.50 When Gian clubbed him and killed a Redarm who had turned against him, Jelert shot Gian dead with a railcaster. He then led the escape from the collapsing palace.53

Three months later Jelert was Master Engineer of an independent Burunt, overseeing new cyrusite mining and planning a magno-signaric rail network to link the islands. He had cut his ties with the Empire and continued to feel guilt over Gian's death.55

Dusan: Dusan became Jelert's friend during the voyage to Burunt and later cautioned him that the island was not what it appeared to be.12

Jelert pushed Dusan away under Blazej's influence and later regretted it.20, 22 He at first avoided contacting him in order to keep him safe,37 then brought him into the conspiracy, and Dusan fought beside him on the final night.38, 48, 50

Amara Khar: Jelert has been taken with Amara since their first meeting.7, 8

Amara at first treated him as a useful contact and had Balfourd answer his letters on her behalf.13, 23 After she apologized for misleading him, the two acknowledged their feelings,39 and by the epilogue they were romantically involved. She gave him a new coat combining Prikizan and Burition styles.55

Blazej Rodion: A fellow Petrovskaya graduate and Jelert's only ally in the laboratory, Blazej used Jelert's research to build the railcaster and took the credit for it.8, 25, 31

Kyndel Heim: Jelert saved Kyndel's life, and Kyndel's views shaped his decision to act.28, 31 Their alliance survived Jelert's confession, although Kyndel resented him for killing Gian.49, 55

Gian Magnus: Gian courted, threatened and imprisoned Jelert in turn, and described the engineer's work as his destiny.35, 45 Jelert eventually killed him.53

title: Amara Khar
blurb: Lady Amara Khar is the young head of the impoverished noble House Khar of Burunt and one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall.

quote.text: Anyone we meet is either an opportunity, an ally, or a tool.

rows: Lady Amara of House Khar; heir and acting head of House Khar37; first Queen of Burunt55
Not stated; Kyndel judges her a few years older than himself<cite>4</cite>
House Khar; the Alshien27
Trader and shipping merchant3; smuggler6
Lady Dhonya Khar (mother)6; her late father, former head of House Khar3

lead:
Lady Amara Khar is the heir to House Khar, one of the old noble houses of Burunt, and one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall.3 Her family has lost most of its fortune, and she manages its trade personally, outmaneuvering merchants, cutting household expenses and walking across the city to save money.3 She sorts everyone she meets into three categories: opportunities, allies and tools.3

Amara looks after her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar, and has promised to take care of everything herself.3, 6 Composed and calculating, she relies on strict decorum for protection in a city where her house's poverty is common knowledge.3

sections.html:
Amara has long, wavy black hair that she often braids, hazel eyes inherited from her mother, sharp cheekbones and a slight build.3, 6, 7 Her kaftans are faded but well kept, mended by her maid Sireen; her finest outfit is a sapphire kaftan with gold embroidery and a crimson sash.7, 9

She is proud, self-controlled and calculating. Her dignity is the one thing she refuses to trade, and she treats decorum as a form of armor.3 Her mother taught her to keep her back straight and her face composed and never to show doubt.7 To steady herself she whispers brief reminders of calm and order.11 She has a sharp tongue9 and swears occasionally, usually by Eld's thorns, to the disapproval of her majordomo.6

She justifies manipulating others as a means of survival while feeling guilty about how she uses people,23 and on some days she sees herself as the villain of her own story.36

Amara is an accomplished trader and negotiator with a working knowledge of contract law. Because verbal agreements are not binding in Burunt, she was able to acquire a merchant's goods by signing a written contract for them before his verbal agreement could be honored.3 The text strongly implies that she arranged the delay that kept the merchant from arriving in time.3

She is perceptive, correctly reading the Alshien operative Otisen's identity from his clothing and bearing,11 and adept in society; in a single hour at the Viceroy's gala she secured half a dozen meetings, three verbal commitments and a written contract.21

During the final crisis she proved an able commander, with a talent for logistics, for managing people and for reducing every problem to its essentials.48

Amara's father, the previous head of House Khar, was an open-hearted man of firm principles who died of illness.3 Her mother held the house together for years afterward until she succumbed to an illness of her own, one that proved crueler.3

House Khar once owned a large fleet and a celebrated trading business, both of which collapsed when the Empire outlawed commerce with the Requing Federation.6 Amara has since sold the house's art and rugs one piece at a time and dismissed its guards.6 Her father died when she was nine.13 She was a child when Burunt was still independent, and by the time of the story the island had been part of the Empire for nearly half her life.13

Her mother's illness began when Amara was thirteen, a few years after her father's death.34 At fourteen Amara appeared in court to negotiate compensation for the repossession of the house's first ship.34

Chapters 3 to 9

Amara is introduced at a Burunt marketplace, where she acquires a shipment of goods from Master Naveed and then walks home with her majordomo Balfourd, dealing with household problems along the way.3

She discovered that her father's Founder's ring had been stolen and learned that her bank had transferred her debts to Brothers Incorporated.6 She had already turned to smuggling to keep the house solvent.6 When an inspection threatened to expose the contraband aboard the Alisma, she confronted Dockmaster Riocard, and Major Jelert Egarro unwittingly offered his soldiers to unload the smuggled cargo.7 Seeing a rare contact inside the palace, she invited him to take her to dinner.7 At the Stilton party she argued with a young lord calling himself Khorshed Kazemi, who mocked her mended dress, and noticed the Founder's ring on his hand.9

Chapters 11 to 27

Through Otisen, Amara agreed to supply the Alshien with regular deliveries at a 19 percent surcharge to cover the risk.11 At dinner with Jelert she learned about Yeshall and found herself drawn to him.13 When Otisen and twelve others were detained at the southeast gate, she required Clodagh to sign a confession as leader of the Alshien before sending Balfourd with a letter vouching for the prisoners.17

At the Viceroy's gala Isadore Meyers informed her that the Viceroy had recalled her house's debts.21 Over the evening she defended Jelert against Blazej,23 pressed Khorshed on what he was lying about,24 and watched Gian unveil the railcaster.25 On the ride home Otisen told her how he had saved the young Kyndel Heim from Gian. The account moved her to commit herself to the Alshien in earnest and left her certain that Khorshed was Kyndel.27

Chapters 29 to 42

Gian summoned Amara and showed her her father's ring, recovered from the severed arm of the would-be assassin. Accused of conspiracy, she identified Khorshed as Kyndel Heim, a Draumer, and regretted it once she realized Kyndel might still be alive.29 Gian then hired her company to transport cyrusite in secret.29

Working with Clodagh, Amara came to accept the rebellion as her own cause and proposed reviving House Khar's charity gala as a trap in which to kill Gian.34 She lashed out at her mother and later reconciled with her during a lucid period.34, 36 She recruited Jelert after he confessed his part in creating the railcasters,37, 38 smuggled him into the palace in a crate, and told him that she returned his feelings.39 On the night of the gala she waited for Gian with Alshien crossbowmen concealed along the hall leading to her office.42

Chapters 44 to 55

Gian arrived at the gala with his new Warriors, declared Burunt independent, and had Isadore Meyers charge Amara with treason; House Khar was ordered disbanded.44 The Alshien attack failed, Clodagh was killed, and Amara's mother was struck down.44 A Redarm took Amara into the streets to execute her, and Otisen rescued her.46 Dhonya died soon afterward, urging her daughter to live for the people who were still alive.46

Amara took command of the scattered Alshien and within hours was leading a joint resistance of Buritions and Prikizans. She directed her fighters to aim for the Warriors' torcs and decided that Gian should be captured alive.46, 48

Amara revealed that Gian had used her to smuggle the Obelisk into the palace, sent Kyndel and Jelert to use it, and rallied hundreds of fighters with a speech.49 She then led more than a thousand people to the Warrens, recruited nine surviving Redarms, and gained entry through the Warrens gate by telling Heraldur's men that Kyndel had sent her.51 She was on the wall when the Obelisk's wave brought down the Warriors.54

Three months later the surviving nobility, led by Lord Yasser Turan, crowned Amara the first Queen of Burunt by unanimous vote. She formed a ruling council to balance her authority, offered Prikizans safe passage home, and sent the Empress a request for talks that went unanswered.55 She mourns her mother and Clodagh and privately fears that the future may require monstrous choices.55

Dhonya Khar: Amara is deeply loyal to her mother and shields her from the consequences of her failing memory.6

In private Amara blamed her mother for the house's ruin and on one occasion said so to her face.13, 34 The two reconciled, and before her death Dhonya told Amara that she was proud of her.36, 42, 46

Balfourd: Balfourd is Amara's loyal majordomo, older than her father would have been.3

Jelert Egarro: Amara first regards Jelert as a useful contact with access to the palace.7

She manipulated him at first and felt guilty about it,23 then apologized and admitted her feelings for him.39 By the end of the story their alliance had become a romance.55

Clodagh: The Alshien leader began as a dangerous business partner and became a friend. Amara kept her signed confession and later planned the gala with her.17, 34 Clodagh was killed at the gala.44

Kyndel Heim: Kyndel stole her father's ring.4 Amara revealed his identity to Gian,29 later used his name to gain entry to the Warrens,51 and was disappointed when he did not attend her speech.55

Gian Magnus: Amara depended on Gian's rule while plotting to kill him. He kept her father's ring as leverage and made her his secret carrier of cyrusite.29

title: Gian Magnus
blurb: Gian Magnus is the Viceroy of Burunt, ruling the island for the Prikaz Empire.

quote.text: I’ve heard of some of your exploits in the Empire.

rows: Viceroy of Burunt18; the Empress’s voice in the Burition Isles24; self-proclaimed first king of Burunt44
Prikaz Empire1; his own yellow-banded loyalists4445
A brother, whom Gian says died in a Requing raid24; Heraldur (Heydar Magnus), his brother33
Mentioned in Chapter 1; appears in Chapter 8
Deceased; shot by Jelert Egarro beneath the palace53

lead:
Gian Magnus is the Viceroy of Burunt, governing the island on behalf of the Prikaz Empire.1 He came to power roughly ten years before the story in a violent struggle that left the Warrens burned.1 His government persecutes the Draumer, and Kyndel Heim has sworn to kill him.1

During his purges of the Draumer, Gian killed Kyndel's parents with his own hands.5

sections.html:
Gian has almond-shaped eyes and a warm smile, and he dresses in Prikizan high fashion in place of the flowing silks of his homeland.8 He is affable and calculating, with an expert's understanding of manufacturing and scale.8

He has a hawkish nose and rich brown eyes.29, 35 After the attempt on his life he began wearing gold-wire spectacles with orange lenses and kept a Redarm guard with him at all times.29, 35 He moves easily between charm and menace, and he frames his methods in terms of the carrot and the stick, with promises as the reward and violence as the punishment.35

Gian's public account of his rise, delivered in a speech at the palace gala, runs as follows. Ten years earlier his brother was killed in a raid by the Requing Federation; Gian rallied the Prikizan soldiers docked in the city to crush the assault, then guided Burunt into the Empire, which gave the island the means to defeat the Draumer threat.24 Kyndel regards this account as a lie.24

When Gian stormed the Heim estate, Otisen wounded him in the shoulder with a crossbow bolt.27 A fuller history later came from his brother Heraldur, whose real name is Heydar Magnus. The brothers had once worked together for a free Burunt and built the Obelisk together. When Heraldur tried to destroy it, Gian chained him, tortured him with the machine and cut his face. He then sold the island to the Empire and kept his brother as a source of cyrusite, while the official story held that Heydar Magnus had died fighting the Requing.33

Amara knew the Requing incursion to be a fiction that Gian had used to destroy his rivals before signing the island over to the Empire.44 Clodagh identified him as the central figure in the persecution of the Draumer, observing that Prikaz had shown no particular hatred of them before its alliance with him.34

Gian inspected Signarium Hall and rejected Jelert's rail proposal as too costly.8 He later federalized the city's banking and recalled the debts of the nobility,21 and at his gala he unveiled the railcaster and credited Blazej Rodion with its invention.25 When Kyndel attacked him in Master Lazaro's office, Gian threw Lazaro into the path of the blade and fled.26

Gian kept overdrawn Draumer enslaved as his Redarms by means of rune-etched collars, an arrangement the Empress knew about.28 After Amara identified Kyndel, he kept her Founder's ring and hired her to move cyrusite in secret.29 He appointed Jelert Master Engineer, had Blazej killed for lying, and bombed Signarium Hall to silence the engineers who protested his weapons, blaming the bombing on the Alshien.35 He showed Jelert raw cyrusite from a source outside the Empire,35 and he caught Jelert after the railcaster factory was destroyed.40

At the House Khar gala Gian revealed his Warriors, giant armored constructs, and declared that Burunt would submit to neither the Empire nor the Requing.44 Forewarned of the Alshien plan by his double agent Farzin, he had Amara charged with treason and House Khar condemned.44, 45 His forces fought loyal Prikizan troops through the night until his own Warriors went berserk, and he was last seen fleeing from them.45, 48

Kyndel, Jelert, Dusan and Otisen found Gian in the cavern beneath the palace, filthy and frantic, trying to make the Obelisk work.50 He maintained that Lazaro's designs should have functioned and claimed that the Redarms would die if he did.50 He agreed to a truce and worked alongside Jelert, but once the Obelisk was running he clubbed Jelert and shot a Redarm who had turned against him. Jelert then shot Gian beneath the collarbone, and Gian bled to death at the foot of the Obelisk. To the end he claimed that the Warriors had been intended to protect Burunt.53

title: Heraldur
blurb: Heraldur is the leader of a powerful crew in the Warrens of Burunt.

quote.text: That might be the dumbest idea I’ve heard all year,

rows: Draumer with an affinity for jade14; signaric engineer14
Mentioned in Chapter 1; appears in Chapter 5
Deceased; found dead outside Mintika Point47

lead:
Heraldur leads a powerful crew in the Warrens of Burunt; by the time the story begins, his organization has absorbed the district's rival fences.1

He is the most feared of the Warrens Barons, a one-eyed gang leader who carries a heavy jade cane.5 He forces Kyndel Heim into service as a thief and spy and later becomes his teacher.5, 14

sections.html:
Heraldur has a gaunt face marked on its right side by a web of old scars, and slicked-back black hair that is graying at the temples. He wears an intricate leather eyepatch over his right eye and owns several such patches.5, 9 He dresses in the imperial style, in black slacks and a gold-trimmed waistcoat.5 His usual manner is calm and cold, interrupted by sudden outbursts of extreme violence after which he returns at once to composure.5

Beneath the patch is a glowing eye of pale honey color.14 He addresses Kyndel dismissively as a boy, and the explosive temper he normally conceals emerges during their lessons.16 He holds that giving power to others only arms them against oneself.16

Heraldur has been a Draumer all his life and forges jade.14 He can move with inhuman speed,14 reshape a construct after forging it (his jade club flows into a sword and back), and sense when another Draumer draws on a tether.19 He is also a self-taught signaric engineer with a hidden workshop beneath the Warrens.14, 33

He is overdrawn in one eye only, a consequence of the Obelisk having been used on him.33

Heraldur is Heydar Magnus, the brother of Gian Magnus.33 The brothers once worked toward a free Burunt. Heraldur taught himself Signarium so that his devices could be built in Gian's factories, and together they constructed the Obelisk, intended to let a Draumer produce cyrusite willingly.16, 33 In practice the machine tore power out by force.33 When Heraldur attempted to destroy it, Gian chained him, tortured him with it and cut his face.16, 33 Heraldur killed the four soldiers sent to move him and escaped, while Gian announced that Heydar Magnus had died fighting the Requing.33 After two further attempts on Gian's life failed, Heraldur spent five years building up his power in the Warrens.33

Heraldur killed Luca, ordered the death of Baron Taher, and conscripted Kyndel after recognizing him as Enir's son.5 He sent Kyndel to steal rune-covered artifacts and knowingly accepted a forged copy of the hexagonal plate.9, 10, 14 After saving Kyndel from a Redarm, he revealed that he was a Draumer and agreed to train him in exchange for the location of the Draumer camps.14 He told Kyndel that the stolen runes were meant for a signaric vambrace to protect them both from the Obelisk.19

When Kyndel brought him the torc from the palace, Heraldur disclosed his past and his plan: destroy the Obelisk, free the Draumer, hold the Warrens and then storm the palace. He reluctantly agreed to give the Redarms a single chance at freedom.33 He rejected the Alshien aim of dispersing freed Draumer, preferring to keep them united as a fighting force.41 On the night of the Khar gala he wore his vambrace into the Draumer prison and freed about two dozen prisoners, and he blamed Kyndel when it emerged that the Obelisk had been moved.43

When Liena attacked as a Warrior, Heraldur abandoned Kyndel to fight her alone, remarking that he disliked losing a good tool.47 Kyndel later found him dead against a building outside Mintika Point, with a wound beneath his ribs and two Warriors he had killed lying nearby. His eyes had turned brown.47 Kyndel took his broken vambrace.47

Kyndel later remembered him as paranoid, brilliant and bitter, a man who trusted nobody and died with nobody beside him.49 The vambrace, repaired by Jelert, allowed Kyndel to power the Obelisk safely.50, 52

title: Liena
blurb: Liena is a Draumer from Kyndel Heim's past whose obsidian flower he carries everywhere.

quote.text: You don’t get to give up.

rows: Mentioned in Chapter 4; appears in Chapter 14

lead: Liena is known at first only through an obsidian flower that Kyndel Heim carries, his last remaining connection to her and to anyone at all.4 The flower hums with a familiar signature that steadies him.4, 9

sections.html: Liena has short black hair, delicate features, high cheekbones and large almond-shaped eyes. Her eyes were once a warm earthen brown and now glow with a honey-colored light, and her face has grown older and sharper.26

Liena was a Draumer child imprisoned in the camps alongside Kyndel, who insists that they were only close friends and still children at the time.14 She gave him the flower and kept him alive, refusing to let him give up.14, 19 Kyndel believed that she had died overdrawn after a final session at the Obelisk.14, 16

In fact she had been taken from the cells and made one of Gian's Redarms, overdrawn Draumer bound by lethal collars.26, 28

A Redarm attacked Kyndel in an alley, stopped when it saw the flower, asked him who he was and fled with it.14 At the palace, the shorter of the two Redarms guarding Master Lazaro's office ordered her partner Latif to take Kyndel alive. When Latif tried to execute him instead, she killed Latif with an obsidian blade and removed her helmet, revealing herself as Liena.26 She then carried the overdrawn Kyndel away.26

She brought him to Jelert Egarro's door and explained to Jelert what the Redarms and their collars were. Before returning to Gian's service she left Kyndel a new obsidian flower and a warning to leave Burunt.28

Other Redarms later told Kyndel that Liena had been due to be spared but had broken ranks to help him and was taken as a result.43 Gian made her into a Warrior: her limbs were cut away and her torso fused into a steel frame controlled by a bronze torc.47 The torc drove her mad whenever she forged, and in that state she killed two Redarms. After Kyndel broke the torc she recognized him and told him that he had allowed her to die as herself instead of as a monster. She died as her eyes faded back to brown.47

title: Dusan
blurb: Dusan is a lieutenant of the Iron Spears brigade and Jelert Egarro's friend.

quote.text: This island? It’s not what it seems,

lead: Lieutenant Dusan commands the soldiers of the Iron Spears brigade aboard the troop ship that carries Jelert Egarro to Burunt.2 He is young for his rank, dryly humorous and paternal toward his men.2

sections.html:
A career soldier, Dusan considers weapons a necessary deterrent, yet he responds sympathetically when Jelert admits that he refuses to make them.2 He is frank, compassionate and fond of teasing.2

He is tall, broad and massively built,7, 20 and he jokes that he cannot trust a man who will not have a drink.20

Dusan organized a celebration aboard the ship to ease tension between his soldiers and the sailors, and told Jelert that the men had nicknamed him Major Meddle. When Alshien raiders attacked, he pushed Jelert into cover and led the charge that drove them off.2 In Burunt he helped unload Amara Khar's ship and advised Jelert to wait before calling on her.7, 8

Dusan's unit hunted the Alshien leader Farzin, who always seemed to anticipate their traps, and found the local soldiers uncooperative.12, 20 He warned Jelert that the island was not what it appeared to be.12 The friendship cooled after Jelert, under Blazej's influence, told him that his work mattered more than Dusan did; Dusan began addressing him coldly by his rank. At the gala he suggested that Blazej was using Jelert, and the two parted on bad terms once more.20, 22

Jelert later sought permission to bring Dusan into the conspiracy against Gian.38 On the night of the uprising the Iron Spears dug in and held the last barracks still standing,45 and Dusan joined Amara's council, where he reported how the Warriors chose their targets and supported her move to the Warrens.48

He volunteered for the mission to the palace,49 killed a Warrior with a kinetic pulse from his signaric spear,50 and helped defend the Obelisk while it was being readied.50, 52 He survived and carried the unconscious crystal-forging Redarm out of the collapsing palace.53 He does not appear in the epilogue.55

title: Otisen
blurb: Otisen is a weathered Burition fighter who comes to House Khar on behalf of unnamed buyers.

quote.text: ‘Rebel’ is a strange label for a person defending their home

rows: House guard of the Heim estate27
A sister in the countryside; a cousin27

lead: Otisen is an Alshien operative who approaches Amara Khar to buy supplies.11 In appearance and smell he resembles a caravan guard.11

sections.html: Otisen is a sturdy islander with a thick, unkempt beard and mustache, a faint scar across his forehead and dark, exhausted eyes. He wears well-worn leathers patched with great care and carries a sword at his hip.11

Otisen was a house guard on the Heim estate when Gian stormed it. He saw Gian cut Mistress Heim's throat in front of her son, wounded Gian in the shoulder with a crossbow bolt, and fled with the boy, Kyndel, at Master Heim's pleading.27 He hid Kyndel with his sister in the countryside until his own cousin sold the child to Prikizan soldiers. To protect his family Otisen did nothing to stop the sale, and he left that same night to join the rebellion.27

Otisen negotiated a contract with Amara for regular deliveries, and she deduced that he was Alshien.11 He was later detained at the southeast gate with twelve others while moving them to a safe house; according to the Alshien leader Clodagh, he mattered more to the movement than he let on.17

Serving as Amara's bodyguard at the Viceroy's gala, he told her his history on the ride home and added that he had seen a young man who looked as Kyndel might look grown up.27 When Amara later told him that Khorshed Kazemi was Kyndel, he went pale and was sent to find him.34

During Gian's coup Otisen killed the Redarm about to execute Amara, broke her stone manacles, and told her that with the Alshien leaders dead or missing she was now the movement's hope.46

Kyndel recognized him at Amara's command post and cut short his apology, asking him to help instead. Otisen swore his life to Kyndel by the Eldtree and by the graves of Kyndel's parents.49 He fought Warriors beside Kyndel beneath the palace, saved his life, and carried him out as the palace collapsed.52, 53 Three months later he is with Kyndel in the Warrens, where he tells him that living in a world without Gian will be a far greater revenge.55

title: Clodagh
blurb: Clodagh is a blunt, older Burition woman who bursts into House Khar demanding help for her people.

quote.text: Name’s Clodagh, and I’m no lady. I work for a living.

rows: Alshien (leader of its largest group)1734
Deceased; killed at the House Khar gala44

lead: Clodagh is a leader of the Alshien, the Burition rebels who oppose the Viceroy and the Empire.17 She becomes Amara Khar's partner and eventually her friend.17, 34

sections.html: Clodagh is several decades older than Amara, with dark brown hair heavily streaked with gray, a deeply lined face and the sinewy build of a laborer. She wears trousers, a loose shirt and a short jacket, with a long knife at her hip.17 She is headstrong and gruff, addresses Amara as girl, and distrusts both nobles and Prikizans.17, 34, 38

Clodagh forced her way into Amara's office to demand help after Otisen and twelve Alshien were detained at the southeast gate.17 She explained that many Alshien are parents of children who had woken with Draumer abilities, which she described as a curse.17 Amara agreed to help only after Clodagh signed a confession as leader of the Alshien to serve as insurance.17 The confrontation ended in wary mutual respect, with Amara conceding that she might need to reconsider her view of the Draumer.17

After Amara joined the rebellion, Clodagh went through House Khar's books, insisted that Amara treat the rebellion as theirs jointly, and briefed her on Alshien strength: just over a thousand fighters in Clodagh's own group and perhaps five hundred more following Farzin.34 Her group had rescued dozens of Draumer children from Gian.34 She agreed to Amara's plan to kill Gian at a revived House Khar gala.34 At first she refused to trust Jelert Egarro, whom she dismissed as an imperial dog, but she accepted him after hearing his story.34, 38

Clodagh wore formal silks to the gala.42 When Gian revealed his Warriors and the plot collapsed, she charged him out of a smoke screen and was killed by a Warrior's blow to the chest.44

Her full name, Clodagh Askar, is carved on the memorial to the Remembered of Crownfall, where Amara grieves for her.55

title: Balfourd
blurb: Balfourd is the long-serving majordomo of House Khar.

quote.text: Perhaps you would like to remove the ink from your face first?

lead: Balfourd is the majordomo of House Khar and Amara Khar's right hand.3 He has remained loyal to the house throughout its decline.3

sections.html:
Balfourd is a thin, older Burition, older than Amara's father would have been. He has dark skin and eyes, white hair combed back behind his ears, an immaculate beard that hides his thin neck, and a nearly expressionless face.3 He is exceptionally patient, and he carries a leather folder and a graphite stylus.3

His reedy voice made him, in Amara's memory of her childhood, a poor storyteller.6 He is stoic with a dry wit, and he makes the household's coffee from over-roasted beans.11

Balfourd attends Amara in the marketplace and briefs her on the household's troubles: an overgrown bougainvillea, a leaking fountain, a delayed cargo and a cook who has quit.3

He investigated the theft of the Founder's ring and researched Brothers Incorporated,6 and he went with Amara to the harbor dockhouse when her smuggled cargo was threatened.7 He placed himself between Amara and Otisen at their first meeting11 and rode to the southeast gate with Amara's letter to free the detained Alshien.17 At the Viceroy's gala he watched over Dhonya Khar.21 On Amara's instructions he answered Jelert Egarro's letters with vague replies that she dictated.23

After the Viceroy's gala he took Dhonya home while Amara stayed behind to look for business.27 Once Amara joined the Alshien, he worked with Clodagh on the house's books and formed a rapport with Otisen, a fellow trusted deputy.34 He took Dhonya's side when Amara lashed out at her,34 and he kept close watch on Amara throughout the Khar gala.42 When Gian's forces seized the estate, he was dragged from the kitchens bleeding from a head wound.44

Balfourd survived. Three months later, dressed in gray robes, he serves Queen Amara as her dependable majordomo.55

title: Dhonya Khar
blurb: Lady Dhonya Khar is Amara Khar's mother and the former matriarch of House Khar.

quote.text: Even broken things can last if you’re stubborn enough to keep patching the cracks.

rows: Mentioned in Chapter 3; appears in Chapter 6

lead: Lady Dhonya Khar is the mother of Amara Khar. After her husband's death she held House Khar together for years until she was overtaken by a worse illness of her own.3 She loves the estate's garden.3

sections.html: Dhonya has hazel eyes and thin, waxy skin.6 Her memory is failing, and she often lives in the past: she plans the house's annual gala, speaks of her husband as if he were alive, appeals to the Council of Lords and forgets that Burunt is ruled by the Empire.6 She frequently takes her husband's Founder's ring and then misplaces it.6 In her prime she dominated the island's social circles through intelligence and determination, and her name was spoken with respect and at times with fear.13, 21

Dhonya raised House Khar to prominence after her husband died.13 Her illness began when Amara was thirteen. Amara blames her for squandering the house's wealth on failed ventures and unreliable allies.34

Dhonya later admitted that she had lived for her husband's memory and lost her own sense of self after his death.46

Dhonya attended the Viceroy's gala in white and silver, her former vigor briefly restored.21 When she demanded the Founder's ring for a charity ball, Amara snapped at her, and Dhonya apologized in a moment of clarity.34 During a rare lucid spell she advised Amara that leadership means holding things together with one's bare hands and that strength has nothing to do with wearing a crown.36

On the night of the Khar gala she told Amara she was proud of her, made clear that she knew more than a party was under way, and went to hide in the kitchens.42 When Gian's men seized the estate she was knocked to the floor and struck her head.44 The Alshien carried her to a townhome, where she told Amara that legacies belong on tombstones and urged her to live for those still alive. She died soon after.46

Her name is carved on the memorial to the Remembered of Crownfall in the form Dhonya Khar’Andor.55

title: Blazej Rodion
blurb: Blazej Rodion is a Prikizan engineer at Signarium Hall who befriends Jelert Egarro.

quote.text: Word to the wise: the competition here is cutthroat.

rows: Signaric engineer at Signarium Hall8
His father is a railway engineer in Prikaz15

lead: Blazej Rodion is an engineer at Signarium Hall who graduated from the Petrovskaya Academy a few years ahead of Jelert Egarro.8 He warns Jelert that the laboratory is ruthlessly competitive and proposes an alliance.8

sections.html: Blazej is slender and gaunt, with pale eyes and short, stylish dirty-blond hair, and he wears an engineer's apron and gloves.8 He suffers from seasickness, swears by the Goddess's blood and the Hallowed Halls,15 and does not drink at taverns.20 He is jovial and admiring toward Jelert, although his eyes lit up at the destructive force of their prototype.18

Blazej helped Jelert when the other engineers shunned him, learned of Jelert's new rune, and suggested a stabilizing matrix for the rail design.15 He insisted on building a working prototype and warned Jelert to be careful of Dusan, arguing that outsiders resent the work of engineers.18 He took charge of coordinating with the Viceroy's private engineers while Jelert worked on ways to reduce the cost of a causeway to the mainland.20 Dusan suspected that Blazej was isolating Jelert from his friends in order to use him.22 At the Viceroy's gala Blazej tried to draw Jelert away from Amara Khar, insulting her as a tart, and Amara accused him of leaning on Jelert's work.23

Gian then introduced Blazej as the engineer behind the railcaster, a weapon built from Jelert's runes, and hailed him as the father of Burition signarium.25 Blazej later claimed that he had acted for both of them, but let slip that he had gone to Gian on inspection day. That visit had sunk Jelert's rail project, and Jelert punched him.31

When Jelert told Gian the truth about the railcaster's origin, Gian replied that his men had caught Blazej leaving the city and that he could not tolerate liars within his walls, implying that Blazej was dead.35 Jelert later stated outright that Gian had had him killed.38

title: Lazaro
blurb: Master Lazaro is the head engineer of Signarium Hall in the Viceroy's palace.

quote.text: It’s inspection day, and I will not have your station in disarray while the Viceroy is present.

rows: Master Engineer, head of Signarium Hall8

lead: Master Lazaro is the head engineer of Signarium Hall, the palace laboratory in which Jelert Egarro works.8

sections.html: Lazaro is hunched and weathered, roughly the Viceroy's age, with bad knees, a cane and a harsh, grating voice.8, 26 He guards the Viceroy's time jealously and encourages cutthroat competition and favoritism among his engineers.8, 12, 15 His office lies at the end of the east wing on the third floor, behind a door marked with silver sigils. It is cluttered with parchment, half-eaten meals and strange devices and lit by lanterns that sense movement.26

On inspection day Lazaro reprimanded Jelert, steered the Viceroy away from his station, and dismissed his rail proposal as unrealistic given Burunt's limited supply of cyrusite, adding with a glare that he too would be watching Jelert's progress.8 Jelert soon concluded that he had made a very poor impression on Lazaro, and his requisitions for basic supplies were denied.15 Lazaro presided over the presentation days at which engineers demonstrated their work to the Viceroy.15, 18 He kept a rune-etched torc in his office, and Kyndel Heim stole it during the Viceroy's gala.24, 26 When Lazaro arrived with Gian, Kyndel charged the Viceroy, and Gian threw Lazaro into the path of the dagger, which struck him between the ribs.26

Lazaro died of the wound.29, 30 Gian told Amara that the assassin had murdered his head engineer.29 The engineers were given a few days' leave after the death, allowing Jelert to keep the wounded Kyndel hidden; Kyndel maintained that Gian had used Lazaro as a shield.30

Lazaro had been building the torc as a prototype, and when Jelert asked for the head engineer's post, Gian made its completion his test.31 As Master Engineer, Jelert inherited Lazaro's notes and materials.37 Lazaro had also helped Gian develop the railcasters and had begun building the equipment to produce them.35, 38 Jelert's completion of the torc made Gian's Warriors possible.45 Gian later insisted that Lazaro's designs and prototype ought to have worked.50

title: Farzin
blurb: Farzin is a Burition figure tied to the Alshien rebellion.

rows: Alshien12; secretly Gian Magnus45
Mentioned in Chapter 12; appears in Chapter 45

lead: Farzin is described as an Alshien leader who led the raid on the ship carrying Jelert Egarro and Dusan to Burunt.12

sections.html:
Dusan's Iron Spears hunted Farzin for months, and he consistently seemed to anticipate their traps.12

Clodagh told Amara that most Alshien factions outside her own looked to Farzin for leadership. She disapproved of his raids, which caused heavier losses on both sides.34

On the night of the House Khar gala, Farzin reported to Gian in his carriage as Captain Farzin, wearing the yellow armband of Gian's loyalists. He had been Gian's agent from the start.45 The Alshien learned that he had been seen leaving House Khar with Gian's men after betraying their plans and targets to the Viceroy.46 His subsequent fate is not stated.46

title: Khamron
blurb: Khamron is a bald, heavily built enforcer in Heraldur's Warrens crew.
lead: Khamron is the principal enforcer of Heraldur's crew in the Warrens. He is bald and barrel-chested, with very thick, muscular arms.4, 5 He holds Kyndel responsible for the failure of a smuggling operation and insults him for it.5

sections.html:
Khamron was in charge of a crew unloading smuggled signaric devices when Kyndel, pursued by a Redarm, ran through their operation. The cargo exploded, and Khamron seized the stunned Kyndel and brought him before Heraldur.4, 5 Heraldur then dispatched Khamron with three dozen men and rune charges to kill Baron Taher and to burn the inn belonging to Luca.5 Khamron later served as a guard at Heraldur's stronghold, where he acknowledged Kyndel with a brief nod of respect.10

After Kyndel overdrew, he returned to the hideout with glowing eyes and was met with hostility; Khamron recognized him and halted the fighting.32 Khamron took part in Heraldur's planning meeting for the raid on the Draumer camps41 and joined the raid itself. There he tried and failed to force the door of the Obelisk chamber with his shoulder, then made way for Kyndel.43

title: Lefty
blurb: Lefty is a large fence in the Warrens who buys stolen goods from Kyndel Heim.

quote.text: I’ll get you eventually, Lordling.

lead:
Lefty is a fence and forger who operates from a basement in the Warrens cluttered with books, gadgets and disassembled signaric lamps.1 He is enormous, standing two heads taller than Kyndel and several times broader, with heavy, sagging features, a rough voice and a left eye that is clouding over.1

His dealings with Kyndel combine hostility and familiarity. He habitually attacks Kyndel with a pair of rusted shears on arrival, addresses him by the mocking nickname Lordling, and pays for his goods in imperial silvers.1 When Kyndel raises the possibility of buying forged papers to enter noble society, Lefty tells him that he would need a far larger sum and a convincing family history.1

sections.html:
Although Lefty presented himself as independent of the Warrens gangs, Heraldur informed Kyndel that the fence was in fact one of his own people.5

By the time of the raid on the Draumer camps, Lefty had become Heraldur's quartermaster, and one of his eyes had turned entirely white. He and Kyndel recalled their earlier dealings, and Lefty joked that he was to blame for Kyndel joining Heraldur's crew. He was aware of Liena and teasingly described her as a Redarm in love with Kyndel.41

title: Latif
blurb: Latif is one of the armored Redarms in the Viceroy's service.

rows: Draumer; forges deep gray stone26

lead: Latif is a Redarm who, together with a second Redarm, guards the office of Master Lazaro at the time of Kyndel Heim's attack on Gian.26

sections.html:
During the fight, Kyndel severed the strap of Latif's helmet, exposing a powerfully built Burition with a broad nose, jet-black hair and pale, honey-colored eyes. Latif is a Draumer whose forging produces large axes of gray stone.26 Kyndel considered him a match for Heraldur in skill. Latif dissolved his axe head and re-formed it around Kyndel's spear, then took off Kyndel's left arm with it.26 Although the Redarms had been ordered to capture Kyndel alive, Latif declared that death was preferable to Kyndel joining their ranks and prepared to kill him. The second Redarm, Liena, killed Latif first by driving an obsidian blade through his throat.26

Liena subsequently admitted to Jelert that she had killed a fellow Redarm in order to save Kyndel.28

title: Isadore Meyers
blurb: Isadore Meyers is a banker with Brothers Incorporated who manages House Khar's accounts.

rows: Mentioned in Chapter 6; appears in Chapter 21

lead: Isadore Meyers is a banker named as the point of contact in a letter notifying Amara Khar that her accounts have been moved to Brothers Incorporated. The firm is a growing local bank with a reputation as a trader in debt.6

sections.html:
Isadore is an elderly, thin man with a tidy mustache and silver-rimmed spectacles who wears a gray waistcoat and speaks in a high, thin voice. He is nervous by temperament and admits that delivering bad news distresses him.21 At the Viceroy's gala he informed Amara that the Viceroy, acting under the newly federalized banking system, had called in House Khar's debts. Ten percent of the total was due within a month, and the remainder was subject to a three-month grace period.21

At the House Khar gala, Isadore formally read the treason charges against Amara and announced the dissolution of her house.44 Afterward he rode in Gian's carriage. When Jelert appealed to him for help, he declined, claiming that he paid attention only to what he was supposed to hear. An explosion then overturned the carriage, and Isadore was killed by a rock that came through the window.45

title: Yasser Turan
blurb: Lord Yasser Turan is an older, irreverent noble of Burunt.
lead: Lord Yasser Turan is a nobleman of Burunt. At the Viceroy's gala he signed a preliminary contract with Amara Khar, which was drafted on the back of a server for lack of a table.21

sections.html:
Yasser is an older man whose skin is light for a Burition. His black hair is streaked with gray, and he wears full mutton chops joined to his mustache while keeping his chin clean-shaven.24 He is blunt, irreverent and given to practical jokes; Amara regards him as a decent and honest man.24 He had been a longtime friend of Kyndel's father and spent many hours debating questions of leadership at the Heim family hearth, but he failed to recognize Kyndel as an adult. At the gala he openly offered his assistance to Kyndel in the guise of Khorshed Kazemi before departing to tease Ziba.24

When Amara was arrested at her own gala, Yasser turned his eyes away.44 After Crownfall, he presided over the unanimous vote of the surviving nobles to make Amara Queen, commending the decisiveness and boldness of her leadership, and he signaled the start of her address.55

title: Enir
blurb: Enir is the father of Kyndel Heim.

rows: Guild Master Heim; Master Heim27
Kyndel Heim (son)5; Mistress Heim (wife)27

lead: Enir is the father of Kyndel Heim. He was a guild master and a prominent Draumer, well enough known that Heraldur identifies Kyndel as his son on sight.5

sections.html: In Kyndel's memories Enir is a mason, his hands marked with fresh mortar9, who ran a masonry workshop where Kyndel saw a mason's hammer.14, 32 Lord Yasser Turan was his friend, although the two were never firm political allies, and they spent long evenings at the hearth debating leadership.24 Known formally as Guild Master Heim, Enir wielded considerable influence among the craftsmen and Draumer of the city, even though the Heims were not a noble house.27

Enir was killed when Gian Magnus seized power. Kyndel's memory of the event is of his father dying as he reached toward him.5 According to the house guard Otisen, Master Heim was bound and forced to his knees, and in his last moments he pleaded with the guards to take his son and flee.27 Kyndel later explained that neither of his parents has a grave, since their bodies were consumed when the family house burned.49

title: Luca
blurb: Luca is the son of a Warrens Baron and the keeper of an inn in the Warrens.
lead: Luca is a young, muscular man, the son of the Warrens Baron Taher. He runs a tavern and had arranged to buy goods from a shipment belonging to Heraldur.5

sections.html:
When the shipment was delayed, Luca forced his way into Heraldur's cellar, demanded his goods and told Heraldur to give up his position. Heraldur feigned agreement and then killed him with a blow of his jade cane that crushed his skull, with Kyndel looking on.5 Heraldur afterward ordered that Luca's inn be burned, with care taken that the fire did not spread.5

The killing stayed with Kyndel. He recalled it when he broke a chair apart in the palace26, and during his overdraw fever he had a vision of Luca's blood pooling on the floor while he himself stood over the corpse holding an iron cane.30

title: Taher
blurb: Baron Taher is one of the Warrens Barons who control the gangs of the Warrens.
lead: Baron Taher is one of the Warrens Barons and the father of Luca.5 He is only mentioned and never appears in person. After killing Luca, Heraldur sent Khamron with three dozen men and rune charges to kill Taher, along with any potential successor who might try to take over his position.5 The novel neither depicts the attack nor confirms whether Taher died.5

title: Mirek
blurb: Mirek is a private of the Iron Spears aboard Jelert Egarro's troop ship.
lead: Private Mirek is a soldier of the Iron Spears, a very large man with a closely shaved scalp.2 After Jelert repairs the troop ship's stove, Mirek asks him to mend his damaged signaric spear, explaining that he does not want to reach Burunt with poorly maintained gear. Jelert turns him down.2

sections.html: Mirek died during the attack on the ship by Alshien raiders. Jelert discovered the body lying on its side with the unrepaired spear still in its grip, and was overcome with guilt over his refusal.2

title: Naveed
blurb: Master Naveed is a merchant whom Amara Khar outmaneuvers in a Burunt marketplace.
lead: Master Naveed is a heavyset merchant with pale cheeks who held a verbal agreement to purchase goods from an elderly stall-keeper.3 The harbor master detained his cargo, citing a clerical mistake, and in the meantime Amara Khar concluded a written contract for the same goods. Because verbal agreements carry no legal force in Burunt, the shipment went to her.3 Naveed accused Amara of wrongdoing and was hurling insults at her as she departed.3

sections.html: Otisen later disclosed that the goods had been intended for the Alshien and that Naveed had been supplying them without inquiring into their purpose.11

title: Riocard
blurb: Riocard is the dockmaster of Burunt's harbor.
lead: Dockmaster Riocard is a stout Burition who wears a loose robe and oversees the harbor from the dockhouse. Amara Khar suspects him of accepting bribes.7 When Amara pushed into his office to complain about the delay to her ship, the Alisma, Riocard told her that an imperial vessel transporting a senior officer and a prisoner had been given precedence. The Alisma had been moored alongside it, which prevented even its own crew from unloading the cargo.7 Half of Riocard's workers were occupied attending to the Prikizans.7 Lieutenant Dusan later gave him a list of the supplies the raiders had stolen.7

title: Sireen
blurb: Sireen is a maid in the household of House Khar.

rows: Mentioned in Chapter 3; appears in Chapter 6

lead:
Sireen is one of the small number of servants still employed by House Khar. Amara intends to have her make up a bed in the servants' quarters for a new cook.3

Sireen is a few years older than Amara, round-cheeked and soft-spoken, and becomes flustered easily.6 She attends to Lady Dhonya Khar, steering her gently back whenever her attention wanders6, and through careful mending keeps Amara's outdated wardrobe in spotless condition.7 She does not appear or receive mention after Chapter 7.7

title: Ziba
blurb: Ziba is a guest at the Viceroy's gala mentioned by Lord Yasser Turan.
lead: Ziba is mentioned by name only once. While at the Viceroy's gala, Lord Yasser Turan excuses himself from a conversation by announcing that he intends to provoke Ziba until she flushes red and throws her wine at him. He then walks over to a Prikizan woman, who frowns at his approach.24 The text does not establish whether this woman is Ziba, nor what connection she has to Yasser.24

title: The Empress
blurb: The Empress is the ruler of the Prikaz Empire.

rows: Alive; has not answered Burunt55

lead: The Empress is the sovereign of the Prikaz Empire. She is unnamed and does not appear directly in the novel. Jelert Egarro was in her employ before his posting to Burunt.8

sections.html:
Jelert served the Empress for several years.13 Discovering a new rune is a path to her favor: the most recent person to do so was appointed to her personal advisory board.15 Jelert refers to her policy opposing the development of signaric weapons in the territories.18

The Empress adapted Jelert's runeforge capacitor for military use and employed it to suppress the uprising at Yeshall.28, 31 Liena believed that the enslavement of the Redarms formed part of an arrangement between the Empress and Gian, although the Empress was probably unaware of the railcasters.28 Gian was careful to keep his weapons and his cyrusite concealed from anyone who might report back to her.29, 35

After Crownfall, Queen Amara sent the Empress a request to parley, which went entirely unanswered, with neither a reply nor a military response. Reports at the time described rising political and religious unrest within the Empire.55

title: Valenska
blurb: Valenska is the Earth Mother, the goddess of the Prikaz Empire.
lead: Valenska, also known as the Earth Mother, is the goddess worshipped in the Prikaz Empire. Prikizans consider cyrusite, which was thought to occur only beneath the imperial capital, to be her blood and a gift from her, and they believe it confers a mandate to raise up other civilizations.13

sections.html: Jelert Egarro prays to Valenska for good fortune and uses the Goddess in his oaths.18 He later contended that the discovery of a source of cyrusite outside the Empire would undermine belief in Valenska, on which imperial authority rests.38 When Kyndel revealed that the Obelisk converts Draumer power into cyrusite, Prikizan officers denounced the claim as blasphemy against the gifts of the goddess.49

title: Minor characters
blurb: A list of the minor named and unnamed characters of Crownfall, with a short note on each.
lead: This page lists characters of Crownfall who appear only briefly or are only mentioned. Characters with their own articles are listed on the Characters index. Unnamed figures are listed by description, and entries are grouped loosely by where the characters appear.

sections.html:
• Amara's father: The late head of House Khar, a warm-hearted man of firm principles who earned the loyalty of others and died of illness. The Founder's ring was the possession he valued most.3, 6 Amara was nine years old when he died.13
  • Mistress Heim: Kyndel's mother, who kept a library, wore a red shawl with tassels, and was killed by Gian Magnus.1, 5, 9 Otisen witnessed Gian cut her throat.27
