  • Jelert's father: A member of the Egarro military family who took pride in his son's talent for signarium but looks down on his assignment to Burunt.13
  • Otisen's sister and cousin: The sister hid the young Kyndel in the countryside; the cousin later turned him over to Prikizan soldiers to collect the bounty.27
  • Heydar Magnus: The true name of Heraldur. Gian had publicly announced that he died in battle against the Requing.33

• Lady Ebelin: A woman whom Dhonya Khar mentions with contempt, pointedly questioning her right to the title of lady. Dhonya says that her late husband's ring serves as a necessary reminder to Ebelin. Her identity is never explained.6
  • Khorshed Kazemi: The assumed identity under which Kyndel moves among the nobility: nephew and presumed heir of the childless Lord Kazemi of a remote island estate, with a father who operates a logging business.9 At the Viceroy's gala he claims to come from a farming island in the west.24
  • Lord Kazemi: Head of House Kazemi, a Founding House that has long been absent from Burunt, and the uncle named in Kyndel's cover story. The book does not state whether he actually exists.9
  • Lord Stilton: An elderly lord who holds a party at his white brick manse, where the hexagonal plate is displayed among his collection of signaric artifacts.9 During the theft of the plate he shot at Kyndel with a rare Requing musket.10
  • Lord Modir: A noble who hosts a gala occupying the whole second floor of his manse.37
  • Lady Teymoor: A noble said by rumor to have been involved in a mishap with a plate of custard at a previous gala.37
  • The Khar cook: The former cook of House Khar, who left to work for the family of a Prikizan military captain.3
  • The drunk noblewoman: A guest at Lord Modir's gala who congratulates Jelert on the railcasters, misnaming them.37

• The elderly stall-keeper: The merchant from whom Amara buys the goods promised to Master Naveed.3
  • The ship's captain: Commander of the troop ship carrying Jelert to Burunt. He has casks opened for a celebration and refuses to pursue the raiders into shallow water.2
  • The ship's cook: A cook on the troop ship who served Jelert custard.2
  • The Alshien prisoner: A raider captured alive in the attack on Jelert's ship.2 The imperial ship responsible for delaying Amara's cargo is transporting a prisoner.7

• Anard and Maju: Fences whose operations were taken over by Heraldur's crew shortly before the novel opens.1
  • The skinny smuggler: A member of Khamron's crew whose thrown signaric device triggers a series of explosions.4
  • The thug with slicked-back hair: One of Heraldur's men, who questions Khamron about the captive Kyndel.5
  • The bonesaw: A surgeon with unsteady hands who serves as the nearest equivalent to a doctor in the Warrens; he trimmed the stump of Kyndel's arm.41
  • The scarred man on the parapet: A guard at the Warrens gate from Heraldur's crew. He lets Amara through after she tells him that Heraldur is dead and that Kyndel Heim sent her.51
  • The Draumer girl: A girl of roughly eight to ten whom Kyndel watches forge a crowbar near the Warrens. Hers is the first tether he ever perceives.32

sections.h: The palace, the army and the Empire
sections.html:
• The young imperial soldier: A soldier of about Kyndel's age whom Kyndel catches kicking an elderly homeless woman in Mintika Point. Kyndel slashes his thigh and leaves him to bleed to death.1
  • The old homeless woman: The woman Kyndel rescues from the soldier. She runs away afterward.1
  • The Captain: The commanding officer of Dusan, who divides the Iron Spears into continuous shifts to pursue reported Alshien sightings.20
  • The captain at Yeshall: An acquaintance of Dusan who witnessed a new signaric explosive kill both rebels and civilians at Yeshall.12
  • The Burition maid: An older maid at the palace who dresses the wound on Kyndel's arm and points him toward Master Lazaro's office.26
  • The wounded servant: A Burition servant whose forearm is cut by shrapnel during the railcaster demonstration; the crowd takes no notice.25
  • Gian's advisors: Two aged Prikizan men in conference with Gian at the moment Jelert storms into his office.31
  • The factory foremen: A narrow-eyed foreman at the building presented as a factory, who claims it is an imperial storehouse, and a foreman on the railcaster assembly line who allows the workers a rest after one of them loses a hand.39, 40
  • The Prikizan soldiers: Three loyal soldiers who assist Jelert in assembling and setting off a bomb against four Warriors after Gian's carriage is overturned.45
  • The Prikizan brigade leader: An officer on Amara's council who reports that a militia is holding the Warriors out of the Warrens.48
  • The Prikizan merchants: Three merchants and factory owners who remain in Burunt and request cyrusite from Jelert for their own use.55

• The tall, thin Redarm: A lanky Redarm whose hands carry a lightning charge. It battles Kyndel across the rooftops until he kicks it off a roof.19
  • The bow-wielding Redarm: An older woman with gray in her short-cropped hair who forges a silvery-white metal and holds Kyndel responsible for what became of Liena. Liena, transformed into a Warrior, kills her.43, 47
  • The crystal-axe Redarm: A broad-shouldered older man who forges a crystalline axe and explains that the collars kill anyone who interferes with them. Liena tears his arms off.43, 47
  • Amara's captor: A stone-forging Redarm who takes hold of Amara at the gala and attempts to execute her in the street. Otisen kills him with a handaxe.44, 46
  • The stone Redarm: One of the two Redarms accompanying Gian beneath the palace. He forges a hammer and an axe of black stone, turns against Gian, and is shot dead.50, 53
  • The crystal Redarm: The second Redarm beneath the palace, a woman who fights with crystal swords. Dusan carries her out unconscious as the palace collapses.50, 53
  • The burly Redarm: The leader of the last nine free Redarms, who goes without a helmet and promises to aid Amara's people.51
  • The copper Redarm: A Redarm on the Warrens wall who forges copper. When the wave from the Obelisk hits, a Burition breaks his collar, and he recovers as a free man.54

• The burly man: One of Gian's men, who knocks Dhonya Khar to the floor at the gala.44
  • The townhome owner: A woman with two children who allows the resistance to use her house south of Mintika Point.46
  • The teen scout: A young scout who brings in the bound Jelert, believing him to be a Prikizan officer.46
  • The young Alshien: A rebel of around thirty who estimates that more than a hundred Warriors are at large in the city.48
  • The woman with the woodcutter's axe: A heavyset civilian who cracks a Warrior's torc during Amara's march to the Warrens.51
  • The Prikizan laborer: A laborer who dies on the Warrens wall.54

title: Draumer
blurb: People of Burunt born with the power to draw energy through a tether and forge objects out of gray mist.

quote.text: Unite and defend your home from Draumer counterfeits.

rows: Enhanced senses, speed, strength and balance; forging
Kyndel Heim, Heraldur, the Redarms

lead:
Draumer are people of Burunt who can draw power through an inner connection called a tether. The power heightens their senses and physical abilities and allows them to forge solid objects from a gray mist that forms in their hands.1 Kyndel Heim, one of the three point-of-view characters of Crownfall, is a Draumer.1

Draumer once moved freely through Burunt. Under Viceroy Gian Magnus and the Prikaz Empire they are persecuted: older propaganda posters denounced them as counterfeiters, newer ones offer rewards for information leading to a capture, and captured Draumer are sent to the Draumer labor camps.1

sections.html:
A Draumer activates the power by mentally pulling on the tether.1 The draw produces a sense of euphoria, brightens colors, sharpens the senses and grants increased speed, strength and balance. Kyndel uses it to evade a swing of Lefty's shears and to punch a stone wall.1 Drawn power also provides sight in the dark and allows Kyndel to drop a dozen feet from a wall without injury.4

Power held in the body is unstable. It presses to be either used or released, and the pressure grows the longer it is held.1 Releasing it sends the power back through the tether and leaves the Draumer with dulled perception and a sense of emptiness.1 Power held for too long is torn away all at once, leaving the Draumer abruptly weakened, so Kyndel learned to draw in short, repeated bursts.4

Under Heraldur's training, Kyndel learned to draw in advance of movement, and a full draw makes him noticeably faster and more fluid in combat.19

A Draumer can also direct the power outward. Gray mist gathers in the palm and solidifies into whatever object the Draumer pictures.1 Forged objects are brittle and release a burst of bright light when they break; Kyndel once shattered a dagger to blind an opponent.1 Such objects are called creations or constructs and are described in detail under Draumer creations.

According to Heraldur, forged material differs from material taken from the earth. Forged iron lacks the exact properties of natural iron and is about as durable as glass, and the quality of any construct depends on the creator's focus and will at the moment of forging.16 Strong constructs ordinarily require daily practice and meditation, but Heraldur also teaches forging in anger as a shortcut, since rage fixes the mind on a single thought.16 Kyndel's first lasting dagger was made this way, when he threw one in a moment of fury.14

Experienced Draumer can reshape a construct after forming it. Heraldur turned a jade club into a sword and back again while fighting Kyndel, and withheld instruction in the technique as a punishment.19

Each Draumer forges a single characteristic material. Kyndel's affinity is iron, although while he is unskilled his iron breaks as easily as glass.4

Other affinities revealed during the story include jade (Heraldur)14, obsidian (Liena, the only Draumer Kyndel has known with that affinity)26, and dark gray stone (Latif).26

Later chapters introduce Redarms whose affinities include a bright silvery-white metal and crystal43, iridescent stone46, black stone and crystal50, red stone, dull dark metal and brass51, and copper.54 A young Draumer girl in the streets near the Warrens forges a crowbar of black material.32

The principal cost of Draumer power is overdraw. Drawing too much causes sharp pain behind the eyes and at the base of the skull, narrowing of vision and a risk of collapse.4 In the camps Kyndel saw Draumer die after taking in more power than their bodies could survive.14

The story later introduces a second, permanent condition. A Draumer who draws to the absolute limit becomes overdrawn: the tether locks at full draw, and the Draumer either adapts to the change or dies.28 Overdrawn Draumer have glowing orange eyes and a constant draw that can be reduced but never stopped, along with lasting improvements to their senses, strength, speed and stamina.2832 Every Redarm is an overdrawn Draumer.28

Every creation emits a pulse that other Draumer can feel by touch, known as a haptic signature. Kyndel identifies a Founder's ring as a Draumer creation by the pulse it sends up his arm.4 Heraldur likewise identified Kyndel as a Draumer by touching an iron plate Kyndel had forged.14

Heraldur can also sense when another Draumer draws power.19 Overdrawn Draumer see tethers directly, as a cable of light rising from the back of the neck that brightens when its owner draws, and the Redarms use this brightening to track Draumer through the city.32 Heraldur also showed Kyndel the Eldtree, a network of vast tendrils of light rising across Burunt and converging above the palace, which he regards as the tether of the world itself. He does not know what it draws energy from or for what purpose.33

• Kyndel Heim.1 His affinity is iron, and he escaped from the Draumer labor camps.45
  • Enir, Kyndel's father, a guild master and well-known Draumer.5
  • Heraldur (jade), the Warrens Baron.14
  • Liena (obsidian), Kyndel's companion from the camps.1426
  • An old woman in the camps whose explosion allowed Kyndel to escape.14
  • Latif (stone), a Redarm.26
  • The Redarms as a whole.2628
  • An unnamed girl near the Warrens, about eight to ten years old.32
  • The Warriors, each built around a mutilated Draumer.4547

Imperial printing presses spread anti-Draumer propaganda throughout Burunt, and current posters offer rewards for information about Draumer.1 The Viceroy's Redarms hunt the Draumer still at large, and captured Draumer are forced to kneel before the Obelisk and surrender their power.4 In the early years of Gian's rule, his purges also rounded up prominent relatives of Draumer.5 The bounties are large enough that house guards hope to retire on a single capture.10

The official account holds that Draumer defrauded the people of Burunt for years until Gian stopped them.17 In his gala speech, Gian credited the Empire with supplying Burunt the means to defeat the Draumer threat and their counterfeit creations.24 Clodagh rejects the official account as a lie and says that many members of the Alshien are parents whose children suddenly developed Draumer abilities.17

Clodagh attributes the propaganda, the roundups and the camps to Gian personally, stating that Prikaz held no particular hostility toward Draumer before its alliance with him.34 The Warrens, which imperial patrols avoid, served as the last refuge for free Draumer.9

Draumer power and imperial Signarium initially appear to be opposing forces. Kyndel regards signaric technology as a form of dark magic.4

Over the course of the story the two are shown to be closely linked. The Obelisk is a signaric machine that extracts power from Draumer and converts it into cyrusite, the crystal that powers all signaric devices.3349 Heraldur, himself a Draumer, taught himself Signarium and designed the machine, and later built a signaric vambrace to protect Draumer from it.1933

Gian's Redarms are overdrawn Draumer controlled by rune-etched collars28, and his Warriors are Draumer fused into signaric armor and bound by torcs that take control of their tethers.4548 Gian's orange-lensed spectacles allow a person who is not a Draumer to see tethers.45

During the climax, a Draumer supplied power to the Obelisk voluntarily through his tether, without having it forcibly extracted. The resulting wave disabled every Warrior in the city and neutralized the Redarm collars, after which the Obelisk erupted into an enormous cluster of cyrusite.525354

The book does not explain the origin of Draumer power or why only some people possess it. Clodagh's account indicates that the ability can manifest suddenly in a child.17 Heraldur does not know what the Eldtree draws its energy from or for what purpose.33

title: Tether
blurb: The inner channel through which a Draumer draws power.

quote.text: He mentally yanked on his tether, drawing as much of the power as he could.

rows: Enhanced senses, speed, strength, balance, night vision; forging
A cable of light from the back of the neck

lead: A tether is the channel through which a Draumer draws power. Pulling on it fills the body with energy, sharpening the senses and strengthening the limbs, and it supplies the power used to forge creations.1

sections.html:
Drawing on the tether produces euphoria, brighter colors and sharper senses.1 The power can be retained in the body for strength and speed or channeled down the arm for forging.1 Retained power presses to be released, and releasing it returns the Draumer's perception to its ordinary dullness.1

Kyndel learned to draw in short bursts to keep the power from being torn away4, and Heraldur trained him to draw before he needed to move.19

When Liena carried Kyndel away from the palace, tendrils of light extended from the back of her skull as a glowing cable that brightened as she drew strength.26 After becoming overdrawn, Kyndel saw a Draumer girl's tether as a cable of light rising from the back of her neck while she forged, and understood that the flare of his own tether had been guiding the Redarms to him.32

Jelert later observed tethers through Gian's spectacles as cords of light rising a few feet above the neck of every Redarm and Warrior, flaring whenever they attacked.45 Warriors can also see tethers and are enraged by the sight of them.48

The torcs fitted to Gian's Warriors take control of the tethers of the Draumer inside. When a Warrior forges, the torc and the tether combine into a band of light that causes intense pain and drives the Warrior mad.454748

Heraldur showed Kyndel the Eldtree, a structure of enormous tendrils of light that rise from the ground across Burunt and merge above the palace into a single column, which branches out above the clouds. Heraldur described it as the world's tether and said that only a few people can see it.33

During the fever that followed his overdraw, Kyndel felt his tether widen and briefly made contact with an immense source of energy.30 Powering the Obelisk consumed his tether entirely and left him unable to forge.52

title: Draumer creations
blurb: Objects forged by a Draumer out of gray mist, solid but brittle.

quote.text: In his bare palm, a cloud of gray mist materialized, shifting and undulating as if alive.

lead: Draumer creations, also called constructs, are objects that a Draumer forges from gray mist using power drawn through the tether. They resemble ordinary material but are brittle, and they burst into light when they break.1

sections.html: To forge, the Draumer channels power down the arm until gray mist appears in the bare palm, then fixes a mental image on the mist until it solidifies.1 Forging takes effort: making handfuls of caltrops gives Kyndel pain in the skull and narrows his vision.4 Under extreme strain, the mist can emerge from a Draumer's pores instead of the palm.26

Creations break apart in a burst of bright light when they fail, which can blind an opponent.1 Kyndel's forged lockpicks break one after another as he works a lock, and a Redarm crushes one of his daggers into fragments of light.4

According to Heraldur, forged iron differs from natural iron and is roughly as durable as glass, and every forged object carries a pulsing signal unique to its creator (see haptic signature). The strength of a construct depends on its maker's focus and will at the moment of creation, and Heraldur judges Kyndel's constructs weak because his focus is unsteady.16 Constructs forged in anger are considerably stronger; Kyndel's rage-forged dagger withstood a jade weapon and lodged in a stone floor.1416

Skilled Draumer can alter a construct after forming it. Heraldur changed a jade club into a sword19, and Latif dissolved his stone axe head into mist and re-formed it around Kyndel's spear.26 Kyndel gained this ability after becoming overdrawn and practiced by shifting a dagger into a hammer, a spoon, a hook, a lockpick and shears. A thrown dagger cannot be reshaped while in flight.32

After losing his left arm, Kyndel sealed the stump with a rough mass of forged iron26, which he later reshaped into a functional iron arm that he controls finger by finger through its signature.32 The arm obeys him as long as his skin is in contact with the iron. Because it chafes his skin raw, he shapes it with ventilation holes, and most observers take it for armor.41

The arm can form claws, flow into a lock and expand to break it43, and change into a shield or a billhook.4750

• Kyndel's daggers, lockpicks and caltrops.14
  • The Founder's rings, long-lasting Draumer relics.45
  • Liena's obsidian flower.414
  • Kyndel's iron replica of the hexagonal plate.10
  • Stone manacles without chains, forged by a Redarm.46
  • An iron wall that Kyndel braced into the rock of a palace tunnel, the largest object he had ever forged.50

title: Overdraw
blurb: The danger a Draumer faces when drawing too much power through their tether.

quote.text: He was dangerously close to overdraw. If he didn't let go now, it would destroy him.

rows: Pain behind the eyes and at the base of the skull

lead: Overdraw is the harm a Draumer suffers from pulling too much power through the tether. Its first sign is pain in the skull.4

sections.html:
Kyndel experiences overdraw as sharp pain behind the eyes and at the base of the skull, accompanied by tunnel vision.4 Once it sets in, it prevents concentration and the power slips out of the Draumer's grasp, and a period of rest is required before drawing again.4

Severe overdraw leaves an aftereffect similar to a hangover, and Kyndel avoids alcohol for this reason.9

In the camps Kyndel saw Draumer die from taking in more power than their bodies could survive.14 He believed that Liena had died of overdraw after her final session at the Obelisk.16

This belief proved false. Liena survived and became a Redarm.26

When a Draumer draws until no further power can be taken, the tether locks at full draw. According to Liena, the process cannot be halted once it begins, and the Draumer either adapts or dies.28

Kyndel entered this state after losing his arm in the fight in Lazaro's office.26 He spent several days in Jelert's room suffering convulsions, fever and delirium while amber spread through his eyes.2830

Kyndel survived the transformation. His power now flows steadily instead of resisting him, and the constant draw can be reduced but not shut off; it enhances his senses and stamina. His eyes turned a vivid orange, and he gained the abilities to reshape constructs and to see tethers.32

Heraldur became overdrawn while being tortured with the Obelisk, though in his case the change affected only one eye, possibly because the device was then smaller and cruder.33

All Redarms are overdrawn Draumer.28 Heraldur concealed his orange eye under an eyepatch for years. After Kyndel's transformation the two men displayed their eyes openly, and rumors of fire-eyed demons spread through the Warrens.41 The condition does not remove the danger of overreaching, and Heraldur warns Kyndel that he is exhausting himself to the point of ruin.41

When an overdrawn Draumer dies, the eyes revert to their natural color, as Liena's and Heraldur's did.47

title: Haptic signature
blurb: The pulse a Draumer creation gives off, unique to the Draumer who made it.

quote.text: Its familiar haptic signature smoothed the tension in his shoulders.

lead: A haptic signature is the pulse that a Draumer creation gives off, which other Draumer can feel by touch.4 Each signature is unique to its creator.16

sections.html: When Kyndel touches the Khar Founder's ring, a faint pulse travels up his arm to the base of his neck and identifies the ring as a Draumer creation.4 Liena's obsidian flower carries a signature he knows well; it feels cool and faintly buzzing, and handling it calms him.49

Heraldur explains that every Draumer artifact carries a pulsing signal unique to the Draumer who made it.16 He recognized Kyndel as a Draumer as soon as he touched the iron plate Kyndel had forged to replace the hexagonal plate.14
Kyndel learned to operate his forged iron arm by following the pulses of its signature, eventually distinguishing its individual parts from the whole.32

title: Founder's rings
blurb: Silvery rings carried by the oldest noble bloodlines of Burunt.

quote.text: The entire band was carved from a single piece of silvery metal, a delicate branch etched along its center.

rows: A single piece of silvery metal

lead: Founder's rings are rings carried only by the oldest bloodlines of Burunt, the Founding Houses.4 The ring of House Khar, which belonged to Amara Khar's late father, plays a part in the story.6

sections.html:
Each ring is carved from a single piece of silvery metal with a fine branch etched along its center, and the family name is engraved inside the band. The Khar ring bears the name Khar'andor.4

The rings are Draumer creations, and a Draumer can feel their pulse on contact.4 Heraldur notes that Draumer relics have only sentimental value and cannot be sold.5 The book does not explain who made the rings or how they have endured.

Apart from the inscription the rings are identical, and Khar'andor was the original surname of the Khar family.29

Kyndel assumes that the ring is worn by the ruling head of a House, and therefore that an heir without one has not yet taken leadership.9 Amara regards the ring as worthless as a trade good because of its political significance.6

The ring was the most prized possession of Amara's father. Her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar, frequently took it and misplaced it, so Amara kept it in a locked drawer.6 Kyndel Heim stole it during his burglary of the Khar house and found it too recognizable to sell.4

Kyndel wore the ring as part of his disguise as Khorshed Kazemi and discovered that he could not remove it.9 When Amara saw it at the Stilton party, she accepted his claim to belong to House Kazemi.9

After Kyndel lost his left arm in the palace, Gian showed Amara the ring, recovered from the severed arm, and held it as leverage over her.29 Gian's men returned it a few days before the Khar gala, where Dhonya wore it.42

title: Obsidian flower
blurb: A small flower of black glass that Kyndel Heim carries as a keepsake.

quote.text: Its familiar haptic signature smoothed the tension in his shoulders.

lead: The obsidian flower is a palm-sized flower of black glass carried by Kyndel Heim. It has kept its fine shape through years of rough handling, and it is his last remaining connection to someone named Liena.4

sections.html: The flower is a Draumer creation whose haptic signature is familiar to Kyndel. It feels cool and faintly buzzing to the touch, and its hum steadies him when he is anxious.49

Heraldur's men took the flower from Kyndel after his capture, and Heraldur returned it when Kyndel silently demanded it.5 Kyndel later told Heraldur that it came from Liena, a Draumer friend from the camps whom he believed to be dead.14

During a fight with a Redarm, the flower fell from Kyndel's pocket. The Redarm stopped, asked who he was, and fled with it.14

That Redarm was Liena herself, the only Draumer Kyndel had known who could forge obsidian.26 When she left Kyndel in Jelert's care, she gave Jelert an obsidian flower for him; the text does not state whether it was the same one.28 Kyndel held it when he regained consciousness.28

title: Signarium
blurb: The rune-based engineering of the Prikaz Empire, powered by cyrusite.

quote.text: Signarium has the power to change the world.

rows: Signaric engineers, such as Jelert Egarro

lead:
Signarium is the rune-based engineering of the Prikaz Empire. Engineers carve sequences of runes, organized into runic arrays, into metal connected to cyrusite, and the arrays direct the crystal's energy to perform work.213 Anything built on these principles is described as signaric.1

Signaric technology powers the Empire's ships, weapons and lamps, and the Empire introduced it to Burunt. Major Jelert Egarro, a signaric engineer, believes it could improve the life of every citizen and end scarcity.2

sections.html:
A signaric device operates by passing power from cyrusite through engraved runes. Jelert repairs a ship's stove by realigning one of its arrays to restore the flow of energy to the heating element, a repair he considers basic for anyone who completed the academy's introductory course on runic symbols.2

Any change in the placement of runes alters the flow of power, and a misaligned sequence can cause the energy to falter, fail or rebound.18 Runes function only while intact, so a broken artifact is useless.10 Devices can be activated remotely by pressing an activation rune linked to a matching array.18 The discovery of a new rune is extremely rare; the last engineer to make one was appointed to the Empress's personal advisory board.15

Signarium is taught at the imperial academy, where Jelert graduated first in his class.2

The discipline was traditionally a delicate and painstaking practice, closer to artisanship than to industry.40 Gian's hidden factory beneath the palace changed this by using heated stamps to imprint runes onto parts, so that a single trained engineer was needed only to produce the stamps.40

The Empire brought signaric technology to Burunt together with its rule. Signaric lamps light the noble district and the main roads, while the narrower side streets still rely on ordinary flame.19 According to Jelert, the territory has gained farming machinery, fireless lighting, plumbing and factories over the past decade.38

The center of signaric work on the island is Signarium Hall, a laboratory in the palace that serves as both study and forge. It contains worn worktables, shelves of rune-etched books and powdered reagents, and a furnace, and the Viceroy inspects its engineers' work every month.8

Under Master Lazaro, the hall's engineers compete aggressively and sabotage one another, and Jelert's requisitions for even basic supplies are refused.1215

Gian's ambitions redirected the hall toward weapons production. Engineers who objected to the railcasters were killed when Signarium Hall was bombed, an attack Gian blamed on the Alshien. He presented the bombing as the punitive counterpart to the reward of a city built on Signarium.35

• Signaric lamps with a steady white-blue light, mounted on posts in Mintika Point and along the main roads.19
  • Signaric ships that sail without masts or sails.2
  • The signaric spear and the brightshield of the Iron Spears (see signaric weapons).2
  • Rune charges, palm-sized explosive devices smuggled in the Warrens.45
  • An engraving tool with a heated tip powered by a cyrusite chip.8
  • Chandeliers dimmed by exchanging their symbols.21
  • Lanterns with sensors that light when someone steps forward.26
  • Kinetic absorption runes lining Gian's carriage.45
  • A vocal amplification node of bronze inlaid with cyrusite and runes.55

The creation of signaric weapons is illegal in the Empire's territories, including Burunt.2

Signaric devices are strictly regulated, and gangs in the Warrens smuggle them.4

The territories receive only refined cyrusite, cut to standard sizes and stamped with the imperial seal through a process that limits its power.35

Gian avoided imperial oversight by building weapons in laboratories beneath the palace, an operation that Liena says he had been expanding for years, and he concealed his own cyrusite shipments from Prikizan soldiers who might report them to the Empire.2829

• Jelert Egarro, a signaric engineer and major of the Empire.2 He discovered aetheric magnetic flux.15
  • Master Lazaro, head engineer of Signarium Hall.8
  • Blazej Rodion, an engineer of the Petrovskaya Academy.8
  • Heraldur, who taught himself Signarium and keeps a secret workshop beneath the Warrens.1433

• Runeforge capacitor: Jelert's power device, converted into an explosive at Yeshall.13
  • The magno-signaric rail system: Jelert's plan to connect the islands by rail.8
  • Aetheric magnetic flux: Jelert's rune for a levitating rail.15
  • Railcaster: a weapon built from Jelert's runes.25
  • Signaric vambrace: Heraldur's protection against the Obelisk.19
  • Torc: an energy converter later used to power the Warriors.2845
  • Signaric lenses: spectacles that reveal tethers.45
  • The Obelisk: the machine that converts Draumer power into cyrusite.33

In Burunt, Signarium is presented as the Empire's gift and is opposed to the Draumer. Kyndel regards it as a form of dark magic, and the Redarms who pursue him wear armor lit by runes.4

The story reveals a close connection between the two systems. The Obelisk converts Draumer power into cyrusite, the fuel of every signaric device, and Gian kept a Draumer chained to it to build up his stockpile.33

Rune-etched collars control the overdrawn Draumer who serve as Redarms28, and signaric torcs take over the tethers of the Draumer sealed inside Gian's Warriors, whose armor responds to them as an extension of their own bodies.4548

In the climax, Jelert used Signarium to allow a Draumer to power the Obelisk voluntarily, as Heraldur had originally intended. The resulting wave disabled the Warriors and extinguished the city's signaric lights.5254

Three months after the fall of the palace, Burunt mines its own cyrusite. Jelert, now Master Engineer, plans to make Signarium available to the whole city, including a magno-signaric rail linking the islands of the chain.55 The cluster on the palace site has shown the world that the Empire is no longer the only major signaric power.55

title: Cyrusite
blurb: A glowing orange crystal that powers all signaric devices.

quote.text: The pale orange crystal glinted softly.

rows: Pale orange; honey-colored when raw

lead: Cyrusite is the pale orange crystal that powers signaric devices. Gems of it are set into weapons and tools, and runic arrays draw on its energy.2

sections.html:
Cyrusite gives off a soft glow.2 Small chips used in tools dim as their energy is spent and must be replaced through requisition.8

Raw cyrusite is volatile. It glows a warm amber-orange, and its facets project outward in an irregular, branching form. Only refined cyrusite, cut to standard sizes and stamped with the Empire's seal, is shipped to the territories, and the refining holds its power to a consistent middle level.35

Overloading cyrusite causes an explosion, and when viewed through signaric lenses the blast releases thousands of threads of light.45

Burunt receives a limited allocation of refined cyrusite, and Gian cites the cost when rejecting Jelert's rail.8 Prikizan belief holds that cyrusite forms only beneath the imperial capital as the gift and blood of the Earth Mother, Valenska, a doctrine that gives the Empire a mandate to share its technology and raise up other civilizations.13

Jelert argues that the discovery of cyrusite outside the Empire would undermine faith in Valenska, on which the Empress's rule depends.38

Gian showed Jelert a piece of raw cyrusite, suggesting that he had a source outside the Empire.35

While smuggling cyrusite for Gian, Amara concluded that a factory between the city's center and Mintika Point concealed a mine.39

The actual source was the Obelisk, which extracts power from Draumer and converts it into cyrusite. Gian kept his brother alive as a power source for the machine, adding its output to his stockpile.33 Jelert confirmed that he had seen the device's product in Gian's possession.49

When the rebuilt Obelisk was activated, it erupted into an enormous cluster of orange cyrusite that destroyed the palace.5354 Three months later, imperial shipments have ceased, and Burunt has begun mining its own cyrusite, setting aside an emergency reserve before selling any.55

title: The Obelisk
blurb: A machine connected to the Draumer labor camps of Burunt.

quote.text: He’d rather die than kneel before the Obelisk again, feeding them his power like a sacrificial lamb.

rows: Heraldur, with Gian Magnus
Draws power from Draumer and turns it into cyrusite
Draumer camp beneath Mintika Point; later the palace
Bloomed into a colossal cyrusite cluster

lead: The Obelisk is a device connected to the Draumer labor camps of Burunt.4 Captured Draumer are forced to kneel before it and surrender their power.4

sections.html: In Kyndel's memory the Obelisk is a black, branching pillar in a circular room, where chains closed around prisoners' wrists without anyone fastening them.30 The place where it stood in the camp is ringed by six iron loops used to chain its victims.43 Fully assembled, it is a tall structure of dark metal in the form of a twisted tree, with bare branches and faint runes that pulse in a slow, regular rhythm.50

Kyndel was made to kneel before the Obelisk for years. The process drained him painfully, and many Draumer died from it.16

Heraldur reveals that the original design was intended to let a Draumer produce cyrusite voluntarily, and that the forcible extraction of power was an unintended and brutal outcome.33 Kyndel later identifies the machine as a signaric device that drains power from Draumer and converts it into cyrusite.49 Its effective range is about thirty feet.49

Heraldur reveals that he built the Obelisk in his youth, hoping to give Burunt Draumer power with which to resist the powerful nations across the sea.16 He built it together with his brother, Gian Magnus.33

When Heraldur tried to destroy the machine, Gian chained him, turned the Obelisk on him and cut his face, and Heraldur became overdrawn after yielding to the device.33 Gian then sold Burunt to the Empire, imperial engineers completed the machine, and Heraldur was held as a power source supplying cyrusite to Gian's stockpile until he escaped.33

Heraldur spent years building a signaric vambrace to protect Draumer from the Obelisk, intending to destroy it.19 When he and Kyndel raided the camp beneath Mintika Point, the Obelisk had been removed, and only a pale circle remained on the floor.43

Amara revealed that Gian had used her to smuggle the Obelisk into the palace in pieces, on three wagons.49 Kyndel proposed turning it against the Warriors. Jelert and Gian rebuilt it on the floor of the old railcaster factory and removed its cyrusite chamber, so that it could draw directly from Kyndel's tether through Heraldur's repaired vambrace.4950

With Kyndel supplying power through proper channels, the Obelisk released a blinding white wave across the entire city. Every Warrior collapsed, the Redarm collars were neutralized and signaric lights went dark, while ordinary people felt no effect.525354

The Obelisk then erupted as orange cyrusite grew rapidly from its branches and brought down the palace. An enormous translucent cluster of cyrusite now stands on the site.5354

title: Redarms
blurb: Armored hunters who track down Draumer for the Viceroy.

quote.text: they were the Viceroy’s hounds, tasked with hunting down the remaining Draumer. They were Redarms.

rows: Black armor, crimson sleeves, geometric helms, lightning gauntlets, runic boots
Freed after the fall of Gian

lead: The Redarms are armored enforcers who serve the Viceroy as hunters, charged with tracking down the Draumer who remain free in Burunt.4

sections.html:
Redarms wear black metal armor over the chest, hands and feet, with crimson sleeves and smooth angular helmets whose eye slits glow pale orange.4 Their gauntlets carry an electric charge that drops anyone within reach, and runic boots allow them to leap twenty feet.4 They throw bolos, move with unnatural speed and appear able to see in the dark.4

They also carry steel batons, and their helmets give their voices a metallic tone.14

Kyndel long assumed that the Redarms were Prikizan constructs.4 The Redarm who recognized Liena's flower, however, spoke with a voice that sounded partly human and cried out in pain as a person would.14

In Lazaro's office, Kyndel cut the strap of a Redarm's helmet and exposed a Burition man with honey-colored eyes, Latif, who then forged a stone axe, establishing that the Redarms are Draumer. The second Redarm present was Liena.26

Liena explained that every Redarm is an overdrawn Draumer enslaved by Gian through a rune-etched collar. The collar kills its wearer if Gian activates it, if the wearer tampers with it, or if Gian dies.28 According to Liena, the Empress knows of the arrangement as part of her agreement with Gian.28
Overdrawn Draumer can see tethers, and the Redarms locate free Draumer by the flare of their tethers when they draw power.32

Redarms pursued Kyndel through the city on several occasions41419, demonstrated the railcaster at Gian's gala25, and guarded Gian after Kyndel's attack on him.35

Liena was taken after she broke ranks to save Kyndel.43 Two older Redarms ambushed Kyndel and Heraldur in the prison camp. They agreed to talk when Kyndel offered to free them, but warned that their collars would kill them if anyone tampered with them.43

During the night of Crownfall, Gian deployed Redarms alongside his Warriors, and the Warriors attacked Redarms before any other target.4448

Gian claimed that the Redarms would die if he did, and showed a signaric band on his wrist.50 Nine surviving Redarms joined Amara's column51, and a Redarm who forged stone turned against Gian in the palace and was shot dead.53

The Redarms collapsed when the Obelisk's wave crossed the city. One Redarm's collar was broken while the device was neutralized, and he revived a minute later, free of it.54 The book does not state whether the wave is the reason the Redarms survived Gian's death.

• Liena (obsidian).26
  • Latif (stone).26
  • An older woman who forges silvery-white metal, and an older man who forges crystal.43
  • Amara's captor, who forges iridescent stone.46
  • A Redarm who forges black stone and one who forges crystal, both guarding Gian in the palace.50
  • A Redarm who forges copper, on the Warrens wall.54

title: Signaric weapons
blurb: Weapons powered by cyrusite and runes, illegal to make in the Empire's territories.

quote.text: The creation of signaric weapons is illegal there, so you can focus on sanitation.

rows: Illegal to create in the territories

lead: Signaric weapons are arms powered by cyrusite and runic arrays. Their creation is illegal in the territories of the Prikaz Empire, including Burunt.2 Jelert Egarro refuses to make them.2

sections.html:
The characteristic weapon of the Iron Spears is a short spear with a runic array engraved along the shaft, linking the blade to a weighted butt that holds a cyrusite gem.2

Dusan's spear can emit a pulse of kinetic force.50
A brightshield holds cyrusite at its center and converts the kinetic energy of each blow into a harmless flash of light. It is designed to withstand repeated engagements.2

Smugglers in the Warrens carry palm-sized signaric devices that detonate in a burst of light4, and Heraldur sends his men against a rival armed with rune charges.5

The runeforge capacitor, a power device invented by Jelert, was converted into the explosive used to crush the Yeshall rebellion.1213

Jelert later built a crude impact-triggered bomb from the cyrusite housing of Gian's carriage.45

Jelert chose Burunt in part because weapons cannot legally be made there.13 He cites the Empress's prohibition on signaric weapons in the territories.18

Gian broke this law openly when he unveiled the railcaster at his gala.2527 He told Jelert that he intended to build weapons to defend Burunt against the Empire itself.35

• Railcaster.25
  • Warriors.4445

title: Railcaster
blurb: A signaric weapon that fires metal projectiles, unveiled by the Viceroy.
lead: The railcaster is a signaric weapon introduced late in the first half of Crownfall. Viceroy Gian Magnus unveiled it at his gala as a means of repelling enemies at a distance.25

sections.html:
A railcaster has a broad base about half an armspan long that tapers toward one end, with a handle at its midpoint and a shoulder strap. Runic arrays glow along the base.25

A switch builds up a humming, visible charge, and touching the activation rune fires metal projectiles with a sharp electric crack, with enough force to shatter heavy wooden targets.25

The prototypes were assembled from parts of Jelert's rail, with the addition of a portable housing, larger cyrusite reserves and a soldered projectile chamber.31

In use, guards fire metal disks in straight-line bursts and reload from cylinders worn at the hip.43

At the demonstration, Jelert recognized his own aetheric magnetic flux runes in the weapon and was reminded of Yeshall. Gian introduced Blazej Rodion as the founder of Burition Signarium.25

Blazej had developed the weapon from Jelert's rail prototype without his knowledge, and on inspection day had approached Gian to undermine the rail project in the weapon's favor.31

The weapons were manufactured in caverns beneath the palace.2838

Jelert discovered a complete assembly line there, producing one railcaster every six minutes, with perhaps two hundred already crated. He destroyed the line's central engine by removing its regulator runes and forcing all of its power into the furnace.40

Prison guards used railcasters against Heraldur's raid43, and Jelert and Gian used prototypes during the fight in the factory beneath the palace.52

Gian killed a Redarm with one, and Jelert killed Gian with another.53

title: Aetheric magnetic flux
blurb: A signaric rune discovered by Jelert Egarro for a levitating rail.

quote.text: A rail system that uses aetheric magnetic flux.

lead: Aetheric magnetic flux is a signaric rune connected to Jelert Egarro's work on rail transport. Jelert discovered it, and it forms the basis of his design for a levitating rail system.15

sections.html:
Jelert first proposed to the Viceroy a magno-signaric rail linking Burunt to the mainland across the archipelago, in which refined cyrusite would be channeled through tuned runic conductors to generate a magnetic propulsion field.8 Gian and Lazaro rejected the plan as too expensive.8

The design channels the resonant properties of cyrusite into a polarized repulsion field between rail and carriage, allowing the carriage to float without friction at low power.13

New runes are discovered so rarely that Blazej Rodion was astonished by the discovery.15 Blazej proposed a stabilizing matrix to keep the cyrusite core from overloading.15

Jelert and Blazej built a test track with interchangeable rune plates. On activation, a square metal puck rose an inch above the rails and moved along them; alternating the polarity allowed them to push and pull the payload, and faster switching between poles increased its speed.18 In an earlier test the puck was propelled into the stone wall.18
The runes were adapted into the railcaster without Jelert's knowledge.25
After Crownfall, Jelert plans a magno-signaric rail linking every sizable island in the chain, capable of moving goods between islands in half a day.55

title: Runeforge capacitor
blurb: A power device invented by Jelert Egarro that the Empire turned into a weapon.
lead: The runeforge capacitor is a signaric device connected to Jelert Egarro's past. He invented it while working for the Empress.13

sections.html: Jelert describes the capacitor as a device able to power very large machines, with applications in manufacturing, medicine and construction. Someone later found a way to increase its power draw exponentially, causing it to discharge all of its energy at once as an explosion.13

The Empire used the weaponized capacitor to crush a rebellion in Yeshall, a territory north of Prikaz, killing thousands, among them women and children.121338

Jelert received a medal for the invention. He later volunteered for the post in Burunt partly because signaric weapons are illegal in the territories.13

The memory troubled him again when his rail runes were turned into the railcaster, and he feared that the Empress would seize those designs as she had seized the capacitor.2528

title: Hexagonal plate
blurb: A rune-covered signaric artifact that Heraldur sends Kyndel to steal.

quote.text: It’s quite distinctive, covered in Prikizan runes.

lead: The hexagonal plate is a six-sided metal disk about a hand span wide, covered in Prikizan runes. Heraldur sends Kyndel Heim to steal it from the Stilton estate and declines to say what it does.9

sections.html: The plate was displayed on a velvet cushion in a copper-framed glass case, in a room of the Stilton estate filled with similar rune-carved objects.9

Kyndel's first attempt during the Stilton party failed after his confrontation with Amara Khar attracted a crowd.9

He returned that night, lifted the unlocked case using Draumer strength and escaped while Lord Stilton fired at him with a musket. In an alley he found that the plate had cracked in two. Believing a broken artifact to be worthless, he forged an iron replica that copied its shape and runes, and discarded the halves.10

The replica was darker and duller in color than the original. Kyndel warned Heraldur that it was brittle, and Heraldur nonetheless praised his work.10

Heraldur later revealed that he had recognized the plate as a fake from its signature, and that he collected such artifacts for their runes, as references for a device intended to bring Gian down.14 That device was the signaric vambrace.19 The plate's original function is never stated.

title: Torc
blurb: A rune-etched neck ring stolen from the palace, whose design proves central to Gian's plans.
lead: The torc is a signaric device in the form of a neck ring. Heraldur sent Kyndel to steal one from the Master Engineer's office as the final component of his device against the Obelisk.24

sections.html:
The stolen torc consists of two metal spirals whose open ends nearly meet. It is sized to close around a neck and is heavier than it appears.26

While repairing it, Jelert determined that it is a converter built to draw in energy, refine it and release it in a stable form, designed for a power source with a runic signature he had never encountered.28

Kyndel took the torc from Lazaro's office on the night he tried to kill Gian.26 Jelert repaired it while sheltering Kyndel28, and Kyndel then gave it to Heraldur.33 Kyndel noticed that the Redarms' collars resemble it.33

Gian tested Jelert by having him complete a partial prototype of Lazaro's, which Jelert recognized from its anchor pattern and central ring array. Jelert secretly added runes intended to set off a feedback loop under high energy loads, so that the torc would pass testing and fail in actual use.31

Gian later revealed that Jelert's completion of Lazaro's torc had made the Warriors possible. Jelert initially believed that his sabotage had never taken effect.45

Each Warrior wears a heavy bronze torc around its neck.47 The torcs take control of the tethers of the Draumer inside, and when a Warrior forges, torc and tether merge into a band of light that drives it mad.4548

Destroying the torc frees the Warrior from the feedback loop, but the Draumer inside cannot control the armor afterward and dies soon after. Amara ordered every squad to target the torcs.48

Jelert eventually admitted to Kyndel that the flaw he had deliberately built into the design was the cause of the Warriors' madness.49

title: Warriors
blurb: Towering signaric war constructs unveiled late in the story.
lead: The Warriors are towering armored constructs that appear in the final part of Crownfall. Gian Magnus unveiled them at the House Khar gala as the army that would drive the Empire from the islands.44

sections.html: Warriors stand nearly ten feet tall, with angular silver plating, wedge-shaped torsos, long thin limbs and featureless helmets. They move silently, with no gears, steam or engine.44

When Jelert's improvised bomb tore limbs and armor from four Warriors, it exposed human flesh inside.45

Each Warrior contains a mutilated Draumer whose limbs have been amputated and whose torso has been fused into a rune-covered steel frame, with a heavy bronze torc fitted at the neck.47 A Redarm stated that this is the fate Gian reserves for the disloyal.47 Kyndel suspected that the prisoners missing from the Draumer camp had been turned into Warriors.47

Damaged Warriors repair themselves by forging metal, stone or crystal. When they forge, a glowing band of light forms where torc meets tether; the Warrior screams, claws at the torc without being able to touch it, and goes on a rampage, killing allies and enemies alike.4547

A maddened Warrior can spread the madness to others by wounding them until they forge.45 Warriors can see tethers and attack Redarms first, and otherwise target the largest group nearby.48

The madness was caused by Jelert's sabotage of the torc design.49

More than a hundred Warriors were estimated to be loose in the city.48 Breaking a Warrior's torc kills it, and Amara ordered every squad to aim for the torc.4851

When Kyndel powered the rebuilt Obelisk, its wave spread across the city and every Warrior collapsed.5354
Liena was made into a Warrior as punishment for breaking ranks. Kyndel broke her torc, and she recognized him and died free of its madness.47

title: Signaric vambrace
blurb: A signaric arm guard built by Heraldur.
lead: The signaric vambrace is an arm guard carved with signaric runes. Heraldur spent years building it to protect Draumer from the Obelisk.19

sections.html: Heraldur had Kyndel steal rune-covered artifacts to serve as references14, and identified a torc in the Master Engineer's office as the last component he needed.1924

Heraldur wore the vambrace during the raid on the Draumer camp, and it protected Kyndel as long as he stayed close to him.43

After Heraldur's death, Kyndel took the cracked vambrace and collected its broken pieces.47

Kyndel gave the pieces to Jelert and told him that the vambrace had been made by the creator of the Obelisk.49

Jelert repaired and modified it so that Kyndel could feed power into the Obelisk. Because it works only in contact with flesh, it was strapped to Kyndel's right arm. Through it, his power passed along proper channels without being forcibly extracted.5052

Jelert warned that if the connection broke before stabilizing, the resulting feedback would destroy the Obelisk and Kyndel, and probably the chamber as well. The process caused Kyndel severe pain.5253

title: Signaric lenses
blurb: Gian Magnus's orange-lensed spectacles.

rows: Gian Magnus, later Jelert Egarro
Reveal tethers and power flow

lead: The signaric lenses are spectacles with gold wire frames and orange lenses that Viceroy Gian Magnus began wearing after the attempt on his life.29

sections.html:
Jelert found the cracked spectacles in the wreckage of Gian's carriage. Through them he saw a cord of light rising from the neck of every Redarm and Warrior, which he identified as their tethers.45

Jelert concluded that the spectacles are signaric glasses.48 They also allowed him to trace lines of power through runic arrays.53
Jelert wore the lenses during the final assault, using them to watch a dead Warrior's tether fade and to check the Obelisk's arrays, until Gian knocked them from his face.5053

title: Burunt
blurb: Burunt is the island city where Crownfall takes place, a mountainside port ruled for the Prikaz Empire by a Viceroy.

quote.text: There’s no help in this city.

rows: Burition Isles, between the Prikaz Empire and the Requing Federation
Viceroy Gian Magnus, for the Prikaz Empire (later Queen Amara)
Kyndel Heim, Amara Khar, Jelert Egarro, Gian Magnus

lead:
Burunt is an island city built on the slope of a mountain above a busy harbor.1, 3 Nearly all of Crownfall takes place there. When the story opens, the city is a territory of the Prikaz Empire governed by Viceroy Gian Magnus, who took power roughly ten years earlier in a violent struggle during which the slum district of the Warrens was burned.1, 2 The native population are the Buritions, and the imperial Prikizans form a conspicuous ruling presence in the streets.3

All three point-of-view characters live in the city: the thief Kyndel Heim, the impoverished noblewoman Amara Khar, and the newly arrived imperial engineer Jelert Egarro.1, 2, 3 The authorities hunt Draumer, people with innate powers, and imperial signarium supplies the lighting of the wealthier streets.1

sections.html:
The city occupies one island in the chain of jagged islands that links the Prikaz Empire in the west with the Requing Federation in the east.2 Its districts are stacked up the mountainside. The dock ward and its warehouses lie at the bottom, while the noble district of Mintika Point sits high above, still near enough to the harbor to receive its sea breeze.1, 3 The streets are narrow and winding, built of stone and paved with basalt brick. The climate is humid, with frequent breezes and intermittent rain.1, 3

Amara considers the island an inhospitable place because of its strong sun and heavy rainfall.13 Some streets are laid with black cobblestones, and cables for signaric lanterns run across the alleys.14, 19 From a rooftop at night the city can be seen rising toward the distant mountain, with the ocean extending beyond the docks.33 Rain on the island tends to come in brief, heavy bursts.46

Burunt is divided into distinct districts, and the book repeatedly sets its wealthy upper city against its ruined poor quarter.1

  • The Warrens: the poorest quarter, burned a decade ago and controlled by gangs. Imperial soldiers enter only when out of uniform.1
  • Mintika Point: the most aristocratic district, with widely spaced mansions, gardens and signaric streetlamps. A shopping district adjoins its southern edge.1
  • The dock ward and harbor: warehouses, a dockhouse run by imperial clerks, and inspections by the harbor master.3, 7
  • The palace: seat of the Viceroy at the center of the city54, which contains Signarium Hall8.
  • The merchant quarter, on whose edge Mintika Point lies.43, 46
  • The southeast gate, a city gate with a Prikizan checkpoint and gatehouse.17
  • The Three Coins, a modest tavern with salt-encrusted windows used by both locals and imperial soldiers.12
  • The Stilton estate and Lord Modir's manse, both venues of the noble social season.9, 37
  • A system of sewers and tunnels running from the Warrens to Mintika Point and further.14, 43

A Viceroy rules Burunt on behalf of the Prikaz Empire, which classes the island as one of its territories.1, 2 Imperial law prohibits the manufacture of signaric weapons in the territories.2 Local custom does not treat verbal agreements as binding.3 Curfews apply throughout the city except in the Warrens.1

Before imperial rule, Burunt had a governing body that Lady Dhonya Khar refers to as the Council of Lords.6 The noble houses, headed by the oldest bloodlines, the Founding Houses, remain the core of high society.4, 9 Trade bodies, among them the Stockwright's Council, and craft guilds also influence civic life.3, 5 The Empire's ban on commerce with the Requing Federation ruined many of the old trading houses.6

In the course of the story the Viceroy federalized the city's main financial institution, Brothers Incorporated. The move gave him the power to recall debts in an emergency and access to all financial information in Burunt.21

Alshien intelligence estimates the Viceroy's forces at about thirty-five hundred soldiers with signaric support, with the Iron Spears and Redarms as elite units. Prikizan infantry guard the outer walls and the palace and patrol every district apart from the Warrens.34

The population combines native Buritions and imperial Prikizans, producing an uneasy mixture of languages and customs.3 Buritions have their own island tongue, and Prikizans use their native language among themselves.1, 3 The imperial colors are teal and brass, and imperial silvers circulate as currency.1 Draumer once moved freely through the city; propaganda posters now warn against them and promise rewards for their capture.1

Burition religion is centered on Eld, and oaths derived from it, such as Thorns and Eld knows, are in common use.1, 3 The nobility observes a social season of parties beginning in spring.1

Burunt is a port and trading city. Noble houses such as House Khar built their fortunes on shipping, and imports such as Requing liquors pass through the harbor.3 Signaric devices require cyrusite, which the Empire supplies to its territories only in refined, standardized form.8, 35 The Alshien finance their operations by raiding Prikizan ships that carry Burunt's cyrusite payments between the island and the Empire.34

Viceroy Gian secretly controlled a source of raw cyrusite outside imperial supply. Amara deduced that a factory located between the city center and Mintika Point served as a front for his mine.35, 39

The article History of Burunt covers the island's past in detail. In summary, the island was independent within living memory. About ten years before the story, Gian Magnus rose to power in a conflict that burned the Warrens; Burunt then became an imperial territory, and Draumer were hunted and sent to the labor camps.1

Gian's official version of these events, in which a Requing invasion was repelled with Prikizan assistance, was invented. He used it as cover to eliminate his rivals before handing the island over to the Empire.24, 44

Draumer, people with innate powers, once lived openly in Burunt.1 Under the Viceroy they are persecuted. Older propaganda posters call on citizens to protect their homes against Draumer counterfeits, newer ones offer rewards for information leading to an arrest, and those captured are sent to the labor camps.1

The Viceroy's armored Redarms track down the remaining Draumer, and he pays bounties for their capture.4, 5 In the first years of his rule, Draumer and their prominent relatives were purged.5

Draumer abilities can appear suddenly in children, and many members of the Alshien are parents who joined the rebellion to protect such children.17, 34

The Redarms are themselves overdrawn Draumer, kept enslaved by the Viceroy through collars etched with runes.26, 28

Each protagonist experiences a different part of the city. Kyndel Heim moves between the Warrens and the noble estates he robs while planning to assassinate the Viceroy.1 Amara Khar travels from the dock ward to the upper districts in her effort to keep her house solvent.3 Jelert Egarro arrives by ship as an imperial engineer who hopes to use signarium to improve people's lives.2

The three meet at the city's social occasions: the Stilton party, a dinner at a Prikizan-owned restaurant, and the Viceroy's royal gala at the palace, where Gian presented the railcaster.9, 13, 25

On the night of House Khar's gala, Gian proclaimed Burunt independent of both the Empire and the Requing Federation and sent his armored Warriors into the city, which burned for the second time in ten years.44, 48 By the end of the night Gian was dead, the palace had collapsed under a huge cyrusite cluster, and a combined Burition and Prikizan resistance held the Warrens.53, 54

Three months later Burunt was independent. The surviving nobles crowned Amara Khar as the first queen of Burunt, and she established a ruling council as a check on the monarchy.55 Prikizans were offered safe passage home. Many accepted, while hundreds of tradesmen, farmers and blacksmiths remained.55 The city now mines its own cyrusite, and a granite memorial inscribed "The Remembered of Crownfall" stands in the square that was held during the fighting.55 The Empress has not replied to Amara's request for a parley.55

title: The Warrens
blurb: The Warrens is the burned-out slum district of Burunt and Kyndel Heim's home turf.

quote.text: Clean roads gave way to soot-streaked ruins, relics of the fire that had gutted the district a decade ago

rows: Kyndel Heim, Lefty, Heraldur, Khamron
Gangs and the Warrens Barons

lead:
The Warrens is the poorest quarter of Burunt, a district of ruins, mud and improvised shacks.1 Fire destroyed much of it ten years before the story, during the conflict that brought Viceroy Gian Magnus to power.1 Imperial soldiers go there only out of uniform, since wearing the Empire's teal and brass in the district invites a violent response.1

Kyndel Heim lives in the Warrens and sells his stolen goods there to the fence Lefty.1

sections.html:
A broken arch marks the boundary of the Warrens.1 Before the fires, as Kyndel recalls, it was an orderly district of regular rows of stone buildings and basalt-paved roads.1 Since then the paving has degraded to dirt and mud, and most structures are sagging shacks made of wood and cloth.1 The district smells of refuse, old smoke and damp earth.1 Curfews are enforced elsewhere in the city, but the Warrens is largely lawless.1 It also contains public houses where the poor and hungry congregate.3

An extensive tunnel network lies beneath the district. A trapdoor behind the bar of an abandoned inn gives access to it and to Heraldur's concealed signaric workshop.14 Heraldur's people used a disused warehouse as a training ground and an old alehouse as one of their strongholds.10, 16 The Warrens is enclosed by an old district wall, which Heraldur's people quietly repaired.19

Gangs and gang leaders known as Warrens Barons control the district; Heraldur and Baron Taher are among them.5 Shortly before the story Heraldur's crew took over the fences Anard and Maju, and Lefty secretly works for him.1, 5 His organization smuggles regulated signaric devices into the Warrens.4

For a Draumer on the run, the Warrens is the last remaining place of refuge.9

In his early years Gian attempted to suppress the Warrens by force, but after heavy losses among his soldiers he switched to a policy of containment, and Prikizan patrols now deliberately avoid the district.34 A crime boss styling himself the Lord of the Warrens has brought most of the gangs under his control.34

Heraldur and Kyndel later stopped hiding their orange overdrawn eyes, and rumors of demons with burning eyes increased their standing in the district.41 Heraldur intended to make the slums into a fortress and had barricades hidden in readiness along the old district wall.41

On the night of the Khar gala, Heraldur's raid on the Draumer prison left the Warrens by way of the sewers, and the freed prisoners were brought back to bunkers in the district.43 The gangs organized a defense, barricaded every entrance and held off Gian's forces.45

After Heraldur died, Amara Khar relocated her resistance camp to the Warrens. The defenders let her in after she told them of Heraldur's death and said that Kyndel Heim had sent her.48, 51 The district became the survivors' final stronghold. A Warrior broke through part of the wall, and the defenders were losing when the wave released by the Obelisk disabled every Warrior in the city.54

Three months later the Warrens is being slowly and laboriously rebuilt.55 Its square, which has a crumbling fountain, was the busy center of the poor quarter before Gian came to power. Kyndel sits there with Otisen instead of attending Queen Amara's speech.55

title: Mintika Point
blurb: Mintika Point is the noblest district of Burunt, home to its wealthiest estates.

quote.text: The air smelled faintly of citrus and lavender from the carefully maintained gardens lining the estates.

rows: The nobility of Burunt; House Khar (implied)

lead: Mintika Point is the most aristocratic district of Burunt, an area of widely spaced mansions set high above the harbor.1 In Chapter 1 Kyndel Heim spends hours there surveying estates to rob.1

sections.html:
The mansions of Mintika Point have limestone facades, gilded fences and well-tended gardens of citrus and lavender. Signaric lamps on wrought-iron posts light the streets.1 The sky above the district is open and wide, in contrast to the narrow strips visible from the lower city.1 A shopping district borders its southern edge, and an old anti-Draumer propaganda poster hangs in an alley nearby.1

Amara Khar heads from the dock ward toward Mintika Point when going home, which implies that the Khar estate is located there, although the book never says so directly.3

Mintika Point lies on the edge of the merchant quarter.43 During the fighting, Amara's first base was a townhome in the merchant quarter south of the district.46

In Chapter 1, while cutting down an old propaganda poster near the district's southern edge, Kyndel attacked a young imperial soldier who was kicking a homeless woman.1

The Draumer prison in which Kyndel was held lies directly beneath Mintika Point, under the homes of the nobles who had tolerated Gian's exploitation of the city.43 Heraldur's crew reached it from the Warrens through the sewers.43

Amara picked up Gian's cyrusite at a factory between the city center and the edge of Mintika Point, and concluded that the factory was a front for his mine.39

On the night of Crownfall, Heraldur died just outside Mintika Point after killing two Warriors, and Gian was last seen west of the district, fleeing from Warriors.47, 48

title: The palace
blurb: The palace is the seat of the Viceroy of Burunt and home to the city's imperial engineers.

quote.text: Several signaric chandeliers, each the size of a carriage, cast an ethereal glow throughout the room’s enormous height.

rows: Burunt, heart of the city
Gian Magnus; Lazaro, Jelert Egarro, Blazej Rodion
Destroyed; replaced by a colossal cyrusite cluster

lead: The palace is the residence and seat of government of Viceroy Gian Magnus in Burunt.7, 8 It also houses Signarium Hall, the laboratory in which the imperial engineers, among them Jelert Egarro, live and work.8, 15

sections.html:
The grand ballroom contains signaric chandeliers as large as carriages, a balcony along each side and a marble floor. Its tapestries alternate between portraits of the Viceroy and images of Eld, the World Tree.21 The Brothers Incorporated Banking Institute operates a branch within the palace.21

The building includes a signaric wing whose windows are all fitted with blast-proof glass, an engineering wing, and living quarters for the engineers.15, 18 Master Lazaro's office was on the third floor at the far end of the east wing, behind a door marked with silver sigils, and its lanterns lit automatically when someone approached.26

Gian's office contains an unlit hearth, books, maps and a tall window, and a Redarm stands guard at its door.29

Caverns beneath the palace serve as laboratories, factory floors and storage.38 The largest housed a railcaster assembly line powered by a central signaric engine and overlooked by a wrought-iron walkway.40 The precisely cut stone of the upper halls changes to rough rock in the lower levels.50

The Viceroy's royal gala took place at the palace. There Gian unveiled the railcaster and named Blazej Rodion as its inventor.21, 25

After the gala Kyndel stole a torc from Lazaro's office and attempted to kill Gian there, but Gian pulled Lazaro into the path of the blade.26

On Gian's orders Signarium Hall was bombed, killing every engineer inside. Gian blamed the attack on the Alshien.35, 37

Jelert entered the palace hidden among Amara's cyrusite crates and destroyed the engine of the railcaster factory. Gian captured him in the corridor outside.39, 40

The Obelisk was brought into the palace in pieces and assembled on the wrecked factory floor.49, 50 On the night of Crownfall, after it had disabled every Warrior in the city, orange cyrusite erupted from its branches and brought the roof down.53 The palace collapsed, and an enormous translucent cyrusite cluster now occupies its site.54, 55

title: Signarium Hall
blurb: Signarium Hall is the signaric laboratory inside the Viceroy's palace, where imperial engineers design devices.

quote.text: Signarium Hall was an intricate machine, half academic study, half forge, and entirely familiar.

rows: Master Lazaro, Jelert Egarro, Blazej Rodion
Bombed; all engineers inside killed

lead: Signarium Hall is the laboratory of the palace in Burunt, where the Empire's signaric engineers work under a Master Engineer.8 Jelert Egarro is assigned there after his arrival on the island.8

sections.html:
The Hall combines the functions of a study and a workshop. It is furnished with long, worn wooden tables, metal shelving holding rune-etched books and powdered reagents, and overhead signaric lamps, with a furnace burning at the far end.8 Engineers there take apart old devices, build new ones and engrave runes using heated tools powered by cyrusite chips.8

The room is very large, with a high arched ceiling.15, 18 The engineers have quarters elsewhere in the palace and retire to them when the Hall closes for the night.15

The Viceroy conducts a monthly inspection day, and on presentation days engineers show their work to him and to the Master Engineer.8, 15 Newcomers are commonly hazed and deliberately left uninformed.8 Under Master Lazaro the engineers competed aggressively, sabotaging each other and blocking rivals' requisitions. Lazaro encouraged this rivalry and favored certain engineers.12, 15

On his first inspection day Jelert proposed a magno-signaric rail system to Viceroy Gian, who rejected it as too expensive.8 Blazej Rodion then proposed an alliance with Jelert.8

Working late in the Hall, Jelert and Blazej built a levitating rail prototype based on a new rune of Jelert's design.18 Blazej secretly adapted the design into the railcaster.25, 31

Following Lazaro's death Jelert was made Master Engineer with responsibility for the Hall.35 A few days later an explosion destroyed it and killed all the engineers present. Gian held the Alshien responsible, but Jelert later told Amara that Gian had ordered the bombing himself to silence engineers who had objected to the railcasters.35, 37

title: House Khar estate
blurb: The House Khar estate is the ancestral manor of Amara Khar's family, grand but stripped bare by hard times.

quote.text: The floor was tiled in stone from the Burition mountain, sturdy squares of slate that had stood the test of time.

rows: Amara Khar, Dhonya Khar, Balfourd, Sireen

lead: The House Khar estate is the residence of House Khar in Burunt. Amara Khar lives there with her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar, and a diminishing staff headed by the majordomo Balfourd.3 At the beginning of the story the property is in decline: a bougainvillea vine is damaging the southern wall, a leaking fountain has flooded the dew flower beds, and the cook has resigned.3

sections.html:
The floors are laid with slate quarried from the Burition mountain, and the walls are paneled in intricately carved wood from local forests.6 The rooms were once furnished with rugs, artworks and portraits, which have been sold off one at a time.6 Amara's office, which belonged first to her father and then to her mother, contains a desk whose bottom drawer she keeps locked.6, 34

The garden has gravel paths and an old kitchen door covered in vines.4

Other parts of the house shown in the story include a great hall, a gallery, a foyer hung with a costly chandelier, a grand marble staircase, a parlor, the kitchens, and a narrow hallway leading to Amara's office.34, 36, 42

In more prosperous years the family held an annual gala at the estate. Lack of money forced the dismissal of the household guards the week before the ring theft.6

Kyndel entered through the garden kitchen door and stole food, two books and the family's Founder's ring from a locked drawer.4, 6

Once Amara had joined the Alshien, the rebels were frequently at the house, and Clodagh used her office as a base of operations.29, 34

Amara revived the House Khar charity gala at the estate as a trap for Gian, positioning crossbowmen behind openings between two paintings in the hallway to her office.34, 42 Gian turned the event against her, and twenty-seven people were killed at the estate that night.44, 46

title: The docks
blurb: The dock ward is Burunt's harbor district of warehouses and wharves, where imperial clerks inspect every cargo.

quote.text: The usual din of the harbor dulled in her wake.

lead: The docks, also called the dock ward, are at the foot of Burunt, where warehouses line the harbor.3 Amara Khar is at a marketplace there at the start of Chapter 3. The harbor master's inspections determine when cargo may be unloaded.3

sections.html:
The harbor lies far below the noble district of Mintika Point, and the route from the dock ward to the upper city crosses the whole of Burunt.1, 3

The dockhouse employs Prikizan clerks wearing imperial patches on their coats, who work alongside Burition dockhands.7 The dockmaster, Riocard, is a heavyset Burition who wears a flowing robe; Amara suspects him of accepting bribes.7 Imperial ships take precedence over all others, and the entire dock can be closed while one of them is being unloaded.7

The harbor master detained Master Naveed's cargo, citing a clerical error, which allowed Amara to purchase the goods originally promised to him.3

When Amara's ship, the Alisma, was scheduled for an inspection that would have revealed its smuggled cargo, she went to the dockhouse to confront Riocard. Jelert Egarro and Lieutenant Dusan arrived and provided a dozen soldiers to unload the ship, without realizing that the cargo was contraband.7

Because Gian controls the ports, he would learn of any attempt to book passage off the island.37

During the fighting on the night of Crownfall, Amara sent the Iron Spears to rescue civilians trapped near the east docks.48

title: Stilton estate
blurb: The Stilton estate is a Burunt noble manse, host of an early party of the social season.

quote.text: It was an extravagant display, a show of wealth in spotless brick.

lead: The Stilton estate is the manse of Lord Stilton, a member of the old nobility of Burunt.9, 10 It is the venue of a party early in the social season, which both Kyndel Heim and Amara Khar attend.9

sections.html: The manse is constructed of immaculate white brick and illuminated by two signaric limelights.9 Its interior includes lavishly furnished rooms, a library lined with books and a room displaying signaric artifacts.9 The grounds are laid out with gravel paths and clipped hedges.10

Heraldur sent Kyndel to the party, disguised as Khorshed of House Kazemi, to steal a hexagonal plate covered in runes from the display room.9 Kyndel set fire to the drapes in a library to create a diversion, but on his way back he ran into Amara, and the argument that followed attracted a crowd and spoiled his opportunity.9

Kyndel came back later that night and took the plate. Stilton's guards caught him, and Lord Stilton shot at him with a Requing musket from the top of the staircase.10

title: Heim Estate
blurb: The Heim Estate was the childhood home of Kyndel Heim's family.

rows: Guild Master Heim (Enir), Mistress Heim, Kyndel Heim

lead: The Heim Estate was the home of Kyndel Heim's parents. The name is first used by Otisen, who had been a house guard there.27 Kyndel recalls details of his childhood home from the first chapter onward, including his mother's library, where she kept papers of importance.1 He also remembers his father returning home with mortar on his hands.9

sections.html:
Kyndel's father, Enir, was a guild master and a well-known Draumer.5 He worked as a mason and owned a masonry shop.9, 14

The Heims were a guild family. Guild Master Heim had considerable influence among the city's craftsmen and Draumer, and Amara reflects that of all the old powers removed during Gian's rise, none suffered a greater fall.27

Lord Yasser Turan, a friend of Kyndel's father, visited often and debated questions of leadership with him by the fire.24

Kyndel's memories of the estate's fall include fire, burning silk, his mother screaming, and Gian standing over his parents' bodies.5, 16, 24

Otisen's account fills in the events. Gian attacked the estate with foreign soldiers and cut Mistress Heim's throat in front of her son. Otisen wounded Gian in the shoulder with a crossbow bolt, while Master Heim, tied up and on his knees, pleaded with the guards to take his son and flee. Otisen got away with Kyndel, and the other guards were killed.27

Kyndel later explains that his parents have no graves, since their bodies were consumed when the house burned.49

title: Burition Isles
blurb: The Burition Isles are the chain of islands, including Burunt, that lies between the Prikaz Empire and the Requing Federation.

quote.text: the island chain that bridged the Prikaz Empire to the west and the Requing Federation to the east

rows: Between the Prikaz Empire (west) and the Requing Federation (east)
