lead: The Burition Isles are the archipelago on which Burunt is located, a line of jagged islands connecting the Prikaz Empire in the west to the Requing Federation in the east.2 The name forms part of Gian's formal title, "the Empress's voice in the Burition Isles."24

sections.html:
The channels between the islands contain many shallows and rocks, which make them easier to navigate in small boats than in large signaric ships.2

Some of the other islands support estates and industry. Kyndel's cover story locates House Kazemi on a remote island estate that runs a logging business.9

At the royal gala Kyndel says that he comes from a farming island in the west, and Amara describes Khorshed as an heir from one of the western islands.24, 27

Jelert Egarro hopes to connect the islands with causeways and railways, tying Burunt more closely to the Empire.8, 15

Gian refused the proposal because he does not want a railway joining the island to the Empire.35

After Crownfall Jelert plans a magno-signaric rail network connecting every sizable island in the chain, capable of carrying goods between islands within half a day.55

title: Yeshall
blurb: Yeshall is a territory of the Prikaz Empire, mentioned by imperial characters.
lead: Yeshall is a territory of the Prikaz Empire that is mentioned in the story but never visited.12 Its memory troubles Jelert Egarro.12

sections.html:
Lieutenant Dusan tells Jelert about a captain of his acquaintance who served at Yeshall, where commanders deployed a new signaric explosive that killed both rebels and civilians, women and children among them.12

Jelert admits to Amara that the explosive was his own invention, the runeforge capacitor, which was turned into a weapon to put down the Yeshall rebellion. Thousands were killed, and Jelert received a medal.13 Part of his reason for coming to Burunt was that signaric weapons are prohibited in the territories.13

Jelert later explains that Yeshall lies north of Prikaz and that its people sought greater control over their own affairs. He says that whole towns were destroyed instantly, and that he requested a transfer to Burunt as an act of atonement.38

When Jelert discovers that his rail design has been converted into the railcaster, he sees it as a repetition of the runeforge capacitor and Yeshall.25 The memory troubles him again when he assembles a crude bomb on the night of Crownfall.45

title: Prikaz Empire
blurb: The Prikaz Empire is the militant western empire that rules Burunt through its Viceroy.

quote.text: The Prikaz Empire carries the blessing of the Earth Mother, Valenska, in our very lands

rows: Valenska, the Earth Mother

lead: The Prikaz Empire is a powerful state lying thousands of miles west of Burunt.1, 2 Its full name is the Prikaz Continental Empire.35 It is ruled by the Empress and holds Burunt as one of its territories through a Viceroy, Gian Magnus.1, 2 Its people are the Prikizans, and its soldiers wear the imperial colors of teal and brass.1

sections.html:
The Empire administers its distant possessions as territories.2 Imperial law prohibits the manufacture of signaric weapons within them.2

Imperial institutions mentioned in the story include the Imperial Academy, where Jelert Egarro graduated first in his class, the Artificer Corps, and the Admiralty, which grants the Bronze Pin for innovation.2 Jelert and Blazej Rodion both graduated from the Petrovskaya Academy.8 The Iron Spears are a brigade of the imperial army.2

Slavery has been outlawed in the Empire for more than two centuries.28

The Empire ships only refined cyrusite to the territories. Raw crystals are cut to standard sizes and stamped with the imperial seal, a process that caps their power at a uniform, moderate level.35

Prikizans hold that their land is blessed by the Earth Mother, Valenska. Cyrusite, which forms deep below the imperial capital and, according to their belief, nowhere else, is regarded as her blood.13 The Empire takes this gift as a mandate to spread signaric technology and raise up neighboring civilizations, and some interpret that mandate as license for conquest.13

Jelert argues that the Empire's strength rests on the belief that Valenska favors it, and that territories convert after seeing what signarium can do. A cyrusite mine outside the Empire would therefore undermine the religious basis of imperial authority.38

Burunt became an imperial territory about ten years before the story, following Gian Magnus's rise to power.1

Jelert believes that Burunt was among the few territories to have approached the Empire on its own initiative.13 The Empire subsequently banned trade between Burunt and the Requing Federation.6

Liena states that the Empress is aware that the Redarms are enslaved Draumer, and that the arrangement forms part of her agreement with Gian.28

According to Clodagh, Prikizans held no special hostility toward Draumer before their alliance with Gian; the persecution was something they learned.34

Gian was covertly developing weapons with which to resist the Empire.35 On the night of Crownfall he declared Burunt independent of both the Empire and the Requing Federation, and his loyalists, identified by yellow bands, fought Prikizan soldiers who remained loyal to the Empress.44, 45

Three months after imperial cyrusite shipments to Burunt ceased, Queen Amara's request for a parley had received no reply. Some people in the territories have started to doubt imperial doctrine, and reports indicate rising political and religious unrest within the Empire.55 Amara fears that the Empire, which continually seeks to expand, may still return.55
The Empire's principal rival is the Requing Federation to the east.2 Jelert describes the conflict between the two powers as one that could break out again at any time.28

title: Requing Federation
blurb: The Requing Federation is the eastern power that rivals the Prikaz Empire.

quote.text: Requing’s a whole other continent. You could lose yourself there,

rows: East of the Burition Isles, on another continent

lead: The Requing Federation lies east of Burunt, at the opposite end of the island chain from the Prikaz Empire.2 It has long traded with Burunt, where its distinctive liquors, unavailable from other sources, command high prices.3 The Federation does not appear directly in the story, although fear of it continues to influence Burunt's politics.

sections.html:
Requing liquors are highly valued in Burunt.3

The Empire's ban on commerce with the Federation cost House Khar most of its trade routes.6

The Federation relies on black powder in place of signarium. Requing muskets are extremely rare on Burunt, though Lord Stilton owns one.10, 12

Heraldur notes that Requing is a separate continent.14

According to Burunt's official history, the Federation invaded the island about ten years ago, and Gian repelled the attack with imperial help before aligning Burunt with Prikaz. This account portrays the Requing as opportunists.13 The Alshien were founded within the following year.13

At the royal gala Gian said that his brother had been killed in a Requing raid, which he called cowardly, and promoted the railcaster as a defense against a future Requing return.24, 25

The invasion never took place. Gian used the invented threat as an opportunity to eliminate his rivals and afterward signed the island over to the Empire.33, 44

The Alshien wanted the freed Draumer dispersed and sent to Requing, a plan that Heraldur refused.41

After Crownfall Queen Amara is concerned that the Federation may have designs on Burunt.55

title: Buritions
blurb: Buritions are the native people of Burunt and the Burition Isles.

quote.text: The native Buritions stood shorter and leaner, with warm skin and dark eyes that flickered like candles.

rows: Kyndel Heim, Amara Khar, Balfourd, Gian Magnus

lead: Buritions are the native people of Burunt.2, 3 Since Burunt became a territory of the Prikaz Empire, they have lived alongside the imperial Prikizans and largely under their authority.1, 3

sections.html:
Buritions are generally shorter and slighter than Prikizans. They have warm-toned skin, dark eyes, and deep brown or black hair, which they wear long and loose or loosely tied back.3 Their movements are graceful, they gesture expansively when speaking, and their speech is rhythmic and soft in its consonants.3 Burition women wear brightly colored silks, and kaftans and sashes are common garments.3, 7

Complexions vary within the population. Lord Yasser Turan, for example, is noted as having unusually light skin for a Burition.24

Buritions have a language of their own, the island tongue.1, 3 Their religion is focused on Eld, and their oaths use tree imagery, for example Thorns, for root's sake and Eld's canopy.1, 3, 4, 9

Many powerful Buritions, including the Viceroy, have given up traditional Burition silks in favor of Prikizan high fashion.8

The Alshien, a Burition rebel movement, oppose imperial rule.2

Many Draumer are Buritions, including the Redarms Latif and Liena.26, 28

On the night of Crownfall Buritions fought on both sides. Some wore the yellow bands of Gian's loyalists, while others joined Amara's combined Burition and Prikizan resistance.46, 48

title: Prikizans
blurb: Prikizans are the people of the Prikaz Empire, Burunt's imperial rulers.

quote.text: The Prikizan imperials stood out like steel in a land of silk.

rows: Jelert Egarro, Dusan, Blazej Rodion, the Empress

lead: Prikizans are the people of the Prikaz Empire. In Burunt they serve as the soldiers, officials, engineers and merchants of the ruling power.1, 3 The term also functions as an adjective for things associated with the Empire, as in Prikizan fashion or the Prikizan language.3, 8

sections.html: Prikizans are tall and broadly built, with pale, angular faces and straight or slightly wavy hair worn short or tied back.3 They typically wear stiff, sharply tailored uniforms or plain tunics. Amara reads suspicion in their narrowed eyes and finds their speech cold and curt, which she associates with the harsh winters of their homeland.3 They speak the island tongue with a heavy accent.1

Prikizans worship Valenska, the Earth Mother. Their oaths invoke the Goddess and the Halls, in forms such as Halls below and Hallowed Halls.13, 15 Prikizan dishes served in Burunt include kulebyaka, braised hare on buckwheat groats, and pickled cabbage.13 A Prikizan-owned restaurant in the city is decorated with carvings depicting the founding myths of Prikaz.13

Imperial soldiers in teal and brass patrol the city, though they enter the Warrens only out of uniform.1

Prikizan officers of the Iron Spears found Burunt's local troops hostile and unhelpful.12, 20

Jelert came to suspect that Gian was dividing Prikizans who were loyal to the Empire from those loyal to him personally.29, 38

On the night of Crownfall, loyal Prikizan soldiers in teal fought Gian's yellow-banded troops, and many of them joined Amara's combined resistance.45, 48

Afterward Queen Amara offered all Prikizans safe passage home. Many departed, but hundreds of tradesmen, farmers and blacksmiths decided to remain.55

title: Alshien
blurb: The Alshien are a Burition rebel movement fighting imperial rule in Burunt.

quote.text: ‘Rebel’ is a strange label for a person defending their home

rows: Clodagh (largest group), Farzin (other factions)
Otisen, Amara Khar
Just over 1,000 fighters, possibly 500 more in other factions
First year of Gian's rule

lead: The Alshien are Burition rebels who oppose the Prikaz Empire's rule over Burunt.2 Imperial officers such as Lieutenant Dusan regard them as insurgents who reject the benefits of imperial rule, and his Iron Spears were ordered to help the Viceroy destroy them.2 In Chapter 2 the Alshien raided the imperial ship carrying Jelert Egarro to Burunt.2

sections.html:
The raiders who attacked Jelert's ship fought with military discipline under a central commander, and they removed specific crates instead of taking the vessel.2

Five men died in the raid, and the raiders made off with signaric weapons.13 The movement formed in the first year of Gian's rule. In its early years it struck inside the city and targeted imperials exclusively, although bystanders were frequently harmed. It generally leaves trade vessels alone.13

The Alshien depend on anonymity and obtain their supplies (grain, salted fish, medical tinctures, canvas and boots) through intermediaries such as Master Naveed.1117 Many members are parents whose children developed Draumer abilities.17

Clodagh leads the largest group, while most of the other factions follow Farzin, whose raids inflict heavier casualties.34 Combined, the movement fields just over a thousand fighters, with perhaps five hundred more in Farzin's factions.34 After direct attempts to assassinate Gian failed at great cost, the Alshien shifted to small, targeted operations: sabotage, ambushes, and raids on Prikizan ships carrying Burunt's cyrusite payments.34 Clodagh's network has also hidden dozens of Draumer children from Gian.34 The movement is organized in cells.3442

The Alshien preferred to scatter freed Draumer and send them to Requing. Heraldur rejected this approach because he wanted the Draumer united as a fighting force.41

The relationship with House Khar began when Otisen bought the goods Amara had taken from Naveed and she identified him as Alshien. She agreed to supply the movement regularly at fair market price plus a nineteen percent premium for the risk involved.11

When Otisen and twelve others were detained at the southeast gate, Clodagh asked Amara for help. Amara vouched for them in a sealed letter and in exchange obtained Clodagh's signed confession to leading the Alshien.17

After hearing Otisen's account of the night the Heim Estate fell, Amara asked to become a full member of the movement, and the rebels became a constant presence in her household.2729

The partnership benefited both sides. House Khar provided the Alshien with a base, a public front and trade connections, and the rebellion's money reduced the house's debts.34 Together they planned to assassinate Gian at the revived Khar gala.3442

Gian had learned of the plan in advance. When disguised Alshien fighters attacked at the gala, his Warriors destroyed them, and Clodagh was killed while charging the Viceroy.44 Farzin, the commander the Iron Spears had pursued for months, appeared wearing Gian's yellow band; he had betrayed to Gian every target the Alshien intended to strike that night.4546

With its leaders dead or missing, Otisen urged Amara to lead the movement, and she took command of the survivors.46 For the rest of the night Alshien veterans fought alongside Prikizan soldiers in her resistance.4851

Clodagh's full name, Clodagh Askar, is carved on the memorial to the Remembered of Crownfall.55

title: Iron Spears
blurb: The Iron Spears are an imperial brigade sent to Burunt to hunt the Alshien.

quote.text: Dusan’s Iron Spears specialized in rebellious uprisings, in removing the head of a resistance before it became a problem for the Empire.

lead: The Iron Spears are a brigade of the imperial army. A detachment under Lieutenant Dusan sailed to Burunt alongside Jelert Egarro with orders to help the Viceroy destroy the Alshien.2

sections.html:
The brigade's characteristic weapon is the signaric spear, a short spear whose shaft carries a runic array connecting the blade to a weighted butt set with a cyrusite gem.2 Its soldiers also carry brightshields, which convert the force of incoming blows into harmless flashes of light.2

Brightshields work by means of kinetic absorption runes.45 Dusan's spear is also able to release a pulse of kinetic force.50

Alshien raiders attacked the Spears' ship during the voyage to Burunt and were driven off by a charge led by Dusan.2

Private Mirek and two other Spears were killed in the raid.2

After landing, Dusan's soldiers unloaded Amara Khar's ship as a favor, without knowing that it carried contraband.7

The brigade specializes in suppressing uprisings by eliminating the leadership of a resistance movement.12 In Burunt its main target was the Alshien leader Farzin, who repeatedly evaded its traps. The Spears also received little cooperation from local soldiers or help from other brigades.12

Dusan considered Burunt the worst assignment the Spears had ever received. Their Captain divided the squadron into continuous shifts to follow up reported Alshien sightings, none of which produced results.20

The Alshien regarded the Iron Spears and the Redarms as the Viceroy's elite units.34

When Gian turned against the Empire, Prikizan barracks across the city were overrun, but the Iron Spears entrenched themselves and held their position.45 They then joined Amara's resistance. She assigned them to rescue people trapped near the east docks, and Dusan took a seat on her council.48

Dusan accompanied Kyndel, Jelert and Otisen to the palace and survived its collapse.4953

title: Founding Houses
blurb: The Founding Houses are the oldest noble bloodlines of Burunt, each marked by a Founder's ring.

quote.text: It was not my intention to show disrespect to another Founding House of Burunt.

rows: House Khar, House Kazemi

lead: The Founding Houses are the oldest bloodlines of Burunt's nobility. Each possesses a Founder's ring, an heirloom found only among these lineages.4

sections.html:
Each ring is carved from a single piece of silvery metal, with a fine branch etched along its center and the family name engraved on the inner rim.4 When Kyndel handles the Khar ring he senses the faint pulse that identifies it as a Draumer creation.4 Heraldur observes that Draumer relics of this kind have sentimental value but little worth on the market.5

Apart from their inscriptions, the rings are identical.29 The Khar ring bears the name Khar’andor, the family's original surname.429

The ring carries weight at formal occasions; Dhonya Khar maintains that she cannot host the charity ball without wearing it.34

House Khar is the family of Amara Khar. According to Amara, it has existed as long as Burunt itself.13

House Kazemi is a Founding House that has been absent from Burunt's public life for years and maintains a remote island estate.9 Heraldur relied on that obscurity when he created Kyndel Heim's cover identity, Khorshed Kazemi. On seeing him wear a Founder's ring, Amara apologized for having slighted a fellow Founding House.9

When Gian condemned House Khar, he ordered the name Khar’andor removed from the records.44

title: House Khar
blurb: House Khar is an old and once-powerful noble house of Burunt, now led by Amara Khar.

quote.text: Even broken things can last if you’re stubborn enough to keep patching the cracks.

rows: Noble house (Founding House)

lead: House Khar is a noble house of Burunt. At the start of the story, its poverty is common knowledge.3 Its young heir, Amara Khar, manages the house's affairs with the help of the majordomo Balfourd while also caring for her mother, Lady Dhonya Khar.3 Amara's father died of illness, and her mother has since been afflicted by a condition Amara considers crueler still.3

sections.html:
House Khar was once a legitimate and celebrated trading house, and Dhonya commanded a large fleet.6 The house lost most of its trade routes when the Empire banned commerce with the Requing Federation.6 Since then its art and rugs have been sold off one piece at a time and its guards dismissed. Its accounts were held for generations by Goldguard bank.6

Amara says the house has been part of Burunt since the city's creation.13 Her father died when she was nine, after which Dhonya built up the house's standing until her name commanded respect and, at times, fear.13

Dhonya fell ill when Amara was thirteen. Amara holds her responsible for spending heavily on failing ventures and unreliable allies, and at fourteen Amara appeared in court to negotiate compensation for the repossession of the house's first ship.34 The house traditionally closed the social season with an annual charity ball, which it had held every year since before Amara's birth until the custom lapsed.34

The family's original surname, Khar’andor, is inscribed inside its Founder's ring.29

Amara trades aggressively, buying goods ahead of her rivals and selling cargo before it reaches port.3

She also smuggles, carrying contraband in false-bottomed crates aboard the house's only remaining ship, the Alisma.67 During this period the house's accounts were transferred to Brothers Incorporated, and its Founder's ring was stolen.6

A contract to supply the Alshien gave the house its first significant income in years.11 At the royal gala Amara signed a contract with Lord Yasser Turan, but she also learned that the Viceroy had recalled the house's debts, with ten percent due within a month and the balance three months after that.21

The house subsequently committed itself fully to the Alshien, providing them with a base and a public front.2734 Amara also transported cyrusite for Gian, and later the dismantled Obelisk.2949

House Khar revived its charity gala as a trap for Gian. Gian turned the event against the house: his banker read charges of treason ordering House Khar disbanded, its members executed and the name Khar’andor removed from the records.44 Dhonya was struck down that night and later died of her wounds.4446

After Crownfall, the surviving nobility crowned Amara the first queen of Burunt.55 Her mother's name, recorded as Dhonya Khar’Andor, is carved on the memorial to the Remembered of Crownfall.55

title: Council of Lords
blurb: The Council of Lords is a body from Burunt's past, mentioned only in passing.

quote.text: The Council of Lords would never let foreigners dictate our trade.

lead: The Council of Lords is a body from the history of Burunt. The book provides little information about it. Lady Dhonya Khar refers to it as though it still governed the island.6

sections.html:
In her confusion Dhonya forgets that the Empire controls Burunt and declares that the Council of Lords would never allow foreigners to dictate the island's trade.6 This suggests that the Council governed Burunt, or at least regulated its trade, before imperial rule. Its membership and powers are not described.6

In defending his actions to Kyndel, Gian claims that Burunt had been trapped between Prikaz and Requing while a council failed to act, leaving him to take matters into his own hands.50 The text does not specify whether he means the Council of Lords.50
After her coronation, Queen Amara ordered the creation of a ruling council to balance royal authority, a safeguard adopted after Gian's decade of absolute rule.55

title: Warrens Barons
blurb: The Warrens Barons are the gang lords who rule the slum district of the Warrens.

quote.text: I’ve played this game longer than the Warrens have had Barons.

lead: The Warrens Barons are the crime lords of the Warrens, the district of Burunt that imperial soldiers avoid.15 The most feared of them is Heraldur.5

sections.html:
Heraldur is a one-eyed gang lord who carries a jade cane.5 His crew has absorbed the rival fences Anard and Maju, and the fence Lefty secretly works for him.15 He claims to have been active in the Warrens' criminal trade since before the Barons existed.5

Baron Taher is another Warrens Baron. His son Luca ran an inn.5

When Luca demanded his delayed goods and told Heraldur to step aside, Heraldur killed him with his cane. He then sent Khamron with three dozen men and rune charges to kill Baron Taher and any potential successor, and to burn Luca's inn.5 The outcome for Taher is not stated.5

Heraldur's crew smuggles signaric devices into the Warrens and moves supplies through hidden caches.419 He operates from several strongholds, among them an old alehouse, and maintains a hidden workshop at the end of a tunnel network.1014

A crime boss styling himself the Lord of the Warrens has brought most of the district's gangs under his control.34

Within the organization, Khamron serves as a lieutenant and Lefty as quartermaster, while a surgeon with unsteady hands, known as a bonesaw, provides the nearest thing the district has to medical care.41

By the time of Crownfall, every gang in the Warrens answered to Heraldur.48 After his death his men held the district's wall and admitted Amara's column on the strength of Kyndel's name.51

title: Brothers Incorporated
blurb: Brothers Incorporated is a rising local bank in Burunt.

quote.text: They are a local bank that has been rising in financial circles in recent years, primarily known as debt traders

rows: Brothers Incorporated Banking Institute; Brothers Incorporated Bank
Burunt; branch in the palace

lead: Brothers Incorporated is a local bank in Burunt. Its main business is trading in debt.6 It acquired House Khar's accounts and loans from Goldguard bank, and Isadore Meyers became the house's contact there.6

sections.html:
By the time of the royal gala, the Viceroy had federalized the city's banking system and Brothers Incorporated had become Burunt's primary financial institution.21 Federalization gave him emergency powers to recall outstanding debts and access to all financial records in the city.21 Citing a rise in Alshien attacks on shipping, he recalled the debts of House Khar and several other noble houses. Ten percent was due within a month and the remainder after a three-month grace period, whereas House Khar had expected seven more years to repay.21 The Institute maintains a branch inside the palace.21

Amara later concluded that the federalization and the unveiling of the railcaster were parts of a single plan.27

At the Khar gala, Isadore Meyers read out the charges against House Khar, which included paying its debts with stolen currency that had been marked to trace its crimes.44 He was killed later that night when a rock crashed through the window of Gian's overturned carriage.45

title: Goldguard bank
blurb: Goldguard bank is the long-time bank of House Khar.

quote.text: It has been our honor at Goldguard bank to serve and provide for the esteemed House of Khar for generations.

rows: A stylized soldier's helmet with a feathered plume, in yellow wax

lead: Goldguard bank served House Khar for generations.6 Its correspondence is sealed with yellow wax bearing a stylized soldier's helmet topped by a feathered plume.6 Amara Khar has come to dread the sight of the seal.6

sections.html: In Chapter 6 Goldguard notified Amara that it could no longer meet the particular needs of her estate and had transferred her accounts and loans to Brothers Incorporated.6 Amara hoped the change might give her more time, and she instructed Balfourd to investigate the new bank.6

title: Yellow bands
blurb: The yellow bands are armbands that identify one faction in the book's final act.
lead: The yellow bands are armbands that identify a faction late in the book. They mark forces loyal to Viceroy Gian Magnus personally, as distinct from Prikizan soldiers whose loyalty lies with the Empire.4445

sections.html:
Gian mistrusted Prikizan soldiers who were loyal to the Empire, and Jelert came to suspect that Gian was dividing the army along those lines.2938

When Gian arrived at the Khar gala, every uniformed man in his escort wore a strip of yellow cloth around the upper arm.44 He declared that his Warriors, his Redarms and the loyal defenders of Burunt would expel the Empire from the islands.44

During the street fighting that followed, many of Gian's soldiers wore the same teal uniforms as the loyal Prikizans, and the armbands were the only means of telling the two sides apart.45 Buritions fighting for Gian wore them as well.46 Captain Farzin, ostensibly an Alshien commander, reported to Gian wearing a yellow band.45

title: Eld
blurb: Eld, the World Tree, is the center of Burition faith and the source of most of Burunt's oaths.

quote.text: Eld, the World Tree, its sprawling branches reaching past the heavens.

rows: The Eld, the Eldtree, the World Tree

lead: Eld, also called the Eldtree or the World Tree, is the central figure of Burition belief. Buritions invoke it constantly, and many of their everyday oaths and curses draw on tree imagery.13 The narration compares the patience of Balfourd to that of the Eldtree.3

sections.html:
Eld is imagined as an immense tree whose canopy covers the world. Kyndel draws on this picture when thinking about himself and his surroundings, for example in describing a leaping Redarm as an angel of death descending from the tree's branches.45

Eld is also associated with the afterlife. Amara refers to her ailing mother as not yet having joined the Eld.13

The imagery appears in decoration as well. Tapestries in the palace ballroom alternate between portraits of the Viceroy and depictions of Eld, and branch and leaf motifs appear on Amara's gala gown and on the Founder's rings of the old houses.421

Burition speech contains many oaths based on the tree. Recorded examples include:

  • By the Eld's left nut1
  • Thorns and thorning, Kyndel's habitual curses1
  • For Eld's sake and Eld knows3
  • For root's sake and bent-branch4
  • Eld's blood and Eld's canopy59
  • Eld's thorns6
  • What in Eld's bark14
  • Eld-forsaken, Eld-damned and By Eld2426
  • Branches above, root-rotting and roots-foresaken2632
  • Rotsap50

From a rooftop at night, Heraldur showed Kyndel the Eldtree as it appears to overdrawn eyes. Enormous tendrils of light rise from the ground throughout Burunt, pass through buildings without disturbing them, and converge above the palace into a single twisted column that spreads out like a canopy above the clouds.33 Heraldur describes it as the tether of the world itself. According to him it has always existed, but only a few people can perceive it, and it is most visible at night and from a distance.33 He first saw it on the night his brother seized the city, and he never discovered what it draws energy from or for what purpose.33

Otisen swore his loyalty to Kyndel on the Eldtree and on the graves of Kyndel's parents.49

The imperial Prikizans follow a different religion. They worship Valenska, the Earth Mother, and believe cyrusite to be her blood. Their oaths invoke the Goddess and the Halls.1315 Prikizan officers condemned Kyndel's plan to use the Obelisk as blasphemy against the sacred gifts of Valenska.49

title: History of Burunt
blurb: A chronology of Burunt's past, from its Founding Houses to the night of Crownfall and its aftermath.

quote.text: Burunt was always a minor player in the larger game of continental conflict.

lead:
This article lists the known events of Burunt's history in chronological order. The book gives no calendar years, so events are dated relative to the start of the story, which opens in spring at the beginning of the nobility's social season.1 For a more detailed account of the story's own events, see the timeline.

The official version of Burunt's history taught to most citizens casts the Prikizans as protectors, the Alshien as rebels and the Requing as opportunists.13 Much of this account was fabricated by Gian Magnus.44

sections.html:
• Founding: The Founding Houses, Burunt's oldest bloodlines, trace their origins to the city's creation; House Khar claims to have existed since that time.13 Each house possesses a Founder's ring, which is a Draumer creation.413
  • Independent Burunt: The island was self-governing. Draumer moved openly through the streets, and the Warrens was a well-ordered district of stone buildings and basalt roads.1 The Council of Lords appears to have regulated trade.6 Guild Master Heim was highly influential among the craftsmen and Draumer.27 House Khar was a renowned trading house and held an annual charity ball.634
  • Years before Gian's rise: Gian Magnus and his brother Heydar worked together toward Burunt's independence. Heydar taught himself Signarium, and the brothers built the Obelisk, which was intended to let a Draumer produce cyrusite voluntarily. In practice it extracted power by force. When Heydar tried to destroy the device, Gian had him chained and tortured with it, and Heydar became overdrawn.33
  • Amara's childhood: Amara Khar's father died of illness when she was nine, after which Lady Dhonya Khar raised the house's standing. The book does not place these events precisely relative to Gian's rise.13

sections.h: Gian's rise (about ten years before the story)
sections.html:
About a decade before the story, Gian Magnus came to power through a violent struggle during which fire destroyed much of the Warrens.1 Burunt subsequently became a territory of the Prikaz Empire.12

According to Gian's public account, ten years earlier the nation had been on the verge of collapse and his brother had been killed in a Requing Federation raid. Gian claimed that he then rallied the Prikizan soldiers docked in the city, defeated the attack and led Burunt into the Empire.1324

  • The night of the seizure: Gian attacked the Heim Estate with foreign soldiers and killed Mistress Heim. The house guard Otisen shot Gian in the shoulder and escaped with the young Kyndel.27 The Heims' house burned with their bodies inside.49
  • The same night: Heydar Magnus killed the four soldiers sent to transfer him and escaped. Gian announced that Heydar had died fighting the Requing invasion. Heydar later adopted the name Heraldur.33
  • Aftermath: The Requing incursion had never taken place. By inventing an enemy, Gian created the pretext to eliminate his rivals, after which he signed the city over to the Empire and received a team of imperial engineers, who completed the Obelisk.3344

• First year: The Alshien formed and attacked imperials within the city. At the height of the violence Amara and her mother seldom left home for about a month.13
  • Early years: Draumer were purged, their prominent relatives arrested, and captives sent to the labor camps; propaganda posters warned the public against Draumer counterfeiting.15 Gian's soldiers attempted to subdue the Warrens and eventually settled for containing it.34 Kyndel, who had been hidden in the countryside, was sold to Prikizan soldiers for the Viceroy's bounty.27
  • Early years: Lady Dhonya Khar fell ill when Amara was thirteen. At fourteen Amara negotiated in court over the repossession of the house's first ship.34
  • Undated: The Empire banned commerce with the Requing Federation, and House Khar lost most of its trade routes as a result.6
  • Undated: Heraldur made two unsuccessful attempts on Gian's life, the second of which was repelled by the Redarms. He then lived quietly in the Warrens.33
  • About five years before the story: Heraldur began building the numbers, influence and power he would need for his revenge.33
  • Elsewhere in the Empire: The rebellion in Yeshall was suppressed with explosives adapted from Jelert Egarro's runeforge capacitor.1338
  • Two years before the story: Kyndel escaped from the Draumer camp through a hole made by an old woman's explosion.514

• Spring: The social season began.1 The Iron Spears sailed for Burunt and were attacked by the Alshien during the crossing.2
  • Spring: Goldguard bank transferred House Khar's debts to Brothers Incorporated.6
  • The royal gala: The Viceroy federalized Burunt's banking, recalled the debts of noble houses and unveiled the railcaster.2125 Kyndel attempted to kill Gian after the gala, and Master Lazaro was killed.2630
  • Days later: Signarium Hall was bombed on Gian's orders, killing its engineers, and the attack was blamed on the Alshien.3537
  • Later: Jelert Egarro destroyed the railcaster factory beneath the palace and was captured.40

• The night of the Khar gala: Gian declared Burunt independent of both the Empire and the Requing Federation and was proclaimed the first king of Burunt. He then turned his Warriors loose on the city, which burned for the second time in ten years.4448
  • The same night: Heraldur's raid on the Draumer prison found that the Obelisk had been removed. Clodagh, Dhonya Khar, Liena and Heraldur were killed.43444647
  • Before dawn: Drawing power through Kyndel's tether, the Obelisk released a wave that disabled every Warrior in the city. Jelert shot and killed Gian, and the Obelisk erupted into a cyrusite cluster that destroyed the palace.5354

• Three months later (summer): Imperial cyrusite shipments had ceased, and Burunt had begun mining its own.55 The surviving nobility crowned Amara Khar the first queen of Burunt, and she established a ruling council.55
  • Three months later: Prikizans were offered safe passage home, and hundreds chose to stay. The Empress had not responded to Amara's request for talks, and unrest was spreading within the Empire.55 A memorial to the Remembered of Crownfall was erected.55

title: Draumer labor camps
blurb: The Draumer labor camps are the prisons where captured Draumer are held and drained of their power.

quote.text: You don’t get to give up.

rows: Kyndel Heim, Liena

lead: The Draumer labor camps are where Draumer captured in Burunt are sent.1 Kyndel Heim remembers being dragged there by soldiers.1 Prisoners are forced to kneel before the Obelisk, which drains their power.4

sections.html:
The text refers to the site variously as the Draumer labor camps or camp, the Draumer camps, and the Draumer isolation camps.151419

Its location is kept secret. Heraldur, despite years of opposing Gian, does not know where it is and wants Kyndel to guide him there.14

The prison lies beneath Mintika Point at the edge of the merchant quarter, directly under the homes of the nobility who had tolerated Gian's exploitation of the city, and it has held Draumer for the past ten years.43 It can be reached through the city's sewers.4143

Prisoners were kept along a corridor of overcrowded, unheated cells with too few beds.43 The open recreation area, which the guards called the Yard, offered no exercise beyond a fighting ring in which prisoners fought each other for food rations, a practice designed to keep them from turning on their captors.43 The Yard was surrounded by a mess hall, staff offices and the guards' barracks.43

The Obelisk was kept in a locked circular chamber, where prisoners' wrists were chained while it extracted their power, a process Kyndel recalls as agonizing.1630 Six iron loops for chains were fixed into the floor.43

The extraction killed many prisoners. Kyndel witnessed Draumer burned out from within by excessive power.14

After the night Gian seized power, Kyndel was hidden in the countryside until he was sold to Prikizan soldiers for the Viceroy's bounty.1427 He spent several years of his childhood in the camp, where other prisoners beat him over bread and guards forced him to kneel before the Obelisk.163043

In the camp he met Liena, who remained loyal to him after others had abandoned him, gave him bread and insisted that he keep going.19 He believed that she had died there, overdrawn and discarded.16

Liena had in fact been taken from the cells and turned into a Redarm.26

Two years before the story, an elderly Draumer woman caused an explosion that killed her and breached the wall, and Kyndel escaped through the opening. He believes he is the only Draumer ever to have escaped the camps alive.514

On the night of the Khar gala, Kyndel guided Heraldur and nearly a hundred Warrens fighters through the sewers to the repaired breach through which he had escaped.43 They blew open the wall and fought the guards, a mixed force of Prikizans and Buritions, some of them armed with railcasters.43

Only about two dozen starving prisoners remained, and the Obelisk chamber was empty apart from a pale circle on the floor.43 The freed Draumer were carried to bunkers in the Warrens.43 Kyndel suspected that the missing prisoners had been turned into Warriors, and Liena herself later appeared there inside a Warrior frame.47

Amara Khar, acting on Gian's orders, had smuggled the Obelisk into the palace in pieces.3949

title: Social season
blurb: The social season is the round of noble parties and galas held in Burunt from spring onward.

quote.text: The event marking the start of both spring and the highborn social season was only a week away.

rows: Burunt nobility, imperial officials and wealthy merchants

lead: The social season is the period of parties and galas held by the nobility of Burunt. It begins with an event marking the arrival of spring.1 Kyndel Heim intends to forge papers that will admit him to the season's parties so that he can locate and kill the Viceroy.1

sections.html:
• The Stilton party: held at the Stilton estate, where Kyndel, posing as Khorshed Kazemi, first met Amara Khar.9
  • Other parties: Kyndel attended at least two more as Khorshed without encountering the Viceroy.14
  • The royal gala: the Viceroy's gala in the palace ballroom, at which Gian announced the railcaster and the bank recalled the debts of noble houses.2125
  • Lady Teymoor's misfortune: a gala remembered for a rumored incident involving a plate of custard.37
  • Lord Modir's gala: held across the second floor of Modir's manse, with each room set up as a separate, self-contained gathering.37
  • The Khar gala: House Khar's revived charity ball, which traditionally closes the season.3442

Admission requires papers and a credible lineage; the fence Lefty tells Kyndel that acquiring them would cost ten more bags of stolen goods.1

The guests at galas include Burunt nobles, wealthy imperials and military officers.21 Conversation is outwardly polite but loaded with double meanings, and Amara uses each event to pursue contracts and alliances.2124 Members of the Founding Houses wear their Founder's rings.934

House Khar's annual charity ball traditionally ended the season. According to Dhonya Khar, it was held every year without exception, including years when disease struck the city.34

The season's final gala, held at the Khar estate, marked the beginning of Crownfall. Gian used the occasion to arrest House Khar, declare independence and unleash his Warriors, and he described the event as a staged spectacle meant to teach rebels to fear humiliation.4445

title: Glossary
blurb: An alphabetical list of in-world terms used in Crownfall.
lead: This glossary lists terms from Crownfall, each with a brief definition and the chapter in which it is introduced or explained. Definitions that reveal later events are concealed behind spoiler tags.

sections.html:
• Activation rune: A rune that is pressed to trigger a signaric device; Jelert uses one to start his rail prototype.18
  • Aetheric magnetic flux: A rune discovered by Jelert Egarro that underpins his levitating rail design and, later, the railcaster.1525
  • Alisma: The last ship owned by House Khar, used for smuggling.67
  • Alshien: The Burition rebel movement opposing imperial rule. See Alshien.2
  • Artificer Corps: An imperial organization that adopted three of Jelert's designs.2
  • Bonesaw: Warrens slang for a surgeon; Heraldur's bonesaw treated Kyndel's stump.41
  • Brightshield: A cyrusite-cored Iron Spears shield that converts the force of blows into harmless light.2
  • Brothers Incorporated: A rising local bank whose business is trading debt. See Brothers Incorporated.6
  • Burition: A native of Burunt. See Buritions.23
  • Burition Isles: The chain of islands to which Burunt belongs. See Burition Isles.24
  • Collar: A rune-etched band binding a Redarm to Gian, which kills its wearer if activated or tampered with, or if Gian dies.28
  • Construct: An alternative term for a forged Draumer creation, which Kyndel also applies to the Redarms.416
  • Council of Lords: A body that governed Burunt before imperial rule. See Council of Lords.6
  • Crownfall: The name for the night of Gian's fall, whose dead are honored on a memorial.55
  • Cyrusite: A pale orange crystal that powers signaric devices. See cyrusite.2
  • Draumer: A person born with the power to draw on a tether and forge objects from gray mist, persecuted in Burunt. See Draumer.1
  • Draumer labor camps: The prisons to which captured Draumer are sent. See Draumer labor camps.1
  • Eld: The World Tree of Burition religion, invoked in most local oaths. See Eld.13
  • Eldtree: Another name for Eld.3 Heraldur identifies the luminous tree seen by overdrawn eyes as the tether of the world.33
  • Federalization: Gian's seizure of control over Burunt's banking, giving him the power to recall debts and inspect any financial records.21
  • Forging: The Draumer ability to shape gray mist into a solid object, such as a dagger or a set of lockpicks.1
  • Founder's ring: A silvery ring, etched with a branch and engraved with a family name, held by the oldest bloodlines; it is a Draumer creation. See Founder's rings.4
  • Founding House: One of the oldest noble lineages of Burunt. See Founding Houses.49
  • Goldguard bank: The bank that held House Khar's accounts for generations, identified by a plumed-helmet seal in yellow wax.6
  • Gutter rat: An insult for a street child, which Kyndel applies to his own past.510
  • Halls: A Prikizan oath, found in forms such as Halls below and Hallowed Halls.15
  • Haptic signature: The faint pulse, unique to its maker, that a Draumer creation gives off when touched.414
  • Hexagonal plate: A rune-covered metal plate on display at the Stilton estate that Heraldur wants stolen. See hexagonal plate.9
  • Imperial silvers: Coins of the Empire, in which Lefty pays Kyndel.1
  • Inspection day: The Viceroy's monthly review of the work of Signarium Hall.8
  • Iron Spears: An imperial brigade sent to Burunt to hunt the Alshien. See Iron Spears.2
  • Khar’andor: House Khar's original surname, engraved inside its Founder's ring.429
  • Kulebyaka: A Prikizan rye pastry with a filling of sturgeon, rice and eggs.13
  • Lord of the Warrens: The title adopted by the crime boss who united most of the Warrens gangs.34
  • Lordling: A mocking nickname Lefty uses for Kyndel.1
  • Magno-signaric rail: Jelert's proposed rail line between Burunt and the mainland, powered by refined cyrusite.8
  • Major Meddle: The troop ship soldiers' nickname for Jelert.2
  • Master Engineer: The title of the head of Signarium Hall.812
  • Mintika Point: Burunt's most aristocratic district. See Mintika Point.1
  • Obelisk: A device in the Draumer camps that drains prisoners' power, originally built to produce cyrusite. See the Obelisk.433
  • Overdraw: The act of pulling too much power through the tether, which causes pain at the base of the skull and can be fatal. See overdraw.414
  • Petrovskaya Academy: The imperial academy where Jelert and Blazej trained.8
  • Presentation day: An occasion on which Signarium Hall's engineers show their work to the Viceroy.15
  • Prikizan: A person or thing belonging to the Prikaz Empire. See Prikizans.13
  • Railcaster: A signaric weapon that fires metal projectiles using Jelert's rail runes.25
  • Redarm: One of the armored hunters in the Viceroy's service who track down Draumer. See Redarms.4
  • Requing musket: An uncommon black powder firearm made in the Requing Federation.10
  • Rune charge: A signaric explosive.45
  • Runeforge capacitor: A power device designed by Jelert that the Empire converted into an explosive and used at Yeshall.1213
  • Runic array: A series of engraved runes that channels energy from cyrusite.2
  • Sapper: An insult, which Khamron directs at Kyndel.5
  • Signaric spear: The cyrusite-powered short spear that serves as the Iron Spears' signature weapon.2
  • Signaric vambrace: A device made by Heraldur to shield Draumer from the Obelisk.1943
  • Signarium: The imperial discipline of rune-based technology, whose devices are described as signaric. See signarium.12
  • Social season: The series of noble parties that starts in spring. See social season.1
  • Stockwright's Council: A Burunt trade organization that helps merchants find buyers.3
  • Tether: The internal channel through which a Draumer draws power. See tether.1
  • Thorns: A common Burition curse, also used as thorning.1
  • Torc: A rune-etched neck ring; Gian uses torcs to bind the Warriors.2445
  • Valenska: The Earth Mother of the Prikizan religion, whose blood is said to be cyrusite. See Valenska.13
  • Viceroy: The official who governs Burunt for the Prikaz Empire.1
  • Warrens: Burunt's fire-gutted slum district. See the Warrens.1
  • Warrens Baron: A gang lord of the Warrens. See Warrens Barons.5
  • Warriors: Gian's towering armored constructs, each containing a mutilated Draumer.4447
  • The Yard: The recreation area and fighting ring of the Draumer prison.43
  • Yellow bands: Armbands identifying Gian's loyalists. See yellow bands.4445
  • Yeshall: An imperial territory in the north where a rebellion was crushed using Jelert's runeforge capacitor. See Yeshall.13
